title.en: Volume 340 Biographies 99: Lu Dafang and elder brother: Dazhong, younger brother: Dajun, Da Lin, Liu Zhi, Su Song
title.raw: 卷三百四十 列傳第九十九 呂大防兄:大忠 弟:大鈞 大臨 劉摯 蘇頌 Volume 340 Biographies 99: Lu Dafang and elder brother: Dazhong, younger brother: Dajun, Da Lin, Liu Zhi, Su Song

sentences.zh: 呂大防

translations.literal: Lü Dafang
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dafang

sentences.zh: 呂大防，字微仲，其先汲郡人。

translations.literal: Lü Dafang, courtesy name Weizhong, his ancestors were men of Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dafang, whose courtesy name was Weizhong, came from a family originally of Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖通，太常博士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tong was an Erudite of the Imperial Diener.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tong served as Erudite of the Imperial Diener.

sentences.zh: 父賁，比部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Ben was a Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ben held the post of Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 通葬京兆藍田，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Tong was buried in Lantian in Jingzhao, and the family then settled there.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong died he was buried at Lantian in Jingzhao, and the family made their home there.

sentences.zh: 大防進士及第，調馮翊主簿、永壽令。

translations.literal: Dafang passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Main Clerk of Fengyi and Magistrate of Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang passed the jinshi examinations and was posted as main clerk of Fengyi and magistrate of Yongshou.

sentences.zh: 縣無井，遠汲於澗，大防行近境，得二泉，欲導而入縣，地勢高下，眾疑無成理。

translations.literal: The county had no wells and drew water far off from ravines; Dafang traveled the nearby territory, found two springs, and wished to channel them into the county seat, but the ground rose and fell and the multitude doubted that success was possible.
translations.idiomatic: The county had no wells and had to draw water from distant ravines. When Dafang toured the nearby countryside he found two springs and planned to channel them into the seat, but the terrain was uneven and people doubted the project could work.

sentences.zh: 大防用《考工》水地置泉之法以準之，不旬日，果疏為渠，民賴之，號曰「呂公泉」。

translations.literal: Dafang applied the methods of the Kaogongji for placing springs according to terrain and water to gauge it; within less than ten days a channel was indeed opened, the people relied on it, and it was called "Lord Lü's Spring."
translations.idiomatic: Dafang surveyed the site by the Kaogongji's methods for siting springs from terrain and water, and within ten days a channel was cut as planned. The people depended on it and called it "Lord Lü's Spring."

sentences.zh: 遷著作佐郎、知青城縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Editor in the Palace Library and was made magistrate of Qingcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant editor in the Palace Library and appointed magistrate of Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 故時，圭田粟入以大斗，而出以公斗，獲利三倍，民雖病不敢訴。

translations.literal: Formerly, for ceremonial-field grain they took in with the large measure and paid out with the standard measure, gaining profit threefold; though the people suffered, they did not dare complain.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old practice, grain from ceremonial fields was collected with the large bushel but disbursed with the standard bushel, tripling the profit. The people suffered but dared not protest.

sentences.zh: 大防始均出納以平其直，事轉聞，詔立法禁，命一路悉輸租於官概給之。

translations.literal: Dafang first equalized intake and outflow to level the price; the matter was reported upward, an edict established a legal prohibition, and the entire circuit was ordered to deliver rent entirely to the government, which would issue it by standard measure.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang first balanced collections and disbursements to even out the price. When word reached the court, an edict outlawed the practice and required the whole circuit to pay rent to the government, which would then issue grain by the standard measure.

sentences.zh: 青城外控汶川，與敵相接。

translations.literal: Outside Qingcheng one controlled Wenchuan and bordered the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Qingcheng lay Wenchuan, on the frontier where the enemy could be met.

sentences.zh: 大防據要置邏，密為之防，禁山之樵採，以嚴障蔽。

translations.literal: Dafang seized key points and set up courier stations, secretly preparing defenses, forbidding woodcutting in the mountains to tighten the screen.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang held strategic points and established courier posts, quietly strengthening defenses and banning logging in the mountains to keep the border screen intact.

sentences.zh: 韓絳鎮蜀，稱其有王佐才。

translations.literal: When Han Jiang governed Shu, he declared that Dafang had the talent of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang was military commissioner of Shu, he praised Dafang as having the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 入權鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as acting Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital to serve as acting commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，改太常博士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Dafang was changed to Erudite of the Imperial Diener.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Dafang was reassigned as erudite of the Imperial Diener.

sentences.zh: 御史闕，內出大防與范純仁姓名，命為監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: When the censorate had a vacancy, the court issued the names of Dafang and Fan Chunren from within and appointed them acting supervising censors.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor's post fell vacant, the palace released the names of Dafang and Fan Chunren and appointed them supervising censors with acting status.

sentences.zh: 首言：「紀綱賞罰，未厭四方之望者有五：進用大臣而權不歸上；

translations.literal: In his first memorial he said: "In discipline, rewards, and punishments, there are five matters that have not yet satisfied the hopes of the four quarters: promoting great ministers while authority does not return to the sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: In his opening memorial he said: "In discipline and in rewards and punishments, five things still fall short of what the realm expects: great ministers are advanced while authority does not return to the throne;

sentences.zh: 大臣疲老而不得時退；

translations.literal: great ministers, worn and old, cannot retire in due season;
translations.idiomatic: great ministers, worn out with age, cannot step down when they should;

sentences.zh: 外國驕蹇而不擇將帥；

translations.literal: foreign states are arrogant and obstinate while generals are not chosen with care;
translations.idiomatic: foreign powers grow arrogant while commanders are not chosen with care;

sentences.zh: 議論之臣裨益闕失，而大臣沮之；

translations.literal: discussing ministers who remedy omissions and errors are obstructed by great ministers;
translations.idiomatic: censors who would remedy faults are blocked by the great ministers;

sentences.zh: 疆場左右之臣，有敗事而被賞、舉職而獲罪者。

translations.literal: and ministers at the borders, among whom some who failed in duty are rewarded and some who fulfilled duty are punished."
translations.idiomatic: and on the frontiers there are men who fail yet are rewarded and men who do their duty yet are punished."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「富弼病足請解機務，章十餘上而不納；

translations.literal: " He also said: "Fu Bi, ill in the feet, asked to be released from state affairs; he submitted more than ten memorials without acceptance;
translations.idiomatic: " He went on: "Fu Bi, afflicted in the feet, asked to leave state affairs; he sent more than ten memorials without success;

sentences.zh: 張昪年幾八十，聰明已耗，哀乞骸骨而不從；

translations.literal: Zhang Bian is nearly eighty, his keenness already spent, and he pitifully begs to retire his bones without consent;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bian is nearly eighty and his faculties are spent, yet his plea to retire is refused;

sentences.zh: 吳奎有三年之喪，以其子召之者再，遣使召之者又再；

translations.literal: Wu Kui is in the three-year mourning; he was summoned through his son twice, and envoys were sent to summon him twice again;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kui is in mourning for his father and has been summoned twice through his son and twice again by imperial envoys;

sentences.zh: 程戡辭老不能守邊，恐死塞上，免以屍柩還家為請，亦不許。

translations.literal: Cheng Kan declines on account of age, unable to guard the border, fearing death on the frontier, and asks only to be spared having his coffin borne home—this too is not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Kan begs off on account of age, saying he cannot hold the border and fears dying on campaign, asking only the grace of not having to bring his coffin home from the frontier—yet this too is denied.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲盡君臣之分，使病者得休，喪者得終，老者得盡其餘年，則進退盡禮，亦何必過為虛飾，使四人之誠，不得自達邪？」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to fulfill the measure between ruler and minister, let the sick rest, the bereaved finish mourning, and the aged spend their remaining years, then advance and withdrawal would observe full ritual—why must there be excessive empty show, so that the sincerity of these four men cannot reach you?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to honor the bond between ruler and minister—so the sick may rest, the bereaved may mourn, and the aged may live out their years—then let advance and withdrawal follow proper ritual. Why insist on empty ceremony that keeps these four men's sincerity from reaching you?"

sentences.zh: 是歲，京師大水，大防曰：「雨水之患，至入宮城廬舍，殺人害物，此陰陽之沴也。

translations.literal: That year the capital suffered great flooding. Dafang said: "The calamity of rain and water, reaching into the palace city and dwellings, killing people and harming things—this is a baleful sign of yin and yang."
translations.idiomatic: That year the capital was inundated. Dafang said: "When rain and flood enter the palace city and common houses, killing people and destroying property, this is a disorder of yin and yang."

sentences.zh: 」即陳八事，曰：主威不立、臣權太盛、邪議干正、私恩害公、遼夏連謀、盜賊恣行、群情失職、刑罰失平。

translations.literal: " He then set forth eight matters, saying: the sovereign's authority is not established; ministerial power is too great; perverse discourse interferes with what is right; private favor harms the public good; Liao and Xia conspire together; bandits run rampant; popular sentiment loses its proper roles; punishments lose their balance.
translations.idiomatic: " He then listed eight ills: the throne's authority is not firm; ministers are too powerful; wicked counsel overrides right policy; private favor injures the public good; Liao and Xia plot together; bandits roam unchecked; public morale is out of joint; and punishments are uneven.

sentences.zh: 會執政議濮王稱考，大防上言：「先帝起陛下為皇子，館於宮中，憑几之命，緒言在耳，皇天后土，實知所託。

translations.literal: When the chief ministers discussed calling the Prince of Pu "Imperial Father," Dafang submitted a memorial: "The late emperor raised Your Majesty as his son and lodged you in the palace; the charge given at the couch, the trailing words still in the ear—Heaven and Earth truly know to whom the trust was committed.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers debated granting the Prince of Pu the title Imperial Father, Dafang memorialized: "The late emperor raised Your Majesty as crown prince and housed you in the palace. The charge spoken at his couch still rings in our ears; Heaven and Earth know whom he truly entrusted."

sentences.zh: 設使先帝萬壽，陛下猶為皇子，則安懿之稱伯，於理不疑。

translations.literal: Suppose the late emperor had lived ten thousand years and Your Majesty were still the crown prince—then to call An Yi "uncle" would be in reason beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Had the late emperor lived on and Your Majesty remained crown prince, calling Prince An Yi "uncle" would have been entirely proper.

sentences.zh: 豈可生以為子，沒而背之哉？

translations.literal: How can one in life be made a son and in death be turned against?
translations.idiomatic: How can he be made a son in life and repudiated in death?

sentences.zh: 夫人君臨御之始，宜有至公大義厭服天下，以結其心。

translations.literal: When a ruler first takes the throne, there should be utmost public righteousness to satisfy the realm and bind hearts.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of a reign the ruler should win the realm with utmost fairness and public duty, binding hearts to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今大臣首欲加王以非正之號，使陛下顧私恩而違公義，非所以結天下之心也。

translations.literal: Now the great ministers first wish to give the prince an irregular title, causing Your Majesty to look to private affection and violate public righteousness—this is not the way to bind the hearts of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Now the chief ministers would first give the prince an improper title, leading Your Majesty to favor private feeling over public duty. That is no way to win the realm's hearts.

sentences.zh: 」章累十數上，出知休寧縣。

translations.literal: " He submitted memorials repeatedly, more than ten times, and was sent out as magistrate of Xiuning County.
translations.idiomatic: " After more than ten such memorials he was transferred out to serve as magistrate of Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，通判淄州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Dafang was made vice-prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong came to the throne, Dafang was appointed vice-prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，知泗州，為河北轉運副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining he was made prefect of Sizhou and became Vice Transport Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xining he became prefect of Sizhou and vice transport commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 召直舍人院。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to duty in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 韓絳宣撫陝西，命為判官，又兼河東宣撫判官，除知制誥。

translations.literal: When Han Jiang was pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, Dafang was appointed his administrative aide, also concurrently pacification administrative aide of Hedong, and was made Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang was pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, Dafang served as his aide and also as aide to the Hedong pacification commissioner, and was appointed drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 四年，知廷州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 大防、昉欲城河外荒堆砦，眾謂不可守，大防留戍兵修堡障，有不從者斬以徇。

translations.literal: Dafang and Fang wished to fortify desolate beacon forts beyond the river; the multitude said they could not be held. Dafang left garrison troops to repair ramparts and barriers, and those who would not obey were beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang and Fang wanted to wall desolate beacon forts beyond the river, though many said they could not be held. Dafang left garrison troops to build fortifications and executed any who refused, as an example.

sentences.zh: 會環慶兵亂，絳坐黜，大防亦落知制誥，以太常博士知臨江軍。

translations.literal: When troops in Huan and Qing mutinied, Han Jiang was demoted on that account; Dafang also lost his post as drafter of edicts and was made Erudite of the Imperial Diener while governing Linjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huanqing garrison mutinied, Han Jiang was dismissed and Dafang was stripped of his post as drafter of edicts, becoming erudite of the Imperial Diener while governing Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 數月，徙知華州。

translations.literal: After several months he was transferred to be prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was transferred to Huazhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 華嶽摧，自山屬渭河，被害者眾。

translations.literal: Mount Hua collapsed, from the mountain down to the Wei River; those harmed were many.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Hua collapsed, debris running from the mountain down to the Wei River, and many were killed or injured.

sentences.zh: 大防奏疏，援經質史，以驗時事。

translations.literal: Dafang submitted a memorial, citing the classics and testing history to verify present affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang memorialized the throne, citing the classics and weighing history against present events.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「『畏天之威，於時保之。

translations.literal: The gist said: "'Revere Heaven's majesty, and in season preserve it.'
translations.idiomatic: In summary he wrote: "'Revere Heaven's majesty and in due season preserve your rule'—

sentences.zh: 』先王所以興也；

translations.literal: '—this is how former kings rose;
translations.idiomatic: that is how the ancient kings rose;

sentences.zh: 『我生不有命在天』，後王所以壞也。

translations.literal: 'My life is not—there is mandate in Heaven'—this is how later kings were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: 'My life rests not with myself but with Heaven's mandate'—that is how later kings fell.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：『惟先格王，正厥事。

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'Only by first apprehending the king will you rectify his affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: 'Only by first understanding the king can his affairs be set right.'

sentences.zh: 』願仰承天威，俯酌時變，為社稷至計。

translations.literal: ' I pray that Your Majesty look up to receive Heaven's majesty, look down to weigh the changes of the time, and take the utmost plan for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: ' I pray Your Majesty will look up to Heaven's majesty and look down to the changes of the age, and take the course that best secures the realm."

sentences.zh: 」除龍圖閣待制、知秦州。

translations.literal: " He was made Hanlin Academician-on-Waiting at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed academician-on-waiting at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，徙永興。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng he was transferred to Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng he was transferred to Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 神宗以彗星求言，大防陳三說九宜：曰治本、曰緩末、曰納言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong, on account of a comet, sought counsel, Dafang set forth three doctrines and nine measures fit to adopt: treating the root, easing the branch, and receiving words.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet prompted Emperor Shenzong to seek counsel, Dafang offered three doctrines and nine measures: strengthen the root, ease the branches, and welcome frank speech.

sentences.zh: 養民、教士、重穀，治本之宜三也；

translations.literal: Nourishing the people, instructing scholars, and valuing grain—these three are fit for treating the root;
translations.idiomatic: Nourish the people, educate scholars, and value grain—these three strengthen the root;

sentences.zh: 治邊、治兵，緩末之宜二也；

translations.literal: governing the border and governing the army—these two are fit for easing the branch;
translations.idiomatic: govern the frontier and govern the army—these two ease the branches;

sentences.zh: 廣受言之路，寬侵官之罰，恕誹謗之罪，容異同之論，此納言之宜四也。

translations.literal: broadening the road by which words are received, easing punishments for encroaching on office, pardoning offenses of slander, and tolerating differing opinions—these four are fit for receiving words.
translations.idiomatic: widen the channels for counsel, lighten penalties for overstepping office, pardon charges of slander, and tolerate dissent—these four welcome frank speech.

sentences.zh: 累數千言。

translations.literal: In all it ran to several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran to several thousand words.

sentences.zh: 時用兵西夏，調度百出，有不便者輒上聞，務在寬民。

translations.literal: At the time troops were used against Western Xia and requisitions issued in profusion; whenever something was inconvenient he reported upward, striving to ease the people.
translations.idiomatic: While the court campaigned against Western Xia, levies multiplied. Whenever a measure burdened the people he reported it at once, always seeking to lighten their load.

sentences.zh: 及兵罷，民力比他路為饒，供億軍須亦無乏絕。

translations.literal: When the armies ceased, the people's strength in his circuit was more ample than in other circuits, and supplies for the army were also without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: When the war ended, his circuit's people were better off than elsewhere, yet military supplies never ran short.

sentences.zh: 進直學士。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 居數年，知成都府。

translations.literal: After several years he was made prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was appointed prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，召為翰林學士、權開封府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, Dafang was summoned as Hanlin Academician and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Dafang was recalled as Hanlin academician and acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 有僧誑民取財，因訟至廷下。

translations.literal: There was a monk who deceived the people to take wealth; through litigation the case came before the court.
translations.idiomatic: A monk who swindled the people was brought to court in a lawsuit.

sentences.zh: 驗治得情，命抱具獄，即其所杖之，他挾奸者皆遁去。

translations.literal: Investigation established the facts; he ordered the man to carry the instruments of punishment to the place of the crime and there be beaten with the staff; other fraudsters all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Once the facts were proved, Dafang had the man carry the punishment gear to the scene of his crime and beaten there on the spot. Other swindlers fled.

sentences.zh: 館伴契丹使，其使黠，語頗及朝廷，大防密擿其隱事，詰之曰：「北朝試進士《至心獨運賦》，不知此題於書何出？

translations.literal: As host to the Khitan envoy, the envoy was crafty and his words often touched on the court. Dafang secretly brought out a private matter of his and questioned him: "In the Northern Court's jinshi examination there was the rhapsody 'Sincerity Alone Moves the Heart'—do you know from which book this topic comes?"
translations.idiomatic: While hosting a Khitan envoy, a clever man who often alluded to court affairs, Dafang quietly uncovered a compromising detail and asked him: "Your court's recent jinshi examination used the topic 'With Utmost Sincerity the Heart Moves Alone'—from which classic does that phrase come?"

sentences.zh: 」使錯遌不能對，自是不敢復出嫚詞。

translations.literal: " The envoy was flustered and could not answer; from then on he did not dare utter insolent words again.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy was abashed and could not reply, and never again dared speak insolently.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 夏使來，詔訪以待遇之計，且曰：「向者所得邊地，雖建立城堡，終慮孤絕難保。

translations.literal: When a Xia envoy came, an edict sought his plan for receiving them, saying: "The border lands taken before, though we have built castles and forts, in the end we fear they are isolated and hard to hold.
translations.idiomatic: When a Western Xia envoy arrived, the emperor asked his advice on how to treat them, saying: "The frontier lands we recently gained have fortresses, yet we fear they are too isolated to hold.

sentences.zh: 棄之則弱國，守之又有後悔，為當奈何？

translations.literal: To abandon them weakens the state; to hold them brings later regret—what ought to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: To abandon them weakens the state, yet to hold them may bring regret—what should we do?"

sentences.zh: 」大防言：「夏本無能為，然屢遣使而不布誠款者，蓋料我急於議和耳。

translations.literal: " Dafang said: "Xia by nature can do nothing, yet they repeatedly send envoys without showing sincere good faith—probably because they reckon we are eager to discuss peace.
translations.idiomatic: " Dafang replied: "The Xia are not truly formidable, yet they send envoys again and again without sincere overtures because they assume we are eager for peace.

sentences.zh: 今使者到闕，宜令押伴臣僚，扣其不賀登極，以觀厥意，足以測情偽矣。

translations.literal: Now that the envoy has reached the capital, the escorting officials should be ordered to press him on his failure to congratulate Your Majesty's accession, to observe his intent—this is enough to gauge truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the envoy is at court, let the escorting officials press him on why he did not congratulate Your Majesty's accession. His response will reveal his true intentions.

sentences.zh: 新收疆土，議者多言可棄，此慮之不熟也。

translations.literal: As for the newly taken territory, many in discussion say it may be abandoned—this is thinking that is not mature.
translations.idiomatic: As for the newly taken lands, many advisers say we should abandon them—but that judgment is immature.

sentences.zh: 至於守御之策，惟擇將帥為先。

translations.literal: As for the strategy of defense, choosing generals comes first.
translations.idiomatic: For defense, the first priority is choosing the right commanders.

sentences.zh: 太祖用姚內斌、董遵誨守環、慶，西人不敢入侵。

translations.literal: Taizu used Yao Neibin and Dong Zunhui to guard Huan and Qing, and the western peoples did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu posted Yao Neibin and Dong Zunhui at Huan and Qing, and the western peoples dared not invade.

sentences.zh: 昔以二州之力，禦敵而有餘；

translations.literal: Formerly with the strength of two prefectures they repelled the enemy and had surplus;
translations.idiomatic: Once two prefectures sufficed to repel the enemy with strength to spare;

sentences.zh: 今以九州之大，奉邊而不足。

translations.literal: now with the vastness of the Nine Provinces, supplying the border is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: now with the resources of the whole realm, the frontier still seems underfed.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，在於得人而已。

translations.literal: From this it is said: it lies in obtaining the right men, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The difference, in short, is whether we have the right men.

sentences.zh: 」元祐元年，拜尚書右丞，進中書侍郎，封汲郡公。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Yuanyou he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first year of Yuanyou he became right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, then vice director of the Secretariat, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 西方息兵，青唐羌以為中國怯，使大將鬼章青宜結犯邊。

translations.literal: When fighting ceased in the west, the Qingtang Qiang thought China timid and sent the great general Guizhang Qingyijie to invade the border.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting in the west subsided, the Qingtang Qiang judged China timid and sent the general Guizhang Qingyijie to raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 大防命洮州諸將乘間致討，生擒之。

translations.literal: Dafang ordered the generals of Taozhou to seize an opening and strike; they captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang ordered the generals of Taozhou to strike when opportunity allowed and they took him alive.

sentences.zh: 三年，呂公著告老，宣仁后欲留之京師。

translations.literal: In the third year Lü Gongzhu reported old age; Empress Dowager Xuanren wished to keep him in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Lü Gongzhu sought to retire, and Empress Dowager Xuanren wished to keep him in the capital.

sentences.zh: 手札密訪至於四五，超拜大防尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎，提舉修《神宗實錄》。

translations.literal: By handwritten notes she secretly consulted him four or five times and abruptly promoted Dafang to Left Grand Master of the Palace and Vice Director of the Chancellery, with charge over compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: She consulted him privately by letter four or five times, then promoted Dafang to left grand master of the palace and vice director of the Chancellery, putting him in charge of compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong.

sentences.zh: 大防見哲宗年益壯，日以進學為急，請敕講讀官取仁宗邇英御書解釋上之，置於座右。

translations.literal: Dafang saw that Zhezong grew daily stronger in years and made advancing in learning ever more urgent; he asked that the lecture officials be ordered to take Emperor Renzong's Yiying imperial writings with explanations and present them, placing them at the ruler's right hand.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhezong grow older, Dafang pressed daily for his education and asked that lecture officials submit Emperor Renzong's annotated Yiying lectures for placement at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 又摭乾興以來四十一事足以為勸戒者，分上下篇，標曰《仁祖聖學》，使人主有欣慕不足之意。

translations.literal: He also gathered forty-one matters since Qianxing sufficient to serve as admonition, divided into upper and lower fascicles, titled The Sagely Learning of Emperor Ren, so that the ruler would feel delight and admiration without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled forty-one instructive episodes since Qianxing into upper and lower volumes titled The Sagely Learning of Emperor Ren, meant to inspire the ruler with lasting admiration.

sentences.zh: 哲宗御邇英閣，召宰執、講讀官讀《寶訓》，至「漢武帝籍南山提封為上林苑，仁宗曰：『山澤之利當與眾共之，何用此也。

translations.literal: Zhezong attended at the Yiying Pavilion, summoning the chief ministers and lecture officials to read the Precious Instructions, coming to: "Emperor Wu of Han registered the southern hills and raised their bounds to make the Shanglin Park." Emperor Renzong said: "The profit of mountains and marshes should be shared with the multitude—what use is this?"
translations.idiomatic: At the Yiying Pavilion Zhezong summoned the chief ministers and lecture officials to read the Precious Instructions. They came to the passage where Emperor Wu of Han seized the southern hills for the Shanglin Park and Emperor Renzong said: "The bounty of hills and marshes should be shared with the people—what need is there for this?"

sentences.zh: 』丁度曰：『臣事陛下二十年，每奉德音，未始不及於憂勤，此蓋祖宗家法爾。

translations.literal: ' Ding Du said: 'In serving Your Majesty twenty years, whenever I received your virtuous words, they never failed to touch on anxious diligence—this is surely the house law of our ancestors.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' Ding Du replied: "In twenty years serving Your Majesty, every gracious word I have heard has spoken of anxious diligence for the realm—such is our ancestors' household rule."'

sentences.zh: 』」大防因推廣祖宗家法以進，曰：「自三代以後，唯本朝百二十年中外無事，蓋由祖宗所立家法最善，臣請舉其略。

translations.literal: " Dafang thereupon extended the ancestors' house law in a memorial, saying: "Since the Three Dynasties, only our dynasty for one hundred twenty years has been without trouble within and without—this is because the house law established by the ancestors is the best. Your servant asks to set forth its outline.
translations.idiomatic: " Dafang then expanded on the ancestral household rules, saying: "Since antiquity only our dynasty has enjoyed roughly 120 years largely free of turmoil within and without, because the rules our ancestors established are the finest. I beg leave to summarize them.

sentences.zh: 自古人主事母后，朝見有時，如漢武帝五日一朝長樂宮；

translations.literal: From antiquity rulers served their empress mothers with audiences at set times, as Emperor Wu of Han attended the Everlasting Joy Palace once every five days;
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers visited their empress mothers on a fixed schedule—Emperor Wu of Han, for example, attended the Everlasting Joy Palace once every five days;

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來事母后，皆朝夕見，此事親之法也。

translations.literal: since our ancestors, in serving empress mothers, all have seen them morning and evening—this is the method of serving kin.
translations.idiomatic: but our house has always visited empress mothers morning and evening. That is how we honor our kin.

sentences.zh: 前代大長公主用臣妾之禮；

translations.literal: Former ages treated great elder imperial princesses with the rites due to minister and concubine;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties treated elder imperial princesses with the ceremony owed to ministers and concubines;

sentences.zh: 本朝必先致恭，仁宗以姪事姑之禮見獻穆大長公主，此事長之法也。

translations.literal: our dynasty first shows reverence; Emperor Renzong met the Great Elder Princess Xianmu with the rites of a nephew toward an aunt—this is the method of serving elders.
translations.idiomatic: our house always shows respect first—Emperor Renzong received the Great Elder Princess Xianmu with a nephew's courtesy toward his aunt. That is how we honor our elders.

sentences.zh: 前代宮闈多不肅，宮人或與廷臣相見，唐入閣圖有昭容位；

translations.literal: former ages' inner palaces were often not strict; palace women might meet court ministers—the Tang picture of entering the hall has a place for Zhaorong;
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times the inner palace was often lax and palace women might meet court officials—the Tang painting of entering the hall even marks a place for palace ladies;

sentences.zh: 本朝宮禁嚴密，內外整肅，此治內之法也。

translations.literal: our dynasty's palace precincts are strict, inner and outer in good order—this is the method of governing within.
translations.idiomatic: our palace precincts are strict and discipline is maintained within and without. That is how we govern the inner court.

sentences.zh: 前代外戚多預政事，常致敗亂；

translations.literal: former ages' maternal kin often took part in government affairs and frequently brought ruin and disorder;
translations.idiomatic: In former times consort kin often meddled in politics and brought ruin;

sentences.zh: 本朝母后之族皆不預，此待外戚之法也。

translations.literal: in our dynasty the families of empress mothers all do not participate—this is the method of treating maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: in our house the empress mother's kin never hold office. That is how we treat consort relatives.

sentences.zh: 前代宮室多尚華侈；

translations.literal: former ages' palaces mostly prized splendor and extravagance;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier palaces prized lavish ornament;

sentences.zh: 本朝宮殿止用赤白，此尚儉之法也。

translations.literal: our dynasty's palaces use only red and white—this is the method of valuing frugality.
translations.idiomatic: our palaces use only red and white. That is how we value frugality.

sentences.zh: 前代人君雖在宮禁，出輿入輦；

translations.literal: former ages' rulers, though within the palace precincts, went out by carriage and entered by palanquin;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier rulers, even within the palace, rode out in carriages and palanquins;

sentences.zh: 祖宗皆步自內庭，出御後殿，豈乏人力哉？

translations.literal: our ancestors all walked from the inner court when going out to attend the rear hall—was manpower lacking?
translations.idiomatic: our ancestors walked from the inner court to the rear hall—was it for lack of attendants?

sentences.zh: 亦欲涉歷廣庭，稍冒寒暑，此勤身之法也。

translations.literal: They also wished to traverse the broad courtyard and endure a little cold and heat—this is the method of diligent self-discipline.
translations.idiomatic: No—they wished to cross the broad courtyards and bear a little heat and cold. That is how they kept their bodies disciplined.

sentences.zh: 前代人主，在禁中冠服苟簡；

translations.literal: Former ages' rulers in the inner precincts wore cap and robes carelessly and simply;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier rulers dressed casually in the palace precincts;

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，燕居必以禮，竊聞陛下昨郊禮畢，具禮謝太皇太后，此尚禮之法也。

translations.literal: Since our ancestors, at ease one must observe rites; I have heard that yesterday when Your Majesty finished the suburban sacrifice, you performed full rites to thank the Grand Empress Dowager—this is the method of honoring ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Since our ancestors, even in private life we observe proper ceremony. I have heard that after yesterday's suburban sacrifice Your Majesty performed full rites to thank the Grand Empress Dowager. That is how we honor ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 前代多深於用刑，大者誅戮，小者遠竄；

translations.literal: Former ages mostly applied punishments severely; the great were executed, the small were banished far away;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties punished harshly—the greatest offenders were executed and lesser ones were banished far away;

sentences.zh: 惟本朝用法最輕，臣下有罪，止於罷黜，此寬仁之法也。

translations.literal: Only our dynasty applies the law most lightly; when subjects have guilt, it stops at dismissal—this is the method of generous kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Our house alone applies the law most leniently. When officials err, dismissal is the limit. That is how we practice generous clemency.

sentences.zh: 至於虛己納諫，不好畋獵，不尚玩好，不用玉器，不貴異味，此皆祖宗家法，所以致太平者。

translations.literal: As for emptying oneself to accept remonstrance, not liking hunting, not prizing playthings, not using jade vessels, not valuing exotic flavors—all these are ancestral family laws by which great peace was attained.
translations.idiomatic: Emptying oneself to accept remonstrance, shunning the hunt, spurning trifles, eschewing jade ware, and disdaining exotic delicacies—all these ancestral family laws are what brought about great peace.

sentences.zh: 陛下不須遠法前代，但盡行家法，足以為天下。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need not look far to the laws of former ages; simply fully practice the family laws, and that suffices to govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need not look to former ages for models. Simply follow the family laws fully, and that is enough to govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗甚然之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong greatly approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong strongly approved.

sentences.zh: 大防樸厚惷直，不植黨朋，與范純仁並位，同心戮力，以相王室。

translations.literal: Dafang was plain, honest, sincere and upright; he did not set up factional cliques; he shared rank with Fan Chunren and with one heart exerted their strength to assist the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang was plainspoken, honest, and upright, and kept no faction of his own. Sharing office with Fan Chunren, the two worked in concert to serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 立朝挺挺，進退百官，不可干以私，不市恩嫁怨以邀聲譽，凡八年，始終如一。

translations.literal: In court he stood erect and stern; in promoting and demoting the hundred officials no one could influence him with private interest; he did not trade favors or offload resentment to seek reputation—for eight years he was the same from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: In court he held himself erect. No one could sway his decisions on appointing or removing officials through private appeals, nor did he trade favors or shift blame to win renown. For eight years he was unwavering.

sentences.zh: 懇乞避位，宣仁后曰：「上方富於春秋，公未可即去，少須歲月，吾亦就東朝矣。

translations.literal: He earnestly begged to withdraw from office; Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "The emperor above is still in the prime of youth. You, sir, cannot leave at once. Wait a few months—I too shall retire to the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly asked to step down. Empress Dowager Xuanren said, "The emperor is still young. You, sir, cannot leave yet. Wait a few months—I too shall retire to the Eastern Palace."

sentences.zh: 」未果而后崩。

translations.literal: Before this was accomplished, the empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: Before that could happen, the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 為山陵使，覆命以觀文殿大學士、左光祿大夫知潁昌府。

translations.literal: He served as commissioner for the imperial tomb; upon reporting back he was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and prefect of Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: As commissioner for the imperial tomb, he reported back and was appointed grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, left grand master of splendid happiness, and prefect of Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 尋改永興軍，使便其鄉社。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Yongxing Circuit so he might be near his native district and altars.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Yongxing Circuit to be nearer his home.

sentences.zh: 入辭，哲宗勞慰甚渥，曰：「卿暫歸故鄉，行即召矣。

translations.literal: On entering to take leave, Emperor Zhezong comforted and reassured him very generously, saying: "You, sir, will return home for a time—you will soon be summoned again."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to take leave, Emperor Zhezong comforted him warmly and said, "Return home for a time—you will soon be summoned again."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，左正言上官均論其隳壞役法，右正言張商英、御史周秩、劉拯相繼攻之，奪學士，知隨州，貶秘書監，分司南京，居郢州。

translations.literal: Before long, Left Rectifier Shangguan Jun criticized him for ruining the corvée law; Right Rectifier Zhang Shangying and censors Zhou Zhi and Liu Zheng attacked him in succession; his academician title was taken; he was made prefect of Suizhou; demoted to supervisor of the Secretariat; assigned to the Southern Capital branch; and resided at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Left Rectifier Shangguan Jun accused him of undermining the corvée law. Right Rectifier Zhang Shangying and Censors Zhou Zhi and Liu Zheng attacked him in turn. He lost his academician title, was posted as prefect of Suizhou, demoted to supervisor of the Secretariat with duties at the Southern Capital branch, and lived at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者又以修《神宗實錄》直書其事為誣詆，徙安州。

translations.literal: The critics further charged that in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong he had written events directly and thus slandered; he was transferred to Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics also charged that in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong he had written events plainly, which they called slander, and he was moved to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 兄大忠自渭入對，哲宗詢大防安否，且曰：「執政欲遷諸嶺南，朕獨令處安陸，為朕寄聲問之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Dazhong came from Wei to audience; Emperor Zhezong inquired whether Dafang was well and also said: "The chief ministers wished to banish them all south of the mountains; I alone had him placed at Anlu. Convey my greetings to him for me."
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Dazhong came from Weizhou for audience. Emperor Zhezong asked after Dafang's health and said, "The chief ministers wanted to banish them all south of the mountains. I alone had him placed at Anlu. Convey my greetings to him for me."

sentences.zh: 大防樸直，為人所賣，三二年可復相見也。

translations.literal: Dafang is plain and upright—he has been betrayed by others; in two or three years you can meet again.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang is straightforward and has been sold out by others. In two or three years you may see each other again.

sentences.zh: 」大忠泄其語於章惇，惇懼，繩之愈力。

translations.literal: Dazhong leaked these words to Zhang Dun; Dun was afraid and tightened the bonds on him all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong repeated this to Zhang Dun. Dun, alarmed, pressed the case against Dafang even harder.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，遂貶舒州團練副使，安置循州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng he was demoted to assistant commissioner of militia training for Shuzhou and ordered to reside at Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaosheng he was demoted to assistant commissioner of militia training for Shuzhou and exiled to Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 至虔州信豐而病，語其子景山曰：「吾不復南矣！

translations.literal: When he reached Xinfeng in Qianzhou he fell ill and said to his son Jingshan: "I shall go no farther south!"
translations.idiomatic: At Xinfeng in Qianzhou he fell ill and told his son Jingshan, "I will go no farther south!"

sentences.zh: 吾死汝歸，呂氏尚有遺種。

translations.literal: When I die you return home—the Lü clan still has descendants left.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, you return home. The Lü line will not die out.

sentences.zh: 」遂薨，年七十一。

translations.literal: He then died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 大忠請歸葬，許之。

translations.literal: Dazhong requested burial back home, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong petitioned for burial in their home region and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 大防身長七尺，眉目秀發，聲音如鐘。

translations.literal: Dafang stood seven chi tall, with handsome features and hair luxuriant, and a voice like a bell.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang stood seven chi tall, with handsome features and luxuriant hair, and a voice resonant as a bell.

sentences.zh: 自少持重，無嗜好，過市不左右游目，燕居如對賓客。

translations.literal: From youth he was grave; he had no hobbies; passing through the market he did not look about left and right; at ease he was as if receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was solemn and without indulgence. He never glanced about in the marketplace, and even in private he conducted himself as if before guests.

sentences.zh: 每朝會，威儀翼如，神宗常目送之。

translations.literal: At every court assembly his mien was dignified and orderly; Emperor Shenzong often watched him go with his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: At every court assembly his bearing was dignified and precise. Emperor Shenzong often followed him with his gaze as he departed.

sentences.zh: 與大忠及弟大臨同居，相切磋論道考禮，冠昏喪祭，一本於古，關中言《禮》學者推呂氏。

translations.literal: He lived together with Dazhong and his younger brother Dalin, mutually polishing each other in discussing the Way and examining ritual; capping, marriage, mourning and sacrifice—all took antiquity as their basis; in Guanzhong those who spoke of ritual learning honored the Lü clan.
translations.idiomatic: He lived with Dazhong and his younger brother Dalin, studying the Way and ritual together. Capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice in their household all followed ancient models, and in Guanzhong students of ritual pointed to the Lüs as models.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《鄉約》曰：「凡同約者，德業相勸，過失相規，禮俗相交，患難相恤，有善則書於籍，有過若違約者亦書之，三犯而行罰，不悛者絕之。」

translations.literal: He once wrote a Village Covenant, saying: "All who join in the covenant shall encourage one another in virtue and learning, admonish one another over faults, join in ritual and custom, and support one another in hardship. Good deeds shall be recorded in the register; faults and covenant violations shall also be recorded. After three offenses punishment is carried out; those who do not reform are cast out."
translations.idiomatic: He once drafted a Village Covenant: "All members shall encourage one another in virtue and learning, admonish one another over faults, join in ritual and custom, and help one another in hardship. Good deeds are recorded; faults and violations are recorded too. After three offenses there is punishment; the unreformed are expelled."

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，復其官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong came to the throne, Dafang's offices were restored.

sentences.zh: 高宗紹興初，又復大學士，贈太師、宣國公，諡曰「正愍」。

translations.literal: Early in Shaoxing under Emperor Gaozong, his grand academician rank was also restored; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Xuan, with the posthumous title Zhengmin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing reign Emperor Gaozong restored his grand academician title, posthumously enfeoffed him as grand preceptor and Duke of Xuan, and gave him the posthumous title Zhengmin.

sentences.zh: 兄 大忠

translations.literal: Elder brother: Dazhong
translations.idiomatic: Elder Brother: Dazhong

sentences.zh: 大忠，字進伯。

translations.literal: Dazhong, courtesy name Jinbo.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong, courtesy name Jinbo.

sentences.zh: 登第，為華陰尉、晉城令。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations and served as assistant magistrate of Huayin and magistrate of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations and served as assistant magistrate of Huayin and magistrate of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 韓絳宣撫陝西，以大忠提舉永興路義勇。

translations.literal: When Han Jiang was commissioner to pacify Shaanxi, he put Dazhong in charge of the volunteer forces of Yongxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang served as commissioner to pacify Shaanxi, he appointed Dazhong to oversee the volunteer forces of Yongxing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 改秘書丞，檢詳樞密院吏、兵房文字。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secretary of the Secretariat and examined documents in the personnel and military sections of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secretary of the Secretariat and assigned to examine documents in the personnel and military sections of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 令條義勇利害。

translations.literal: He was ordered to itemize the advantages and disadvantages of the volunteer forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to itemize the pros and cons of the volunteer force system.

sentences.zh: 大忠言：「養兵猥眾，國用日屈，漢之屯田，唐之府兵，善法也。

translations.literal: Dazhong said: "Maintaining troops is excessively numerous; state expenditure daily dwindles. Han garrison farming and Tang garrison militia are good methods."
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong said, "The army has grown wastefully large and state finances dwindle by the day. Han garrison farming and Tang militia levies were sound models."

sentences.zh: 弓箭手近於屯田，義勇近於府兵，擇用一焉，兵屯可省矣。

translations.literal: Archer-soldiers are close to garrison farming; volunteer forces are close to garrison militia—choose and use one of them, and military garrisons can be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Archer-soldiers resemble garrison farming and volunteer forces resemble militia levies. Adopt one of these models and garrison costs can be cut.

sentences.zh: 」為簽書定國軍判官。

translations.literal: He was made signing clerk and military administrator of Dingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed signing clerk and military administrator of Dingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，王安石議遣使諸道，立緣邊封溝，大忠與范育被命，俱辭行。

translations.literal: During the Xining era Wang Anshi proposed sending envoys to the various circuits to establish border demarcation trenches; Dazhong and Fan Yu were ordered and both declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining reforms Wang Anshi proposed sending envoys to the circuits to dig border demarcation trenches along the frontier. Dazhong and Fan Yu received the orders but both declined the mission.

sentences.zh: 大忠陳五不可，以為懷撫外國，恩信不洽，必致生患。

translations.literal: Dazhong set forth five reasons why it could not be done, holding that in winning over foreign states, if grace and trust were not in accord, trouble would surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong set out five reasons against the plan, arguing that if grace and trust were not established in dealing with foreign peoples, trouble would follow.

sentences.zh: 罷不遣。

translations.literal: The mission was canceled and not sent.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped and the envoys were not sent.

sentences.zh: 令與劉忱使契丹，議代北地，會遭父喪。

translations.literal: He was ordered to join Liu Chen as envoy to the Khitan to discuss lands north of Dai, but then his father died.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to join Liu Chen on a mission to the Khitan to negotiate over lands north of Dai, but his father died before he could depart.

sentences.zh: 起復，知代州。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he was made prefect of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Called back from mourning, he was appointed prefect of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹使蕭素、梁潁至代，設次，據主席，大忠與之爭，乃移次於長城北。

translations.literal: Khitan envoys Xiao Su and Liang Ying arrived at Dai; when the reception tent was set up they took the chief seat; Dazhong contended with them and the tent was moved to beyond the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys Xiao Su and Liang Ying arrived at Daizhou. When the reception tent was set up they claimed the seat of honor. Dazhong protested and the tent was moved beyond the Great Wall.

sentences.zh: 換西上閤門使、知石州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and prefect of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and prefect of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 大忠數與素、潁會，凡議，屢以理折之，素、潁稍屈。

translations.literal: Dazhong met often with Su and Ying; in every negotiation he repeatedly refuted them with reason, and Su and Ying gradually yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong met repeatedly with Xiao Su and Liang Ying. In every round of talks he wore them down with reason, and they gradually gave ground.

sentences.zh: 已而復使蕭禧來求代北地，神宗召執政與大忠、忱議，將從其請。

translations.literal: Before long envoys led by Xiao Xi came again seeking lands north of Dai; Emperor Shenzong summoned the chief ministers along with Dazhong and Chen to discuss it and was about to accede to their request.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiao Xi was sent again to demand lands north of Dai. Emperor Shenzong summoned the chief ministers along with Dazhong and Liu Chen to consult, and was inclined to accede.

sentences.zh: 大忠曰：「彼遣一使來，即與地五百里，若使魏王英弼來求關南，則何如？

translations.literal: Dazhong said: "They send one envoy and we at once give land five hundred li—if the Wei king Yingbi came seeking Guannan, then what?"
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong said, "They send one envoy and we hand over five hundred li of territory. What if the Wei king Yingbi came demanding Guannan?"

sentences.zh: 」神宗曰：「卿是何言也。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said: "What sort of words are these, sir?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said, "What sort of talk is that?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下既以臣言為不然，恐不可啟其漸。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty already holds my words incorrect—I fear one must not open the way to gradual encroachment."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If Your Majesty rejects what I say, I fear we must not open the door to incremental demands."

sentences.zh: 」忱曰：「大忠之言，社稷大計，願陛下熟思之。

translations.literal: Chen said: "Dazhong's words are a great plan for the altars of state—Your Majesty, I hope you will ponder them deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chen said, "Dazhong speaks for the security of the realm. I urge Your Majesty to weigh his words carefully."

sentences.zh: 」執政知不可奪，議卒不決，罷忱還三司，大忠亦終喪制。

translations.literal: The chief ministers knew the decision could not be changed; the deliberation ended without resolution; Chen was dismissed back to the Three Departments; Dazhong also completed his mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers saw they could not prevail. The deliberations ended unresolved. Liu Chen was sent back to the Three Departments and Dazhong completed his mourning observances.

sentences.zh: 其後竟以分水嶺為界焉。

translations.literal: Subsequently the boundary was finally set at Watershed Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the frontier was fixed at Watershed Ridge.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，為河北轉運判官，言：「古者理財，視天下猶一家。

translations.literal: During the Yuanfeng era he was transport commissioner for Hebei and said: "In antiquity in managing finances one regarded the realm as a single household."
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era, as transport commissioner for Hebei, he said, "In antiquity fiscal administration treated the realm as one household."

sentences.zh: 朝廷者家，外計者兄弟，居雖異而財無不同。

translations.literal: The court is the family; external accountant circuits are brothers—dwelling places differ but finances are not different.
translations.idiomatic: The court is the household and the outer circuits are like brothers. They may dwell apart, but their wealth is shared.

sentences.zh: 今有司惟知出納之名，有餘不足，未嘗以實告上。

translations.literal: Today the offices know only the names of receipts and disbursements; surplus and deficit—they have never reported the facts to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Today officials know only receipts and disbursements by name. Surplus and shortage are never reported honestly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 故有餘則取之，不足莫之與，甚大患也。

translations.literal: Thus when there is surplus they take from it; when there is deficit no one gives—this is a very great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Where there is surplus they take; where there is shortage none is supplied. That is a grave evil.

sentences.zh: 」乃上生財、養民十二事。

translations.literal: He then submitted twelve items on generating wealth and nourishing the people.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted twelve proposals for generating revenue and nourishing the people.

sentences.zh: 徙提點淮西刑獄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to intendant of judicial affairs for Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to intendant of judicial affairs for Huai West.

sentences.zh: 時河決，飛蝗為災，大忠入對，極論之，詔歸故官。

translations.literal: At the time the Yellow River breached its banks and locusts became a disaster; Dazhong entered audience and spoke on both at length; an edict restored him to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River had breached its banks and locusts ravaged the land. Dazhong had audience with the emperor and spoke at length on both crises. An edict restored him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，歷工部郎中、陝西轉運副使、知陝州，以直龍圖閣知秦州，進寶文閣待制。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanyou he successively served as director in the Ministry of Works, deputy transport commissioner for Shaanxi, prefect of Shanzhou; as direct associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall he was prefect of Qinzhou, and advanced to appointed draft master of the Hall for Treasuring Culture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou he served successively as director in the Ministry of Works, deputy transport commissioner for Shaanxi, and prefect of Shanzhou; then, as direct associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall, prefect of Qinzhou, and was promoted to appointed draft master of the Hall for Treasuring Culture.

sentences.zh: 夏人自犯麟府、環慶後，遂絕歲賜，欲遣使謝罪，神宗將許之。

translations.literal: After the Tangut violated Lin Prefecture, Fu Prefecture, Huan Prefecture and Qing Prefecture, they cut off the annual gifts and wished to send envoys to apologize; Emperor Shenzong was about to agree.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tangut attacks on Lin, Fu, Huan, and Qing, they suspended the annual tribute payments and wished to send envoys to apologize. Emperor Shenzong was inclined to accept.

sentences.zh: 大忠言：「夏人強則縱，困則服，今陽為恭順，實懼討伐。

translations.literal: Dazhong said: "When the Tangut are strong they are indulged; when hard pressed they submit—now they outwardly show deference but inwardly fear punitive action."
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong said, "When the Tangut are strong we indulge them; when they are cornered they submit. Now they pretend deference but really fear punishment."

sentences.zh: 宜且命邊臣詰其所以來之辭，若惟請是從，彼將有以窺我矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should first order frontier officials to question the grounds of their coming; if we simply accede to every request, they will find means to probe us."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should first have frontier officials challenge the stated reasons for their mission. If we simply grant every request, they will learn to test us."

sentences.zh: 時郡糴民粟，豪家因之制操縱之柄。

translations.literal: At the time the prefecture purchased grain from the people; great families thereby controlled the power to manipulate the market.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was buying grain from the people, and powerful families seized control of the market.

sentences.zh: 大忠選僚寀自旦入倉，雖斗升亦受，不使有所壅閼。

translations.literal: Dazhong selected subordinate officials to enter the granary from dawn; even a peck or a pint was accepted so that nothing would be blocked up.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong picked officials to staff the granary from dawn, accepting every measure down to the smallest so nothing would be turned away.

sentences.zh: 民喜，爭運粟於倉，負錢而去，得百餘萬斛。

translations.literal: The people rejoiced and competed to transport grain to the granary; bearing money they departed—more than a million hu were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced and rushed grain to the granary. They took payment and left. More than a million hu were collected.

sentences.zh: 馬涓以進士舉首入幕府，自稱狀元。

translations.literal: Ma Juan, ranking first in the jinshi examination, entered the staff office and called himself zhuangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Juan, who had placed first on the jinshi list, joined the staff and styled himself zhuangyuan.

sentences.zh: 大忠謂曰：「狀元云者，及第未除官之稱也，既為判官則不可。

translations.literal: Dazhong said to him: "Zhuangyuan means the title before an office is assigned after passing the examination—once you are a judge it is not appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong told him, "Zhuangyuan is what one is called between passing the examinations and receiving an appointment. As a staff judge you cannot use it."

sentences.zh: 今科舉之習既無用，修身為己之學，不可不勉。

translations.literal: Today the habits of the examinations are already useless—the learning of cultivating the self for its own sake cannot but be urged."
translations.idiomatic: The habits of the examination halls are worthless now. You must devote yourself to learning that cultivates the self."

sentences.zh: 」又教以臨政治民之要，涓自以為得師焉。

translations.literal: He also taught him the essentials of governing and managing the people; Juan considered that he had found a true teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He also taught him the essentials of governance. Juan felt he had found a true teacher.

sentences.zh: 謝良佐教授州學，大忠每過之，聽講《論語》，必正襟斂容曰：「聖人言行在焉，吾不敢不肅。」

translations.literal: Xie Liangzuo lectured at the prefectural school; whenever Dazhong passed by and listened to his lecture on the Analects, he would straighten his robe and compose his expression, saying: "The sage's words and conduct are here—I dare not be casual."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Liangzuo taught at the prefectural school. Whenever Dazhong stopped to hear him lecture on the Analects, he would sit up straight and say, "The sage's words and conduct are present here. I dare not be irreverent."

sentences.zh: 嘗獻曰：「夏人戍守之外，戰士不過十萬，吾三路之眾，足以當之矣。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial saying: "Beyond the Tangut garrisons, fighting troops are no more than one hundred thousand—our forces in the three circuits are sufficient to meet them."
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial: "Apart from garrison troops, the Tangut field no more than one hundred thousand fighters. Our forces in the three circuits are enough to meet them."

sentences.zh: 彼屢犯王略，一不與校，臣竊羞之。

translations.literal: They have repeatedly violated the royal domain and we have not once matched them—I, your servant, am secretly ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: They have violated our territory again and again without our answering once. I am ashamed of this."

sentences.zh: 」紹聖二年，加寶文閣直學士、知渭州，付以秦、渭之事，奏言：「關、陝民力未裕，士氣沮喪，非假之歲月，未易枝梧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaosheng he was given the additional title direct academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and made prefect of Weizhou; Qin and Wei affairs were entrusted to him; he submitted saying: "In Guan and Shaanxi the people's strength is not yet ample and military spirit is depressed—without allowing months and years, it will not be easy to sustain the effort."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaosheng he was made direct academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and prefect of Weizhou, with authority over Qin and Wei. He submitted: "In Guan and Shaanxi the people are not yet recovered and morale is low. Without time, the frontier cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 」因請以職事對。

translations.literal: He therefore requested to report on duties in audience.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to report on his duties in a special audience.

sentences.zh: 大抵欲以計徐取橫山，自汝遮殘井迤邐進築，不求近功。

translations.literal: In general he intended by strategy to take Hengshan gradually, advancing construction from Ruzhe and Canjing in succession, not seeking immediate achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In general he planned to take Hengshan gradually, advancing fortifications step by step from Ruzhe and Canjing without seeking quick success.

sentences.zh: 既而鐘傅城安西，王文郁亦用事，章惇、曾布主之，大忠議不合；

translations.literal: Before long Zhong Fu fortified Anxi and Wang Wenyü also wielded power; Zhang Dun and Zeng Bu backed them; Dazhong's views did not agree;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhong Fu fortified Anxi and Wang Wenyü gained influence, backed by Zhang Dun and Zeng Bu. Dazhong's views differed.

sentences.zh: 又乞以所進職為大防量移，惇、布陳其所言與元祐時異，徙知同州，旋降待制致仕。

translations.literal: He also requested that the office he had submitted be used to effect a moderated transfer for Dafang; Dun and Bu reported that what he said differed from Yuanyou times; he was transferred to prefect of Tongzhou, and soon was demoted from draft master and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the office he had just received be used to secure a less harsh transfer for Dafang. Zhang Dun and Zeng Bu cited his statements as inconsistent with his Yuanyou positions. He was moved to Tongzhou, then demoted from draft master and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，詔復學士官，佐其葬。

translations.literal: He died; an edict restored his academician office and assisted his burial.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, an edict restored his academician title and provided assistance for his burial.

sentences.zh: 弟 大鈞

translations.literal: Younger brother: Dajun
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother: Dajun

sentences.zh: 大鈞，字和叔。

translations.literal: Dajun, courtesy name Heshu.
translations.idiomatic: Dajun, courtesy name Heshu.

sentences.zh: 父蕡，六子，其五登科，大鈞第三子也。

translations.literal: His father Ben had six sons; five passed the examinations; Dajun was the third son.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ben had six sons, five of whom passed the examinations. Dajun was the third son.

sentences.zh: 中乙科，調秦州右司理參軍，監延州折博務。

translations.literal: He placed in the second category of the examinations and was assigned as judicial assistant of the right section of Qinzhou and superintendent of the tea-and-horse trade office at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed in the second examination category and was assigned judicial assistant of the right section at Qinzhou and superintendent of the tea-and-horse trade at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 改光祿寺丞、知三原縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant director of the Office of Imperial Entertainments and made magistrate of Sanyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director of the Office of Imperial Entertainments and appointed magistrate of Sanyuan County.

sentences.zh: 請代蕡入蜀，移巴西縣。

translations.literal: He requested to replace Ben's posting into Shu and was transferred to Baxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to take his father's place on a posting into Shu and was transferred to Baxi County.

sentences.zh: 蕡致仕，大鈞亦移疾不行。

translations.literal: When Ben retired, Dajun also reported illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Ben retired, Dajun also pleaded illness and declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 韓絳宣撫陝西、河東，辟書寫機密文字。

translations.literal: When Han Jiang was commissioner to pacify Shaanxi and Hedong, he recruited him as scribe for confidential documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang served as commissioner to pacify Shaanxi and Hedong, he recruited Dajun as a scribe for confidential documents.

sentences.zh: 府罷，移知候官縣，故相曾公亮鎮京兆，薦知涇陽縣，皆不赴。

translations.literal: When the commissioner's office was abolished, he was transferred to be magistrate of Houguan County; former chief minister Zeng Gongliang governed Jingzhao and recommended him as magistrate of Jingyang County—he accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: When the commissioner's staff was dissolved, he was offered the magistracy of Houguan. Former chief minister Zeng Gongliang, then governing Jingzhao, recommended him for Jingyang. He declined both.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，家居講道。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he stayed home and lectured on the Way.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he remained at home lecturing on the Way.

sentences.zh: 數年，起為諸王宮教授。

translations.literal: After several years he was recalled as lecturer at the Princes' Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was recalled to serve as lecturer at the Princes' Palace.

sentences.zh: 求監鳳翔船務，制改宣義郎。

translations.literal: He requested to superintend the Fengxiang shipping office; by regulation he was changed to Gentleman for Manifest Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to superintend the Fengxiang shipping office and was reclassified as Gentleman for Manifest Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 會伐西夏，鄜延轉運司檄為從事。

translations.literal: When a campaign was mounted against Western Xia, the transport office of Fuyan circuit summoned him as staff aide.
translations.idiomatic: When a campaign was launched against Western Xia, the Fuyan transport office summoned him as a staff aide.

sentences.zh: 既出塞，轉運使李稷饋餉不繼，欲還安定取糧，使大鈞請於种諤。

translations.literal: After they had crossed the border, Transport Commissioner Li Ji could not keep supplies coming; wishing to return to Anding to fetch grain, he sent Dajun to request permission from Zhong E.
translations.idiomatic: After the army crossed the frontier, Transport Commissioner Li Ji could not keep supplies flowing. Wishing to return to Anding for grain, he sent Dajun to ask Zhong E.

sentences.zh: 諤曰：「吾受命將兵，安知糧道！

translations.literal: E said: "I received orders to lead troops—what do I know of supply routes!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong E said, "I was ordered to command troops. What do I know of supply lines!"

sentences.zh: 萬一不繼，召稷來，與一劍耳。

translations.literal: If by chance supplies fail, summon Ji here—I will simply give him a sword."
translations.idiomatic: If they fail, summon Li Ji here and I will give him a sword, that is all."

sentences.zh: 」大鈞性剛直，即曰：「朝廷出師，去塞未遠，遂斬轉運使，無君父乎？

translations.literal: Dajun's nature was firm and upright; he at once said: "The court has sent out the army—you are not yet far from the border and would execute the transport commissioner—have you no lord and father?"
translations.idiomatic: Dajun, who was blunt by nature, replied at once, "The court has sent out this army. We are barely beyond the frontier and you would execute the transport commissioner? Have you no loyalty to ruler and father?"

sentences.zh: 」諤意折，強謂大鈞曰：「君欲以此報稷，先稷受禍矣！

translations.literal: E's spirit was broken; he forced himself to say to Dajun: "Sir, if you wish to avenge Ji in this way, Ji will suffer disaster first!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong E was taken aback and blustered, "If you mean to settle a score for Li Ji this way, Li Ji will be the one harmed first!"

sentences.zh: 」大鈞怒曰：「公將以此言見恐邪？

translations.literal: Dajun angrily said: "Sir, do you mean to frighten me with these words?"
translations.idiomatic: Dajun flared up. "Do you think to frighten me with talk like that?"

sentences.zh: 吾委身事主，死無所辭，正恐公過耳。

translations.literal: I have committed my person to serving my lord; death I would not refuse—I only fear that you go too far."
translations.idiomatic: I have pledged myself to my superiors and would not shrink from death. What I fear is that you are going too far."

sentences.zh: 」諤見其直，乃好謂曰：「子乃爾邪？

translations.literal: E saw his straightforwardness and therefore spoke pleasantly, saying: "So this is the sort of man you are?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his blunt honesty, Zhong E changed tone and said amiably, "So you are that sort of man?"

sentences.zh: 今聽汝矣！

translations.literal: "From now on I grant your request!"
translations.idiomatic: "Very well—I grant your request!"

sentences.zh: 」始許稷還。

translations.literal: Only then did he permit Ji to return.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he allow Li Ji to go back.

sentences.zh: 是時，微大鈞盛氣誚諤，稷且不免。

translations.literal: At this time, but for Dajun's burning indignation in reproaching E, Ji would almost have been unable to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Had Dajun not confronted Zhong E with such fierce indignation, Li Ji would scarcely have escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 未幾，道得疾，卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: Before long, en route he fell ill and died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill on the road and died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 大鈞從張載學，能守其師說而踐履之。

translations.literal: Dajun studied under Zhang Zai; he could preserve his teacher's doctrines and put them into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Dajun studied under Zhang Zai, held fast to his master's teachings, and lived by them.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，衰麻葬祭，一本於禮。

translations.literal: While observing mourning for his father, in dress of hemp and funeral and sacrificial rites, he took ritual as his single standard.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father, his dress, burial, and sacrifices all followed ritual to the letter.

sentences.zh: 後乃行於冠昏、膳飲、慶吊之間，節文粲然可觀，關中化之。

translations.literal: Later he extended this practice to capping, marriage, feasting, drinking, and occasions of congratulation and condolence; the forms were brilliantly visible, and the Guanzhong region was transformed by him.
translations.idiomatic: He later extended these observances to capping ceremonies, weddings, banquets, and occasions of congratulation and condolence. The forms were so clear and orderly that all of Guanzhong took them as a model.

sentences.zh: 尤喜講明井田兵制，謂治道必自此始，悉撰次為圖籍，可見於用。

translations.literal: He especially delighted in clarifying the well-field system and military organization, holding that the way of good government must begin from these; he fully compiled them into diagrams and records that could be applied in practice.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to explaining the well-field system and military organization, arguing that good government must begin there. He compiled complete illustrated records that could be put to use.

sentences.zh: 雖皆本於載，而能自信力行，載每歎其勇為不可及。

translations.literal: Although all derived from Zai, he could believe in himself and act resolutely; Zai often sighed that his bold action was beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: Though his ideas all stemmed from Zhang Zai, he had the confidence to act on them himself, and Zhang often sighed that his boldness was beyond comparison.

sentences.zh: 弟 大臨

translations.literal: Younger brother Dalin
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Lü Dalin

sentences.zh: 大臨，字與叔。

translations.literal: Dalin, courtesy name Yushu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dalin, whose courtesy name was Yushu,

sentences.zh: 學於程頤，與謝良佐、游酢、楊時在程門，號「四先生」。

translations.literal: He studied under Cheng Yi; with Xie Liangzuo, You Zuo, and Yang Shi in Cheng's school, they were styled the "Four Masters."
translations.idiomatic: Studied under Cheng Yi. With Xie Liangzuo, You Zuo, and Yang Shi among Cheng's disciples he was known as one of the "Four Masters."

sentences.zh: 通《六經》，尤邃於《禮》。

translations.literal: He was versed in the Six Classics and especially deep in the Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Six Classics and was especially profound in the Rites.

sentences.zh: 每欲掇習三代遺文舊制，令可行，不為空言以拂世駭俗。

translations.literal: He always wished to gather and practice the transmitted texts and old institutions of the Three Dynasties, making them workable, not empty words that would go against the age and shock custom.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly sought to recover and practice the textual legacy and institutions of the Three Dynasties and make them workable—not empty talk that would shock society.

sentences.zh: 其論選舉曰：

translations.literal: His discussion of selection and appointment says:
translations.idiomatic: On the subject of recruitment and appointment he wrote:

sentences.zh: 「古之長育人才者，以士眾多為樂；

translations.literal: "Those in antiquity who nurtured talent took delight in the multitude of scholars;
translations.idiomatic: "In antiquity those who cultivated talent took joy in having many worthy men;

sentences.zh: 今之主選舉者，以多為患。

translations.literal: those today who preside over selection treat multitude as a trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Those who preside over recruitment today treat a large number as a problem.

sentences.zh: 古以禮聘士，常恐士之不至；

translations.literal: In antiquity scholars were invited by ritual; one always feared that scholars would not come;
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity recruited scholars through ritual courtesies and always feared they would not come;

sentences.zh: 今以法待士，常恐士之競進。

translations.literal: today scholars are treated by law; one always fears that scholars will compete to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Today scholars are managed by regulations and one always fears they will scramble for advancement.

sentences.zh: 古今豈有異哉。

translations.literal: Can antiquity and the present really differ?
translations.idiomatic: How can antiquity and the present truly differ?

sentences.zh: 蓋未之思爾。

translations.literal: It is simply that one has not thought it through.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that people have not thought the matter through."

sentences.zh: 夫為國之要，不過得人以治其事，如為治必欲得人，惟恐人才之不足，而何患於多？

translations.literal: Now the essential of governing a state is nothing but obtaining men to administer affairs; if in governing one necessarily seeks men, one only fears insufficient talent—why worry about too many?
translations.idiomatic: The essence of governing a state is simply to obtain the right men to administer affairs. If one must have talent to govern well, one should fear only a shortage of men—why fret over having too many?

sentences.zh: 如治事皆任其責，惟恐士之不至，不憂其競進也。

translations.literal: If in administering affairs each man is charged with his responsibility, one only fears that scholars will not come—there is no worry about their competing to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When every post carries real responsibility, the only fear is that worthy men will not come—there is no reason to worry about their rushing forward.

sentences.zh: 今取人而用，不問其可任何事；

translations.literal: Today in taking men and employing them, one does not ask what affairs each can undertake;
translations.idiomatic: Today men are appointed without asking what tasks each can undertake;

sentences.zh: 任人以事，不問其才之所堪。

translations.literal: in charging men with affairs, one does not ask what their talent can bear.
translations.idiomatic: And tasks are assigned without asking what each man's talents can sustain.

sentences.zh: 故入流之路不勝其多，然為官擇士則常患乏才；

translations.literal: Thus the paths into the ranks cannot be exceeded for multitude, yet in selecting scholars for office one constantly suffers from lack of talent;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the paths into office are more crowded than ever, yet when choosing men for posts there is a constant shortage of talent;

sentences.zh: 待次之吏歷歲不調，然考其職事則常患不治。

translations.literal: officials waiting their turn go years without reassignment, yet when examining their duties one constantly suffers from poor administration.
translations.idiomatic: While officials awaiting promotion go years without appointment, yet when their work is examined poor performance is the constant complaint.

sentences.zh: 是所謂名實不稱，本末交戾。

translations.literal: This is what is called name and reality not matching, root and branch crossing in conflict.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant when name and reality fail to match and means and ends work against each other.

sentences.zh: 如此而欲得人而事治，未之有也。

translations.literal: Wishing thus to obtain men and have affairs well governed—there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: To expect good government under such conditions has never been possible.

sentences.zh: 今欲立士規以養德厲行，更學制以量才進藝，定試法以區別能否，修辟法以興能備用，嚴舉法以核實得人，制考法以責任考功，庶幾可以漸復古矣。」

translations.literal: Now if we wish to establish regulations for scholars to cultivate virtue and strengthen conduct, reform the school system to measure talent and advance skill, fix examination methods to distinguish ability from inability, refine recruitment methods to raise up talent and prepare it for use, tighten recommendation methods to verify reality and obtain men, and devise evaluation methods to assign responsibility and examine achievement—in these ways we might gradually restore antiquity."
