translations.idiomatic: We should set standards for scholars to cultivate virtue and discipline conduct, reform the school system to measure talent and advance learning, establish examinations to separate the capable from the incapable, refine recruitment to develop and deploy talent, tighten recommendation standards to ensure that appointments match merit, and create evaluation procedures to hold men accountable for results. In this way we might gradually return to the ways of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 富弼致政於家，為佛氏之學。

translations.literal: Fu Bi retired from office and lived at home, practicing Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: After retiring from office, Fu Bi devoted himself at home to Buddhist studies.

sentences.zh: 大臨與之書曰：「古者三公無職事，惟有德者居之，內則論道於朝，外則主教於鄉。

translations.literal: Dalin wrote to him: "In antiquity the Three Excellencies had no routine duties; only men of virtue held these posts—within they discussed the Way at court, without they chiefly taught in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Dalin wrote to him: "In antiquity the Three Excellencies had no routine administrative duties; only men of virtue filled them. Within the court they expounded the Way; abroad they led instruction in their districts.

sentences.zh: 古之大人當是任者，必將以斯道覺斯民，成己以成物，豈以爵位進退、體力盛衰為之變哉？

translations.literal: The great men of antiquity who undertook such responsibility would surely use this Way to awaken the people, completing themselves in order to complete things—how could changes in rank, advancement or withdrawal, or the strength or decline of the body alter this?
translations.idiomatic: The great men who accepted such responsibility sought to awaken the people through the Way, perfecting themselves to perfect the world. How could the rise and fall of office, or the vigor or decline of one's body, change that calling?

sentences.zh: 今大道未明，人趨異學，不入於莊，則入於釋。

translations.literal: Now the Great Way is not yet clear; men rush to heterodox learning—if they do not enter Zhuangzi, then they enter Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Way is not yet fully understood and people flock to heterodox teachings—if not to Zhuangzi, then to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 疑聖人為未盡善，輕禮義為不足學，人倫不明，萬物憔悴，此老成大人惻隱存心之時。

translations.literal: They doubt the sages were not fully good, treat rites and righteousness as unworthy of study; human relations are unclear and the myriad things wither—this is the time when an aged and mature great man should store compassion in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: They doubt the sages were less than perfect and dismiss rites and righteousness as unworthy of study. Human relations are obscured and the world languishes. This is the moment when a seasoned elder should act from humane concern.

sentences.zh: 以道自任，振起壞俗，在公之力，宜無難矣。

translations.literal: Taking the Way as one's charge, rousing up corrupt custom—this lies within your power, and ought to be nothing difficult.
translations.idiomatic: To take the Way upon yourself and revive a fallen age is well within your power—it should not be difficult at all.

sentences.zh: 若夫移精變氣，務求長年，此山谷避世之士獨善其身者之所好，豈世之所以望於公者哉？

translations.literal: As for transforming essence and altering vital breath, striving to seek long life—this is what recluses in mountain valleys who keep their goodness to themselves delight in; how can this be what the world expects of you?"
translations.idiomatic: As for refining the spirit and altering the breath in pursuit of long life—that is the pursuit of recluses who withdraw to the hills and care only for themselves. Is that truly what the world expects of you?"

sentences.zh: 」弼謝之。

translations.literal: Bi thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi thanked him for the admonition.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，為太學博士，遷秘書省正字。

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou reign he served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and was promoted to Correcting Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era he served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and was promoted to Correcting Clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 范祖禹薦其好學修身如古人，可備勸學，未及用而卒。

translations.literal: Fan Zuyu recommended that his love of learning and cultivation of self were like the ancients and that he could fill a post encouraging study; before he could be employed he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zuyu recommended him for his ancient-style devotion to learning and self-cultivation, saying he could serve in promoting scholarship, but before he could be appointed Dalin died.

sentences.zh: 劉摯，字莘老，永靜東光人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhi, courtesy name Xinlao, was a man of Dongguang in Yongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Xinlao, was a native of Dongguang in Yongjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 兒時，父居正課以書，朝夕不少間。

translations.literal: In childhood his father Juzheng drilled him in books, morning and evening without the least pause.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy his father Juzheng drilled him in his studies without respite from morning till night.

sentences.zh: 或謂：「君止一子，獨不可少寬邪？

translations.literal: Someone said: "You have but one son—surely you could relax a little?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "You have only this one son. Surely you could be a little easier on him?"

sentences.zh: 」居正曰：「正以一子，不可縱也。

translations.literal: Juzheng said: "Precisely because I have but one son, I cannot indulge him."
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng replied, "Precisely because I have only one son I must not indulge him."

sentences.zh: 」十歲而孤，鞠於外氏，就學東平，因家焉。

translations.literal: At age ten he was orphaned; he was reared by his mother's family, went to study at Dongping, and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: He was orphaned at ten, raised by his mother's family, and went to study at Dongping, where he settled.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，擢甲科，歷冀州南宮令。

translations.literal: During the Jiayou reign he ranked in the top class of the examinations and served successively as magistrate of Nangong in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiayou era he passed the examinations in the top class and served as magistrate of Nangong in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 縣比不得入，俗化凋敝，其賦甚重，輸絹匹折稅錢五百，綿兩折錢三十，民多破產。

translations.literal: The county was among those not admitted to equivalence; customs were decayed and desolate, and its levies were very heavy—a bolt of silk converted to tax at five hundred coins, two ounces of cotton at thirty coins—and many people were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The county ranked below the standard for tax assessment; customs were decayed and levies crushing—a bolt of silk was assessed at five hundred cash and two ounces of cotton at thirty, and many families were ruined.

sentences.zh: 摯援例旁郡，條請裁以中價。

translations.literal: Zhi cited precedents from neighboring prefectures and submitted a detailed request to fix rates at middle market price.
translations.idiomatic: Citing precedents from neighboring prefectures, Zhi petitioned to set conversion rates at fair market prices.

sentences.zh: 轉運使怒，將劾之。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner was angry and was about to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner was furious and prepared to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 摯固請曰：「獨一州六邑被此苦，決非法意，但朝廷不知耳。

translations.literal: Zhi firmly petitioned: "Alone one prefecture and six districts suffer this hardship; this is certainly not the intent of the law—it is simply that the court does not know."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi pressed his case: "Only one prefecture and six counties suffer this hardship. That cannot be the intent of the law—the court simply does not know."

sentences.zh: 」遂告於朝。

translations.literal: He then reported it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought the matter before the court.

sentences.zh: 三司使包拯奏從其議，自是絹為錢千三百，綿七十有六。

translations.literal: Privy Treasurer Bao Zheng memorialized accepting his proposal; from then on silk was assessed at one thousand three hundred coins and cotton at seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Treasurer Bao Zheng memorialized in favor of his proposal. From then on silk was assessed at thirteen hundred cash and cotton at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 民歡呼至泣下，曰：「劉長官活我！

translations.literal: The people shouted for joy until tears ran down, saying: "Magistrate Liu has saved our lives!"
translations.idiomatic: The people shouted for joy until they wept, crying, "Magistrate Liu has saved our lives!"

sentences.zh: 」是時，摯與信都令李沖、清河令黃莘皆以治行聞，人稱為「河朔三令」。

translations.literal: At this time Zhi, together with Magistrate Li Chong of Xindu and Magistrate Huang Shen of Qinghe, were all renowned for their governance; people called them the "Three Magistrates of Heshuo."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhi, together with Li Chong of Xindu and Huang Shen of Qinghe, were all known for excellent administration and were called the "Three Magistrates of Heshuo."

sentences.zh: 徙江陵觀察推官，用韓琦薦，得館閣校勘。

translations.literal: He was transferred to investigating clerk of Jiangling observation commissioner; through Han Qi's recommendation he obtained the post of collating clerk in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to investigating clerk at Jiangling and, on Han Qi's recommendation, received appointment as collator in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 王安石一見器異之，擢檢正中書禮房，默默非所好也。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi at first sight regarded him as extraordinary and promoted him to reviser in the Rites Section of the Secretariat-Chancellery; silently he found it not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was impressed at first meeting and promoted him to reviser in the Secretariat-Chancellery's Rites Section, but Zhi quietly found the post uncongenial.

sentences.zh: 才月餘，為監察御史裏行，欣然就職，歸語家人曰：「趣裝，毋為安居計。

translations.literal: After barely more than a month he became investigating censor by provisional appointment; he gladly took office and on returning told his family: "Quick, pack—we must not plan for settled comfort."
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month he was appointed provisional investigating censor. He took the post gladly and told his family on returning home, "Pack up—we must not plan on settling in."

sentences.zh: 」未及陛對，即奏論：「亳州獄起不止，小人意在傾富弼以市進，今弼已得罪，願少寬之。

translations.literal: Before he had yet been received in audience he memorialized: "The case in Bozhou keeps arising without end; petty men intend to overturn Fu Bi to buy advancement; now that Bi has already been punished, I wish you would show a little leniency."
translations.idiomatic: Before his first audience he memorialized: "The case at Bozhou keeps resurfacing. Petty men mean to ruin Fu Bi for their own advancement. Now that Bi has already been punished, I beg you to show some leniency."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「程昉開漳河，調發猝迫，人不堪命。

translations.literal: He also said: "Cheng Fang opened the Zhang River—conscript labor was sudden and urgent, and the people could not endure it."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Cheng Fang's opening of the Zhang River canal was rushed through with sudden conscription; the people could not bear it."

sentences.zh: 趙子幾擅升畿縣等，使納役錢，縣民日數千人遮訴宰相，京師喧然，何以示四方？

translations.literal: Zhao Ziji on his own authority raised the grade of metropolitan counties and required payment of corvée money; county people daily numbered in the thousands blocking the way to appeal to the chief councillor—the capital was in uproar; how can this be shown to the four quarters?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ziji arbitrarily raised the grade of metropolitan counties and demanded corvée payments. Thousands of county residents daily blocked the roads to appeal to the chief councillor, stirring uproar in the capital. What message does this send to the realm?

sentences.zh: 張靚、王廷老擅增兩浙役錢，督賦嚴急，人情嗟怨。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang and Wang Tinglao on their own authority increased corvée money in the Two Zhes—the collection of levies was harsh and urgent, and popular sentiment groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang and Wang Tinglao unilaterally raised corvée payments in the Two Zhes, enforcing collection with harsh urgency and stirring widespread resentment.

sentences.zh: 此皆欲以羡餘希賞，願行顯責，明朝廷本無聚斂之意。」

translations.literal: All these wish to use surplus revenue to seek rewards; I wish you would impose conspicuous punishment and make clear that the court from the first had no intent to amass wealth."
translations.idiomatic: All of these men seek rewards through surplus revenue. I urge clear and public punishment to show that the court never intended to enrich itself through exactions."

sentences.zh: 及入見，神宗面賜褒諭。

translations.literal: When he entered audience, Shenzong personally bestowed praise and commendation to his face.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience Shenzong personally praised and commended him.

sentences.zh: 因問：「卿從學王安石邪？

translations.literal: He then asked: "Did you study under Wang Anshi?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Did you study under Wang Anshi?"

sentences.zh: 安石極稱卿器識。

translations.literal: Anshi greatly praises your capacity and insight."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi speaks very highly of your talent and judgment."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣東北人，少孤獨學，不識安石也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject is a man of the Northeast; orphaned in youth I studied alone—I do not know Anshi."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I am from the northeast. Orphaned as a youth, I studied on my own. I do not know Wang Anshi."

sentences.zh: 」退而上疏曰：

translations.literal: On retiring he submitted a further memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawing he submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 「君子小人之分，在義利而已。

translations.literal: "The distinction between the gentleman and the petty man lies in righteousness and profit, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: "The line between gentleman and petty man is drawn between righteousness and profit, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 小人才非不足用，特心之所向，不在乎義。

translations.literal: Petty men's talent is not insufficient for use; it is only that what their hearts aim at does not lie in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men are often capable enough; what they lack is any orientation toward righteousness.

sentences.zh: 故希賞之志，每在事先；

translations.literal: Thus the desire to seek reward is always ahead of the matter;
translations.idiomatic: Their eagerness for reward always comes before the public good;

sentences.zh: 奉公之心，每在私後。

translations.literal: the heart that serves the public is always after private interest.
translations.idiomatic: Their devotion to public duty always comes after private interest.

sentences.zh: 陛下有勸農之意，今變而為煩擾；

translations.literal: Your Majesty had the intent to encourage agriculture; now it has changed into vexation and turmoil;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty meant to encourage agriculture, yet it has become vexation and turmoil;

sentences.zh: 陛下有均役之意，今倚以為聚斂。

translations.literal: Your Majesty had the intent to equalize corvée; now it is relied upon as a means of amassing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty meant to equalize corvée duties, yet they have become a tool for revenue extraction.

sentences.zh: 其有愛君之心，憂國之言者，皆無以容於其間。

translations.literal: Those who possess a heart that loves the ruler and words that worry for the state all have no place to be received among them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who truly love the ruler and speak for the state's welfare find no place among them.

sentences.zh: 今天下有喜於敢為，有樂於無事。

translations.literal: Today in the realm there are those who rejoice in daring action and those who delight in doing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm divides between those who delight in daring action and those who delight in doing nothing.

sentences.zh: 彼以此為流俗，此以彼為亂常。

translations.literal: The former take the latter as vulgar convention; the latter take the former as disturbing the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Each side calls the other vulgar or disruptive of proper order.

sentences.zh: 畏義者以進取為可恥，嗜利者以守道為無能。

translations.literal: Those who fear righteousness regard advancement as shameful; those who crave profit regard guarding the Way as incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: Men who revere righteousness are mocked for seeking office; men who crave profit dismiss integrity as weakness.

sentences.zh: 此風浸成，漢、唐黨禍必起矣。

translations.literal: As this wind gradually forms, the faction calamities of Han and Tang are sure to arise.
translations.idiomatic: If this spirit takes hold, the factional disasters of Han and Tang will surely come again.

sentences.zh: 惟君子為能通天下之志。

translations.literal: Only the gentleman can penetrate the wills of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only the gentleman can truly unite the minds of the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下虛心平聽，審察好惡，前日意以為是者，今更察其非；

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to empty your heart and listen with balance, carefully examine likes and dislikes—what yesterday you thought right, today examine further for its wrong;
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to listen with an open mind and weigh preferences carefully—what seemed right yesterday, examine today for its errors;

sentences.zh: 前日意以為短者，今更用其長。

translations.literal: what yesterday you thought a shortcoming, today further employ its strength.
translations.idiomatic: What seemed a failing yesterday, employ today for its strengths.

sentences.zh: 稍抑虛譁輕偽、志近忘遠、幸於苟合之人，漸察忠厚慎重、難進易退、可與有為之士。

translations.literal: Gradually suppress those who are empty and clamorous, light and false, whose aims are near and forget what is far, who rely on hasty agreement; gradually discern those who are loyal and thick, careful and weighty, hard to advance and easy to withdraw, men with whom one may accomplish something.
translations.idiomatic: Restrain somewhat the brash, superficial, short-sighted men who grasp at easy compromise, and gradually discern the loyal, prudent men who are slow to advance and quick to withdraw—men capable of real achievement.

sentences.zh: 收過與不及之俗，使會於大中之道，則施設變化，惟陛下號令之而已。」

translations.literal: Gather the customs of excess and insufficiency and make them meet in the great central Way—then in setting forth and transforming, it is only for Your Majesty to command."
translations.idiomatic: Reconcile excess and deficiency in custom and bring them together in the great middle Way. Then whatever reforms you undertake will depend on Your Majesty's command alone."

sentences.zh: 又論率錢助役、官自雇人有十害，其略曰：

translations.literal: He also discussed the ten harms of the levy money to assist corvée and government hiring of laborers; the summary says:
translations.idiomatic: He also set out ten evils of the corvée-assistance levy and official hiring of laborers, in summary as follows:

sentences.zh: 「天下州縣戶役，虛實重輕不同。

translations.literal: "Household corvée across the prefectures and counties of the realm differs in emptiness and fullness, heaviness and lightness."
translations.idiomatic: "Household corvée obligations differ from place to place in burden and exemption."

sentences.zh: 今等以為率，則非一法所能齊；

translations.literal: If now equalizing to apply a single rate, one law cannot make them uniform;
translations.idiomatic: If a single uniform rate is imposed, no one law can make them equal;

sentences.zh: 隨其所宜，各自立法，則紛擾散殊，何以統率？

translations.literal: if following what is suitable each place legislates separately, then confusion and dispersal differ—how can they be unified?
translations.idiomatic: If each locality legislates as it sees fit, confusion and inconsistency multiply—how can the system be governed as one?

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: This is the first.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first evil.

sentences.zh: 新法謂版籍不實，故令別立等第。

translations.literal: The new law says household registers are untrue, therefore it orders the separate establishment of grades.
translations.idiomatic: The new law holds that household registers are unreliable and therefore orders new gradings.

sentences.zh: 且舊籍既不可信，今何以得其無失？

translations.literal: Yet if the old registers are already untrustworthy, how can the new ones be free of error?
translations.idiomatic: If the old registers were untrustworthy, why should the new ones be free of error?

sentences.zh: 不獨搔擾生事患，將使富輸少，貧輸多，二也。

translations.literal: Not only will it scratch and stir up affairs as a trouble—it will also make the rich pay less and the poor pay more; this is the second.
translations.idiomatic: This will not only stir up trouble but also make the rich pay less and the poor pay more. That is the second evil.

sentences.zh: 天下上戶少，中戶多。

translations.literal: In the realm upper households are few and middle households many.
translations.idiomatic: Upper households are few throughout the realm; middle households are many.

sentences.zh: 上戶役數而重，故以助錢為幸。

translations.literal: Upper households' corvée duties are numerous and heavy, so they regard assistance money as fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Upper households bear numerous and heavy corvée duties, so they welcome paying money in lieu.

sentences.zh: 中戶役簡而輕，下戶役所不及。

translations.literal: Middle households' corvée is simple and light; lower households' corvée does not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Middle households face lighter duties; lower households are barely touched.

sentences.zh: 今概使輸錢，則為不幸，三也。

translations.literal: If now all are made to pay money without exception, then for them it is misfortune; this is the third.
translations.idiomatic: To require all alike to pay money is a misfortune for them. That is the third evil.

sentences.zh: 有司欲多得雇錢，而患上戶之寡，故不用舊籍，臨時升降，使民何以堪命？

translations.literal: The officials wish to obtain much hiring money but worry that upper households are too few, therefore they do not use old registers and temporarily raise or lower grades—how can the people endure such orders?
translations.idiomatic: Officials want more hiring money but worry that upper households are too few, so they disregard old registers and manipulate grades on the spot. How can the people bear it?

sentences.zh: 四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth evil.

sentences.zh: 歲有豐凶，而役人有定數，助錢不可闕。

translations.literal: Years have bounty and famine, yet corvée laborers have fixed quotas—the assistance money cannot be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests may be rich or poor, yet corvée quotas stay fixed and the money in lieu of service cannot be waived.

sentences.zh: 非若稅賦有倚閣、減放之期，五也。

translations.literal: It is not like tax levies, which have periods of deferral and reduction—this is the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Unlike tax levies, which may be deferred or reduced, no such relief exists here. That is the fifth evil.

sentences.zh: 穀、麥、布、帛，歲有所出，而助法必輸見錢，六也。

translations.literal: Grain, wheat, cloth, and silk are produced each year, yet the assistance law requires payment in cash—this is the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Grain, wheat, cloth, and silk are produced every year, yet the assistance law demands cash on the barrelhead. That is the sixth evil.

sentences.zh: 二稅科買，色目已多，又概率錢以竭其所有，斯民無有悅而願為農者，戶口當日耗失，七也。

translations.literal: The two taxes and state purchases already involve many categories; now money is also levied proportionally to drain all they have—among these people none are glad to farm; household registers will daily dwindle—this is the seventh.
translations.idiomatic: The two taxes and state purchases already cover many categories, and now proportional cash levies drain whatever people still hold. None among the common folk will gladly remain farmers, and household registers will shrink day by day. That is the seventh evil.

sentences.zh: 僥倖者又將緣法生奸，如近日兩浙倍科錢數，自以為功，八也。

translations.literal: Opportunists will again exploit the law to commit fraud, as recently in Liangzhe where monetary levies were doubled and officials took it as merit—this is the eighth.
translations.idiomatic: Opportunists will exploit the law to commit fraud, as when officials in Liangzhe recently doubled cash levies and counted it as achievement. That is the eighth evil.

sentences.zh: 差法近者十餘年，遠或二十年，乃一充役，民安習之久矣。

translations.literal: Under the dispatch system, near at hand ten-odd years, far off perhaps twenty, before one serves corvée—the people have long been accustomed to this.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old dispatch system, a man might serve corvée only once in ten-odd years nearby, or once in twenty farther out, and the people had long grown used to it.

sentences.zh: 今官自雇人，直重則民不堪，輕則人不願，不免以力毆之就役，九也。

translations.literal: Now the government hires labor itself: if wages are high the people cannot bear it; if low, no one will come—so they cannot avoid using force to drive people into service—this is the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Now the government hires labor itself. If wages are set high the people cannot afford them; if set low, no one will come—and officials cannot avoid driving men into service by force. That is the ninth evil.

sentences.zh: 且役人必用鄉戶，家有常產，則必知自愛；

translations.literal: Moreover, corvée workers must be drawn from native households; when a family has fixed property, they necessarily know to cherish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, corvée workers ought to be drawn from native households; families with fixed property know how to value themselves.

sentences.zh: 性既愚實，則罕有盜欺。

translations.literal: Their nature being simple and honest, theft and fraud are rare.
translations.idiomatic: Simple and honest by nature, they rarely steal or cheat.

sentences.zh: 今一切雇募，但得輕猾浮偽之人，巧詐相資，何所不至？

translations.literal: Now with universal hiring and recruitment, one gets only frivolous, cunning, pretentious men who assist one another in trickery—what would they not do?
translations.idiomatic: Now with universal hiring, one gets only frivolous, cunning, and pretentious men who abet one another in deceit—what would they stop at?

sentences.zh: 十也。」

translations.literal: This is the tenth."
translations.idiomatic: That is the tenth evil."

sentences.zh: 會御史中丞楊繪亦言其非，安石使張琥作十難以詰之，琥辭不為，司農曾布請為之。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Hui also spoke against it; Anshi had Zhang Hu compose ten objections to cross-examine them; Hu declined; Minister of Revenue Zeng Bu volunteered to do it.
translations.idiomatic: About then Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Hui also spoke against the policy. Anshi had Zhang Hu draft ten objections to cross-examine them, but Hu declined, and Minister of Revenue Zeng Bu offered to do it instead.

sentences.zh: 既作十難，且劾摯、繪欺誕懷向背。

translations.literal: Once he had written the ten objections, he also impeached Zhi and Hui for deceit and harboring double allegiances.
translations.idiomatic: After drafting the ten objections, he also impeached Zhi and Hui for deception and divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 詔問狀，繪懼謝罪。

translations.literal: An edict demanded their account; Hui, in fear, apologized.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demanded their written response, and Hui, frightened, apologized.

sentences.zh: 摯奮曰：「為人臣豈可壓於權勢，使天子不知利害之實！

translations.literal: Zhi responded forcefully: "As a subject, how can one be cowed by power and influence, leaving the Son of Heaven ignorant of what is truly harmful or beneficial!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi responded forcefully: "As a subject, how can one be cowed by power and leave the Son of Heaven ignorant of what is truly harmful or beneficial!

sentences.zh: 」即條對所難，以伸其說。

translations.literal: " He then answered each objection point by point to state his case.
translations.idiomatic: " He then answered each objection point by point to make his case.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「臣待罪言責，採士民之說以聞於上，職也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your servant bears office charged with speaking out; to gather what gentry and commoners say and report it upward is my duty.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Your servant holds office charged with remonstrance; to gather what gentry and commoners say and report it upward is my duty.

sentences.zh: 今有司遽令分析，是使之較是非，爭勝負，交口相直，無乃辱陛下耳目之任哉！

translations.literal: Now the authorities hastily order us to debate in detail—making us compare right and wrong, contest victory and defeat, crossing words in mutual refutation—is this not an insult to Your Majesty's role as eyes and ears!
translations.idiomatic: Now the authorities hastily order us to debate in detail, forcing us to contest right and wrong and refute one another—is this not an insult to Your Majesty's role as eyes and ears!

sentences.zh: 所謂向背，則臣所向者義，所背者利；

translations.literal: What is called double allegiance—what I turn toward is righteousness, what I turn against is profit;
translations.idiomatic: As for what is called divided loyalty, what I turn toward is righteousness and what I turn against is profit;

sentences.zh: 所向者君父，所背者權臣。

translations.literal: What I turn toward is sovereign and father; what I turn against is the power-holding minister.
translations.idiomatic: What I turn toward is my sovereign and father; what I turn against is the minister who holds power.

sentences.zh: 願以臣章並司農奏宣示百官，考定當否。

translations.literal: I ask that my memorial and the Minister of Revenue's submission be displayed to all officials, to determine what is right.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that my memorial and the Minister of Revenue's submission be shown to all officials so they may judge what is right.

sentences.zh: 如臣言有取，幸早施行，若稍涉欺罔，甘就竄逐。

translations.literal: If anything in my words proves sound, I pray it be implemented early; if it involves the slightest deception, I willingly accept exile.
translations.idiomatic: If anything in my words proves sound, I pray it be put into effect at once; if it involves the slightest deception, I willingly accept exile.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: " No reply came.

sentences.zh: 摯明日覆上疏曰：

translations.literal: The next day Zhi submitted another memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhi submitted another memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 「陛下起居言動，躬蹈德禮，夙夜厲精，以親庶政。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty's daily conduct and speech embody virtue and ritual; morning and night you exert yourself to attend personally to all affairs of government.
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty's daily conduct and speech embody virtue and ritual; morning and night you exert yourself to attend personally to the affairs of government.

sentences.zh: 天下未至於安且治者，誰致之耶？

translations.literal: That the realm has not yet reached security and good order—who has brought this about?
translations.idiomatic: That the realm has not yet reached security and good order—who has brought this about?

sentences.zh: 陛下注意以望太平，而自以太平為己任，得君專政者是也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty fixes his attention on peace, yet those who hold the emperor's trust and monopolize government take peace as their own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty fixes his attention on peace, yet those who hold the emperor's trust and monopolize government take peace as their own charge.

sentences.zh: 二三年間，開闔動搖，舉天下無一物得安其所者。

translations.literal: In two or three years, openings and closings have been in flux; nothing under heaven has found a settled place.
translations.idiomatic: In two or three years everything has been thrown open and shut again; nothing under heaven has found a settled place.

sentences.zh: 蓋自青苗之議起，而天下始有聚斂之疑；

translations.literal: It began with debate over the Green Sprouts loans, and the realm first grew suspicious of exaction;
translations.idiomatic: It began with debate over the Green Sprouts loans, and the realm first grew suspicious of exaction;

sentences.zh: 青苗之議未允，而均輸之法行；

translations.literal: Before the Green Sprouts debate was settled, the equal-transport law was implemented;
translations.idiomatic: Before the Green Sprouts debate was settled, the equal-transport law was put into effect;

sentences.zh: 均輸之法方擾，而邊鄙之謀動；

translations.literal: While the equal-transport law still stirred turmoil, frontier schemes were set in motion;
translations.idiomatic: While the equal-transport law still stirred turmoil, frontier schemes were set in motion;

sentences.zh: 邊鄙之禍未艾，而助役之事興。

translations.literal: Before frontier calamities had ceased, the labor-assistance policy was launched.
translations.idiomatic: Before frontier calamities had ceased, the labor-assistance policy was launched.

sentences.zh: 至於求水利，行淤田，并州縣，興事起新，難以遍舉。

translations.literal: As for seeking waterworks, practicing silt-field reclamation, merging prefectures and counties, launching ventures and creating new projects—these cannot all be enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: As for seeking waterworks, practicing silt-field reclamation, merging prefectures and counties, and launching one new venture after another—these cannot all be enumerated.

sentences.zh: 其議財，則市井屠販之人，皆召至政事堂。

translations.literal: When finances were deliberated, butchers and peddlers from the market streets were all summoned to the Hall of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When finances were deliberated, butchers and peddlers from the market streets were all summoned to the Hall of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 其征利，則下至歷日，而官自鬻之。

translations.literal: When profit was pursued, it extended even to almanacs, which the government itself sold.
translations.idiomatic: When profit was pursued, it extended even to almanacs, which the government itself sold.

sentences.zh: 推此而往，不可究言。

translations.literal: Push this further and it defies full recounting.
translations.idiomatic: Push this further and it defies full recounting.

sentences.zh: 輕用名器，淆混賢否：忠厚老成者，擯之為無能；

translations.literal: Titles of office are lightly bestowed, blurring the worthy and unworthy: men of loyalty, honesty, and seasoned judgment are pushed aside as incompetent;
translations.idiomatic: Titles of office are lightly bestowed, blurring the worthy and unworthy: men of loyalty, honesty, and seasoned judgment are pushed aside as incompetent;

sentences.zh: 狹少儇辯者，取之為可用；

translations.literal: Narrow, young, glib debaters are taken as useful;
translations.idiomatic: Narrow-minded young glib debaters are taken as useful;

sentences.zh: 守道憂國者，謂之流俗；

translations.literal: Those who hold to the Way and worry for the state are called vulgar conformists;
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold to the Way and worry for the state are called vulgar conformists;

sentences.zh: 敗常害民者，謂之通變。

translations.literal: Those who ruin norms and harm the people are called flexible adaptors.
translations.idiomatic: Those who ruin norms and harm the people are called men of practical flexibility.

sentences.zh: 凡政府謀議經畫，除用進退，獨與一掾屬決之，然後落筆。

translations.literal: All government planning, appointments, promotions, and dismissals are decided alone with one clerk-assistant, and only then put to paper.
translations.idiomatic: All government planning, appointments, promotions, and dismissals are decided alone with one clerk-assistant, and only then put to paper.

sentences.zh: 同列預聞，反在其後。

translations.literal: Colleagues hear of them only afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues hear of them only afterward.

sentences.zh: 故奔走乞丐之人，其門如市。

translations.literal: Hence those who bustle and beg flock to his gate like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Hence those who bustle and beg flock to his gate like a market.

sentences.zh: 今西夏之款未入，反側之兵未安，三邊瘡痍，流潰未定。

translations.literal: Now the Western Xia have not yet submitted in good faith; mutinous troops are not yet pacified; the three frontiers are wounded and ulcerated, with flows of turmoil not yet stanched.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Western Xia have not yet submitted in good faith; mutinous troops are not yet pacified; the three frontiers are wounded and bleeding, and the turmoil has not yet been stanched.

sentences.zh: 河北大旱，諸路大水，民勞財乏，縣官減耗。

translations.literal: Hebei suffers great drought; many circuits face floods; the people are exhausted and funds depleted; government stores dwindle.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei suffers great drought; many circuits face floods; the people are exhausted and funds depleted; government stores dwindle.

sentences.zh: 聖上憂勤念治之時，而政事如此，皆大臣誤陛下，而大臣所用者，誤大臣也。」

translations.literal: At a time when the Sage Sovereign is diligent in his concern for governance, yet affairs stand thus—all this is the great ministers misleading Your Majesty; and what the great ministers employ misleads the great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: At a time when the Sage Sovereign is diligent in his concern for governance, yet affairs stand thus—all this is the great ministers misleading Your Majesty, and what the great ministers employ misleads the great ministers."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，安石欲竄之嶺外，神宗不聽，但謫監衡州鹽倉。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Anshi wished to banish him beyond the Lingnan; Emperor Shenzong did not assent, but demoted him to supervise the Hengzhou salt depot.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Anshi wished to banish him beyond the Lingnan, but Emperor Shenzong did not assent and demoted him instead to supervise the Hengzhou salt depot.

sentences.zh: 繪出知鄭州，琥亦落職。

translations.literal: Hui was sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou; Hu was also dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou, and Hu was also dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 摯乞詣鄆遷葬，然後奔赴貶所，許之。

translations.literal: Zhi requested permission to go to Yun to relocate a burial, then proceed to his place of exile; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi requested permission to go to Yun to relocate a burial and then proceed to his place of exile, and this was granted.

sentences.zh: 先是，倉吏與綱兵奸利相市，鹽中雜以偽惡，遠人未嘗食善鹽。

translations.literal: Earlier, depot clerks and transport soldiers traded corrupt profits; salt was adulterated with spurious and inferior matter; people from afar had never tasted good salt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, depot clerks and transport soldiers traded corrupt profits; salt was adulterated with spurious and inferior matter, and people from afar had never tasted good salt.

sentences.zh: 摯悉意核視，且儲其羡以為賞，弊減什七。

translations.literal: Zhi inspected it thoroughly, set aside surpluses as rewards, and reduced malfeasance by seven-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi inspected it thoroughly, set aside surpluses as rewards, and reduced malfeasance by seven-tenths.

sentences.zh: 父老目為「學士鹽」。

translations.literal: The elders called it "Scholar's Salt."
translations.idiomatic: The elders called it "Scholar's Salt."

sentences.zh: 久之，簽書南京判官。

translations.literal: After some time, he was appointed Acting Secretary and Judge of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, he was appointed Acting Secretary and Judge of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 會司農新令，盡斥賣天下祠廟，依坊場河渡法收淨利。

translations.literal: It happened that a new order from the Ministry of Revenue required the sale of all shrine temples nationwide, collecting net profits by the method used for licensed shops and ferry crossings.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that a new order from the Ministry of Revenue required the sale of all shrine temples nationwide, collecting net profits by the method used for licensed shops and ferry crossings.

sentences.zh: 南京閼伯廟歲錢四十六貫，微子廟十三貫。

translations.literal: In Nanjing, the Quebo Shrine brought in forty-six strings per year; the Weizi Shrine, thirteen strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanjing, the Quebo Shrine brought in forty-six strings per year and the Weizi Shrine thirteen strings.

sentences.zh: 摯歎曰：「一至於此！

translations.literal: Zhi sighed and said: "Things have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sighed and said: "Things have come to this!

sentences.zh: 」往見留守張方平曰：「獨不能為朝廷言之耶？

translations.literal: " He went to see the garrison commander Zhang Fangping and said: "Can you alone not speak to the court about this?
translations.idiomatic: " He went to see the garrison commander Zhang Fangping and said: "Can you not speak to the court about this?

sentences.zh: 」方平瞿然，託摯為奏曰：「閼伯遷商丘，主祀大火，火為國家盛德所乘，歷世尊為大祀。

translations.literal: " Fangping started, and entrusted Zhi to memorialize: "Quebo moved to Shangqiu and presides over the Sacrifice to the Great Fire; fire is borne upon by the state's abundant virtue and has always been honored as a great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " Fangping started, and entrusted Zhi to memorialize: "Quebo moved to Shangqiu and presides over the Sacrifice to the Great Fire; fire is borne upon by the state's abundant virtue and has always been honored as a great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 微子，宋始封之君，開國此地，本朝受命，建號所因。

translations.literal: Weizi was the first enfeoffed lord of Song; he founded the state on this ground; our dynasty received the Mandate and took its founding designation from here.
translations.idiomatic: Weizi was the first enfeoffed lord of Song; he founded the state on this ground; our dynasty received the Mandate and took its founding designation from here.

sentences.zh: 又有雙廟者，唐張巡、許遠孤城死賊，能捍大患。

translations.literal: There is also the Twin Shrine: Tang's Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan died defending a lone city against the rebels, able to ward off great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: There is also the Twin Shrine: Tang's Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan died defending a lone city against the rebels and were able to ward off great calamity.

sentences.zh: 今若令承買小人規利，冗褻瀆慢，何所不為，歲收微細，實損大體。

translations.literal: If petty profiteers are now allowed to lease these for gain, they will profane and insult without limit; the annual revenue is trifling, yet the harm to the larger principle is real.
translations.idiomatic: If petty profiteers are now allowed to lease these for gain, they will profane and insult without limit; the annual revenue is trifling, yet the harm to the larger principle is real.

sentences.zh: 慾望留此三廟，以慰邦人崇奉之意。

translations.literal: I wish to retain these three shrines, to satisfy the people's wish to honor them.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to retain these three shrines to satisfy the people's wish to honor them.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " This was approved.

sentences.zh: 又見《方平傳》。

translations.literal: This is also recorded in the Biography of Fangping.
translations.idiomatic: This is also recorded in the Biography of Fangping.

sentences.zh: 入同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: He entered service as Associate Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Associate Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，改集賢校理、知大宗正寺丞，為開封府推官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era, he was changed to Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and served as investigating officer of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era, he was made Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and served as investigating officer of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.

sentences.zh: 神宗開天章閣，議新官制，除至禮部郎中，曰：「此南宮舍人，非他曹比，無出劉摯者。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong opened the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and deliberated on a new bureaucratic system; when the appointment reached Director of the Ministry of Rites, he said: "This is a Southern Palace Academy drafter—not comparable to other offices; none surpasses Liu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong opened the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and deliberated on a new bureaucratic system; when the appointment reached Director of the Ministry of Rites, he said: "This is a Southern Palace Academy drafter—not comparable to other offices; none surpasses Liu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 」即命之。

translations.literal: " He was immediately appointed.
translations.idiomatic: " He was immediately appointed.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右司郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Director of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Director of the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 他日講筵進讀，至仁宗不避庚戌臨奠張士遜，侍讀曰：「國朝故事，多避國音。

translations.literal: Another day, during lectured readings at court, they came to Emperor Renzong's not avoiding the gengxu day when attending Zhang Shisun's funeral; the Reader said: "Our dynasty's custom often avoids the nation's homophonic taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Another day, during lectured readings at court, they came to Emperor Renzong's not avoiding the gengxu day when attending Zhang Shisun's funeral; the Reader said: "Our dynasty's custom often avoids the nation's homophonic taboos.

sentences.zh: 國朝角音，木也，故畏庚辛。

translations.literal: The nation's pitch is jue, which belongs to wood; hence we fear geng and xin.
translations.idiomatic: The nation's pitch is jue, which belongs to wood; hence we fear geng and xin.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗問：「果當避否？

translations.literal: " Emperor Zhezong asked: "Should it truly be avoided?
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Zhezong asked: "Should it truly be avoided?

sentences.zh: 」摯進曰：「陰陽拘忌，聖人不取，如正月祈穀必用上辛，此豈可改也？

translations.literal: " Zhi advanced and said: "The sages do not heed yin-yang superstitions; in the first month the grain prayer must use the upper xin day—could that be altered?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi advanced and said: "The sages do not heed yin-yang superstitions; in the first month the grain prayer must use the upper xin day—could that be altered?

sentences.zh: 漢章帝以反支日受章奏，唐太宗以辰日哭張公謹，仁宗不避庚戌日，皆陛下所宜取法。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhang of Han received memorials on fanzhi days; Emperor Taizong of Tang wept for Zhang Gongjin on a chen day; Renzong did not avoid the gengxu day—all models Your Majesty should follow.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang of Han received memorials on fanzhi days; Emperor Taizong of Tang wept for Zhang Gongjin on a chen day; Renzong did not avoid the gengxu day—all models Your Majesty should follow.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 摯又言：「諫官御史員缺未補，監察雖滿六員，專以察治官司公事，而不預言責。

translations.literal: Zhi also said: "Censor and remonstrance posts remain unfilled; though the six investigating censors are complete, they are devoted only to inspecting official business and do not share remonstrance duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi also said: "Censor and remonstrance posts remain unfilled; though the six investigating censors are complete, they are devoted only to inspecting official business and do not share remonstrance duties.

sentences.zh: 臣請增補臺諫，並許言事。

translations.literal: I ask to fill the bureau and remonstrance posts and allow them all to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to fill the bureau and remonstrance posts and allow them all to speak on affairs.

sentences.zh: 」時蔡確、章惇在政地，與司馬光不相能。

translations.literal: " At that time Cai Que and Zhang Dun held power and were at odds with Sima Guang.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Cai Que and Zhang Dun held power and were at odds with Sima Guang.

sentences.zh: 摯因久旱上言：「《洪範》：『庶徵肅，時雨若。

translations.literal: Because of prolonged drought, Zhi submitted: "The Hong Fan states: 'When the various signs are orderly, timely rain follows.'
translations.idiomatic: Because of prolonged drought, Zhi submitted: "The Hong Fan states: 'When the various signs are orderly, timely rain follows.'

sentences.zh: 』《五行傳》：『政緩則冬旱。

translations.literal: 'The Treatise on the Five Phases states: 'When government is lax, winter drought follows.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The Treatise on the Five Phases states: 'When government is lax, winter drought follows.'

sentences.zh: 』今廟堂大臣，情志乖暌，議政之際，依違排狠，語播於外，可謂不肅。

translations.literal: Today the ministers in the hall are at odds in mind and feeling; in deliberating policy they waver and clash harshly; their words spread abroad—this can be called disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: Today the ministers in the hall are at odds in mind and feeling; in deliberating policy they waver and clash harshly, and their words spread abroad—this can be called disorderly.

sentences.zh: 政令二三，舒緩不振。

translations.literal: Edicts come in twos and threes, slack and without vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts come in twos and threes, slack and without vigor.

sentences.zh: 比日日青無光，風霾昏曀，上天警告，皆非小變。

translations.literal: Lately the sun has shown no color; wind and haze have dimmed the sky—the warnings of heaven are no small change.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the sun has shown no color; wind and haze have dimmed the sky—the warnings of heaven are no small change.

sentences.zh: 願進忠良、通壅塞，以答天戒。」

translations.literal: I pray you advance the loyal and good, clear blockages, and answer heaven's admonition."
translations.idiomatic: I pray you advance the loyal and good, clear blockages, and answer heaven's admonition."

sentences.zh: 蔡確為山陵使，神宗靈駕發引前夕不入宿，摯劾之，不報。

translations.literal: Cai Que served as commissioner for the imperial mausoleum; on the eve before the late Shenzong's coffin procession departed, he did not stay overnight on duty; Zhi impeached him—no response.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que served as commissioner for the imperial mausoleum; on the eve before the late Shenzong's coffin procession departed, he did not stay overnight on duty. Zhi impeached him, but no response came.

sentences.zh: 及使回，既朝即視事，摯又奏確不引咎自劾。

translations.literal: When the commission returned, Que went straight from court audience to conduct business; Zhi again memorialized that Que had not accepted blame and impeached himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the commission returned, Que went straight from court audience to conduct business. Zhi again memorialized that Que had not accepted blame and impeached himself.

sentences.zh: 無何，確上表自陳，嘗請收拔當世之耆艾，以陪輔王室，蠲省有司之煩碎，以慰安民心。

translations.literal: Before long, Que submitted a self-account, claiming he had once asked to gather worthy elders of the age to assist the royal house and reduce the petty burdens of officials to comfort the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Que submitted a self-account, claiming he had once asked to gather worthy elders of the age to assist the royal house and reduce the petty burdens of officials to comfort the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 摯謂：「使確誠有是請，不言於先朝，為不忠之罪；

translations.literal: Zhi said: "If Que truly made such a request and did not speak of it under the previous reign, that is the crime of disloyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said: "If Que truly made such a request and did not speak of it under the previous reign, that is the crime of disloyalty;

sentences.zh: 言於今日，為取容之計。

translations.literal: To speak of it today is a calculation to curry favor.
translations.idiomatic: To speak of it today is a calculation to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 誠無是請，則欺君莫大於此。

translations.literal: If he truly made no such request, then no deception of the sovereign is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: If he truly made no such request, then no deception of the sovereign is greater than this.

sentences.zh: 」又疏確過惡大略有十，論章惇凶悍輕侻，無大臣體，皆罷去。

translations.literal: " He also listed roughly ten major faults of Que and argued that Zhang Dun was fierce, reckless, and flippant, lacking the bearing of a great minister—both should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " He also listed roughly ten major faults of Que and argued that Zhang Dun was fierce, reckless, and flippant, lacking the bearing of a great minister—both should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 初，神宗更新學制，養士以千數，有司立為約束，過於煩密。

translations.literal: Initially, Shenzong reformed the school system and supported scholars by the thousands; the authorities established regulations excessively detailed and burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Shenzong reformed the school system and supported scholars by the thousands; the authorities established regulations that were excessively detailed and burdensome.

sentences.zh: 摯上疏曰：

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhi submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 「學校為育材首善之地，教化所從出，非行法之所。

translations.literal: "Schools are the foremost ground for nurturing talent, the source from which instruction flows—not a place for enforcing penal law.
translations.idiomatic: "Schools are the foremost ground for nurturing talent, the source from which instruction flows—not a place for enforcing penal law.

sentences.zh: 雖群居眾聚，帥而齊之，不可無法，亦有禮義存焉。

translations.literal: Though many live together in groups and must be led to order and cannot be without rules, rites and propriety also dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Though many live together in groups and must be led to order and cannot be without rules, rites and propriety also dwell there.

sentences.zh: 先帝體道制法，超漢軼唐，養士之盛，比隆三代。

translations.literal: The late emperor embodied the Way and framed laws, surpassing Han and exceeding Tang; the flourishing of scholars rivaled the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor embodied the Way and framed laws, surpassing Han and exceeding Tang; the flourishing of scholars rivaled the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 然而比以太學屢起獄訟，有司緣此造為法禁，煩苛愈於治獄，條目多於防盜，上下疑貳，以求苟免。

translations.literal: Yet recently, because lawsuits have repeatedly arisen at the National University, officials have used this to fabricate prohibitions—more burdensome than governing prisons, more numerous in articles than guarding against theft; above and below are suspicious and doubtful, seeking only to escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recently, because lawsuits have repeatedly arisen at the National University, officials have used this to fabricate prohibitions—more burdensome than governing prisons, more numerous in articles than guarding against theft. Above and below are suspicious and doubtful, seeking only to escape blame.

sentences.zh: 甚可怪者，博士、諸生禁不相見，教諭無所施，質問無所從，月巡所隸之齋而已。

translations.literal: Most strange of all: doctors of learning and students are forbidden to meet; instruction cannot be applied; there is no channel for asking questions—they merely make monthly rounds of the dormitories under their charge.
translations.idiomatic: Most strange of all: doctors of learning and students are forbidden to meet; instruction cannot be applied; there is no channel for asking questions—they merely make monthly rounds of the dormitories under their charge.

sentences.zh: 齋舍既不一，隨經分隸，則又《易》博士兼巡《禮》齋，《詩》博士兼巡《書》齋，所至備禮請問，相與揖諾，亦或不交一言而退，以防私請，以杜賄賂。

translations.literal: Since dormitories differ and assignments follow the classics, a Doctor of Changes also inspects the Ritual dormitory, a Doctor of Odes also inspects the Documents dormitory; where they arrive they observe full ceremony and make inquiries, exchange bows and assents, yet sometimes exchange not a single word before departing—to guard against private requests and shut out bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Since dormitories differ and assignments follow the classics, a Doctor of Changes also inspects the Ritual dormitory and a Doctor of Odes also inspects the Documents dormitory. Where they arrive they observe full ceremony and make inquiries, exchange bows and assents, yet sometimes exchange not a single word before departing—to guard against private requests and shut out bribery.

sentences.zh: 學校如此，豈先帝所以造士之意哉？

translations.literal: When schools are thus, is this the late emperor's intent in nurturing scholars?
translations.idiomatic: When schools are thus, is this the late emperor's intent in nurturing scholars?

sentences.zh: 治天下者，遇人以君子、長者之道，則下必有君子、長者之行而應乎上。

translations.literal: One who governs all under Heaven, if one treats people with the way of the gentleman and the elder, then those below will surely have the conduct of gentlemen and elders in response to those above.
translations.idiomatic: Those who govern the realm, if they treat others with the courtesy due to gentlemen and elders, will surely find those below responding with the conduct of gentlemen and elders in turn.

sentences.zh: 若以小人、犬彘遇之，彼將以小人、犬彘自為，而況以此行於學校之間乎？

translations.literal: If one treats them as petty men or dogs and swine, they will conduct themselves as petty men and dogs—and how much more if this is practiced among the schools?
translations.idiomatic: If you treat them as petty men or dogs and swine, they will behave as petty men and dogs—and how much worse when such treatment is practiced in the schools?

sentences.zh: 願罷其制。」

translations.literal: I ask that this system be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this system be abolished."

sentences.zh: 又請雜用經義、詩賦取士，復賢良方正科，罷常平、免役，引朱光庭、王岩叟為言官。

translations.literal: He also asked to use a mixture of Classic exegesis and poetry and rhapsody to select scholars, to restore the Exemplary and Upright Worthies examination, to abolish the Ever-Normal Granary and corvée-exemption systems, and to appoint Zhu Guangting and Wang Yansou as remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to select officials through a mixture of Classic exegesis, poetry, and rhapsody; to restore the Exemplary and Upright Worthies examination; to abolish the Ever-Normal Granary and corvée-exemption schemes; and to bring in Zhu Guangting and Wang Yansou as remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 執憲數月，正色彈劾，多所貶黜，百僚敬憚，時人以比包拯、呂晦。

translations.literal: Holding the censorate for several months, he impeached with stern countenance, demoted many, and all the hundred officials respected and feared him; men of the time compared him to Bao Zheng and Lü Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the censorate for several months he impeached with stern countenance and demoted many officials; the whole bureaucracy respected and feared him, and contemporaries compared him to Bao Zheng and Lü Hui.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 摯上疏曰：「上之所好，下必有甚。

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial, saying: "What those above love, those below will surely surpass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi submitted a memorial, saying, "Whatever those above favor, those below will surely surpass.

sentences.zh: 朝廷意在總覈，下必有刻薄之行；

translations.literal: When the court's intent is comprehensive review, those below will surely have harsh conduct;
translations.idiomatic: When the court intends comprehensive audits, those below will surely behave harshly;

sentences.zh: 朝廷務在寬大，下必有苟簡之事。

translations.literal: When the court strives for leniency, those below will surely have perfunctory affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the court stresses clemency, those below will surely grow slack and perfunctory.

sentences.zh: 習俗懷利，迎意趨和，所為近似，而非上之意本然也。

translations.literal: Custom harbors profit; men read intent and rush to accord—what they do resembles the aim, yet is not what those above truly mean.
translations.idiomatic: People bent on gain read the mood and rush to conform; their actions merely resemble the aim of policy and do not reflect what those above truly intend.

sentences.zh: 今因革之政本殊，而觀望之俗故在。

translations.literal: Now the policies of repeal and reform are fundamentally different, yet the custom of watching and waiting remains as before.
translations.idiomatic: The policies of repeal and reform are now fundamentally different, yet the old habit of watching and waiting endures.

sentences.zh: 昨差役初行，監司已有迎合爭先，不校利害，一概定差，一路為之騷動者。

translations.literal: When the corvée system was first implemented, circuit intendant-commissioners were already vying to ingratiate themselves, reckoning neither benefit nor harm, fixing assignments across the board—an entire circuit was thrown into uproar for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the corvée system was first introduced, circuit commissioners were already vying to ingratiate themselves, heedless of benefit or harm, fixing assignments wholesale and throwing entire circuits into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 朝廷察其如此，固已黜之矣。

translations.literal: The court, seeing that it was so, had already demoted them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this, the court had already dismissed them from office.

sentences.zh: 以是觀之，大約類此。

translations.literal: Viewing it by this example, it is largely of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by this example, the pattern is much the same elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 向來黜責數人者，皆以非法掊克，市進害民，然非欲使之漫不省事。

translations.literal: Those recently demoted and rebuked had all, through unlawful extortion and buying advancement while harming the people, deserved punishment—yet the intent was not to make them care nothing and neglect their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Those recently dismissed had all extorted unlawfully, buying advancement at the people's expense—but the purpose was not to leave them indifferent and neglectful of their duties.

sentences.zh: 昧者不達，矯枉過正，顧可不為之禁哉？

translations.literal: The obtuse do not understand and overcorrect past wrongs—surely this must be forbidden?
translations.idiomatic: The dull-witted fail to understand and overcorrect past abuses—is this not something that must be stopped?

sentences.zh: 請立監司考績之制。」

translations.literal: I ask that a system for evaluating the performance of circuit intendant-commissioners be established."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a system for evaluating circuit commissioners be established."

sentences.zh: 拜尚書右丞，連進左丞、中書侍郎，遷門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was successively promoted to Left Vice Director and Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and was transferred to Vice Minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then successively Left Vice Director and Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and was transferred to Vice Minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 胡宗愈除右丞，諫議大夫王覿疏其非是，宣仁后怒，將加深譴。

translations.literal: When Hu Zongyu was appointed Right Vice Director, Remonstrance Grandee Wang Di memorialized that it was improper; Empress Dowager Xuanren was angry and was about to impose deeper punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Zongyu was appointed Right Vice Director, Remonstrance Grandee Wang Di memorialized against the appointment; Empress Dowager Xuanren grew angry and was ready to punish him severely.

sentences.zh: 摯開救甚力，簾中厲聲曰：「若有人以門下侍郎為奸邪，甘受之否？

translations.literal: Zhi intervened to rescue him with great force; from behind the curtain a stern voice said: "If someone calls the Vice Minister of the Chancellery treacherous and wicked, will you willingly accept it?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi interceded for him vigorously. From behind the curtain came a stern voice: "If someone accuses the Vice Minister of the Chancellery of treachery, would you willingly accept that?

sentences.zh: 」摯曰：「陛下審察毀譽每如此，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Your Majesty scrutinizes slander and praise in this way—the realm is greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied, "When Your Majesty scrutinizes slander and praise this closely, the realm is greatly fortunate!

sentences.zh: 然願顧大體，宗愈進用，自有公議，必致貶諫官而後進，恐宗愈亦所未安。

translations.literal: Yet I wish that the broader situation be considered: if Zongyu is advanced, there will naturally be public opinion; if censure of the remonstrating official must precede advancement, I fear Zongyu too will feel ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hope Your Majesty will consider the larger situation. Zongyu's advancement would naturally provoke public debate; to demote the remonstrating official before promoting him would leave even Zongyu ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 」宣仁后意解，覿得補郡守。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren's mood relaxed, and Di was appointed as a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren's anger eased, and Wang Di was appointed to a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 摯與同列奏事論人才，摯曰：「人才難得，能否不一。

translations.literal: Zhi with his colleagues presented matters to the throne and discussed talent; Zhi said: "Talent is hard to obtain; capacity and incapacity are not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: While presenting business with his colleagues, Zhi spoke on the question of talent: "Good men are hard to find; capacities vary.

sentences.zh: 性忠實而才識有餘，上也；

translations.literal: Of loyal and faithful nature with talent and insight to spare—the highest grade;
translations.idiomatic: Men loyal at heart with ample talent and judgment—the best;

sentences.zh: 才識不逮而忠實有餘，次也；

translations.literal: Talent and insight not reaching yet loyal and faithful to spare—the second;
translations.idiomatic: Men whose talent falls short but whose loyalty is ample—the next;

sentences.zh: 有才而難保，可藉以集事，又其次也。

translations.literal: Having talent yet hard to guarantee, yet usable to gather affairs accomplished—the grade below that again.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent who cannot be fully trusted, yet can still be used to get things done—the grade below that.

sentences.zh: 懷邪觀望，隨時勢改變，此小人也，終不可用。

translations.literal: Those harboring wickedness and watching the moment, changing with the trends—these are petty men and ultimately cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: Men who harbor wickedness, watch the wind, and shift with the times—these are petty men and should never be employed.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗及宣仁后曰：「卿常能如此用人，國家何憂！

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong and Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "If you always use men thus, what worry has the state!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong and Empress Dowager Xuanren said, "If you always appoint men this wisely, what need has the state to worry!

sentences.zh: 」六年，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Right Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Right Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 摯性峭直，有氣節，通達明銳，觸機輒發，不為利怵威誘。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was stern and upright, with moral fiber; penetrating and keen, he would act whenever provoked, and was neither coaxed by profit nor swayed by intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was stern and upright by nature, a man of integrity—perceptive, sharp, and quick to act when provoked, unmoved by profit or intimidation.

sentences.zh: 自初輔政至為相，修嚴憲法，辨白邪正，專以人物處心，孤立一意，不受謁請。

translations.literal: From first assisting in government to becoming chief minister, he tightened and enforced the laws, distinguished the wicked from the upright, devoted his heart solely to men and affairs, stood alone in one intent, and did not accept private petitions.
translations.idiomatic: From his first entry into government through his years as chief minister, he rigorously enforced the law, distinguished wicked from upright, judged men and affairs on their merits alone, stood apart in purpose, and accepted no private solicitations.

sentences.zh: 子弟親戚入官，皆令赴銓部以格調選，未嘗以干朝廷。

translations.literal: Sons, brothers, and kinsmen entering office were all sent to the Board of Appointments to be selected by regulation—never through appeals to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When sons, brothers, and kinsmen sought office, he made them go through the Board of Appointments and compete under the regular rules, never using his influence at court.

sentences.zh: 與呂大防同位，國家大事，多決於大防，惟進退士大夫，實執其柄。

translations.literal: Sharing rank with Lü Dafang, on great affairs of state decisions largely rested with Dafang; only in advancing and dismissing scholar-officials did he actually hold the power.
translations.idiomatic: Though he shared power with Lü Dafang, most major affairs were decided by Dafang; only in advancing and dismissing scholar-officials did Zhi truly hold the reins.

sentences.zh: 然持心少恕，勇於去惡，竟為朋讒奇中。

translations.literal: Yet he held his heart with little forgiveness, was bold in removing the wicked, and in the end was strangely struck by factional slander.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was sparing in mercy, bold in removing evil, and in the end was felled by a strange stroke of factional slander.

sentences.zh: 先是，邢恕謫官永州，以書抵摯。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xing Shu was demoted to an office in Yongzhou and sent a letter to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xing Shu had been demoted to Yongzhou and wrote to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 摯故與恕善，答其書，有「永州佳處，第往以俟休復」之語。

translations.literal: Zhi had long been on good terms with Shu and replied to his letter with the words: "Yongzhou has fine places—just go and wait for restoration after rest."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had long been friendly with Shu and replied with words to the effect: "Yongzhou has its charms—simply go there and wait until restoration after rest."

sentences.zh: 排岸官茹東濟，傾險人也，有求於摯，不得，見其書，陰錄以示御史中丞鄭雍、侍御史楊畏。

translations.literal: The bank commissioner Ru Dongji was a treacherous man; having made requests of Zhi and failed, he saw his letter, secretly copied it, and showed it to Vice Censor-in-Chief Zheng Yong and Attending Censor Yang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Dongji, a bank commissioner of treacherous character, had sought favors from Zhi and been refused; seeing the letter, he secretly copied it and showed it to Vice Censor-in-Chief Zheng Yong and Attending Censor Yang Wei.

sentences.zh: 二人方交章擊摯，遂箋釋其語上之，曰：「『休復』者，語出《周易》，『以俟休復』者，俟他日太皇太后復子明辟也。

translations.literal: The two were just then submitting memorial after memorial attacking Zhi; they annotated and explained his words and reported upward, saying: "'Restoration after rest'—the phrase comes from the Book of Changes; 'waiting for restoration after rest' means waiting for the day when the Empress Dowager restores the son's enlightened rule.
translations.idiomatic: The two were already submitting memorial upon memorial attacking Zhi. They annotated his words and reported to the throne: "'Restoration after rest' is a phrase from the Book of Changes; 'waiting for restoration after rest' means waiting for the Empress Dowager one day to restore the Emperor to enlightened rule.

sentences.zh: 」又章惇諸子故與摯之子游，摯亦間與之接。

translations.literal: Also, Zhang Dun's sons had formerly associated with Zhi's son for study; Zhi also occasionally received them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun's sons had also studied with Zhi's son, and Zhi occasionally received them as well.

sentences.zh: 雍、畏謂延見接納，為牢籠之計，以冀後福。

translations.literal: Yong and Wei said that extending audiences and accepting association was a scheme of entrapment, hoping for future blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Wei claimed these audiences and associations were a scheme to cultivate allies in hope of future advantage.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后於是面喻摯曰：「言者謂卿交通匪人，為異日地，卿當一心王室。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren then personally admonished Zhi face to face, saying: "The speakers say you associate with bad men and prepare ground for another day—you must devote yourself wholeheartedly to the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren then spoke to Zhi directly: "Critics say you consort with disreputable men and are laying groundwork for the future. You must give your whole heart to the throne.

sentences.zh: 若章惇者，雖以宰相處之，未必樂也。

translations.literal: One like Zhang Dun—even placed as chief minister—would perhaps not be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Someone like Zhang Dun—even if placed in the position of chief minister—would not necessarily be content.

sentences.zh: 」摯皇懼退，上章自辨，執政亦為之言。

translations.literal: Zhi, in great alarm, withdrew and submitted a memorial in self-defense; the chief ministers also spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi withdrew in great alarm and submitted a memorial in self-defense; the chief ministers also spoke on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后曰：「垂簾之初，摯排斥奸邪，實為忠直。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "At the beginning of the regency, Zhi repelled the wicked and was truly loyal and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren said, "At the start of the regency, Zhi drove out wicked men and was truly loyal and upright.

sentences.zh: 但此二事，非所當為也。

translations.literal: But these two matters were not what should have been done.
translations.idiomatic: But in these two matters he did what ought not to have been done.

sentences.zh: 」以觀文殿學士罷知鄆州。

translations.literal: He was dismissed as Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literary Works and made prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his post as Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literary Works and sent out as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中朱光庭駁云：「摯忠義自奮，朝廷擢之大位，一旦以疑而罷，天下不見其過。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretariat Drafter Zhu Guangting rebutted, saying: "Zhi rose by his own loyalty and righteousness; the court elevated him to great rank, yet suddenly dismissed him on suspicion—the realm does not see his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretariat Drafter Zhu Guangting objected: "Zhi rose through his own loyalty; the court elevated him to the highest rank, yet now dismisses him on mere suspicion—the realm sees no fault in him.

sentences.zh: 」光庭亦罷。

translations.literal: Guangting too was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙大名，又為雍等所遏，徙知青州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Daming; again blocked by Yong and the others, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Daming; obstructed again by Zheng Yong and others, he was moved to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，來之邵、周秩論摯變法、棄地罪，奪職知黃州，再貶光祿卿，分司南京，蘄州居住。

translations.literal: At the start of Shaosheng, Lai Zhishao and Zhou Zhi indicted Zhi for the crimes of altering the laws and abandoning territory; his office was stripped and he was made prefect of Huangzhou, demoted again to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, assigned to the Southern Capital as detached service, and ordered to reside in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shaosheng era, Lai Zhishao and Zhou Zhi indicted Zhi for altering the reforms and abandoning territory; he was stripped of office and made prefect of Huangzhou, then demoted again to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with detached service at the Southern Capital and ordered to reside at Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 將行，語諸子曰：「上用章惇，吾且得罪。

translations.literal: About to depart, he told his sons: "The sovereign employs Zhang Dun—I shall soon meet with punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he told his sons, "The Emperor is employing Zhang Dun—I am sure to be punished.

sentences.zh: 若惇顧國事，不遷怒百姓，但責吾曹，死無所恨。

translations.literal: If Dun considers the affairs of state, does not shift anger onto the common people, but holds only us accountable, death would hold no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If Dun keeps the nation's interests in mind, does not vent his anger on the people, and holds only us accountable, I shall die without regret.

sentences.zh: 正慮意在報復，法令益峻，奈天下何！

translations.literal: What I truly fear is that his intent is revenge, laws and edicts grow ever harsher—what is to become of all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: What I truly fear is that he intends revenge, that laws grow ever harsher—what will become of the realm!

sentences.zh: 」憂形於色，無一言及遷謫意。

translations.literal: Worry showed on his face; not a word touched on the thought of banishment and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Worry showed plainly on his face; he spoke not a word about his own exile.

sentences.zh: 四年，陷邢恕之謗，貶鼎州團練副使，新州安置。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, falling into Xing Shu's slander, he was demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Dingzhou and ordered to settle in Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was caught up in Xing Shu's calumny, demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Dingzhou, and ordered to settle at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 惟一子從。

translations.literal: Only one son accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: Only one son went with him.

sentences.zh: 家人涕泣願侍，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Family members wept and wished to attend him; he would not listen to any.
translations.idiomatic: His family wept and begged to accompany him, but he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 至數月，以疾卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: After several months he died of illness, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he died of illness, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 初，摯與呂大防為相，文及甫居喪，在洛怨望，服除，恐不得京官，抵書邢恕曰：「改月遂除，入朝之計未可必。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhi and Lü Dafang were chief ministers, Wen Jifu was in mourning; in Luoyang he nursed resentment; when mourning ended he feared he would not obtain a capital appointment and sent a letter to Xing Shu saying: "Next month the appointment should be made, but the plan to enter court is not yet certain.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Zhi and Lü Dafang were chief ministers, Wen Jifu was in mourning in Luoyang, nursing resentment. When his mourning ended he feared he would not win a capital appointment and wrote to Xing Shu: "The appointment should come next month, but whether I can enter court is far from certain.

sentences.zh: 當塗猜怨於鷹揚者益深，其徒實繁。

translations.literal: Those in power suspect and resent the hawk-banners ever more deeply; their faction is truly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power grow ever more suspicious and resentful of the hawk faction; their following is truly large.

sentences.zh: 司馬昭之心，路人所知也，濟之以『粉昆』，必欲以眇躬為甘心快意之地，可為寒心。

translations.literal: Sima Zhao's heart is known to every passerby; aided by 'Fen Kun,' they must wish to make my slight person the ground of their sweet satisfaction—it is chilling to the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao's heart is plain to every passerby. With 'Fen Kun' at their side they surely mean to make me the object of their malice—it is enough to chill the heart.

sentences.zh: 」其謂司馬昭者，指呂大防獨當國久；

translations.literal: What he meant by Sima Zhao was Lü Dafang's long tenure holding the state alone;
translations.idiomatic: By Sima Zhao he meant Lü Dafang's long tenure as sole holder of power;

sentences.zh: 『粉昆』者，世以駙馬都尉為『粉侯』，韓嘉彥尚主，以兄忠彥為『粉昆』也。

translations.literal: 'Fen Kun': the age took Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant as 'Fen Hou'; Han Jiayan married an imperial princess and called his elder brother Zhongyan 'Fen Kun.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Fen Kun': the age nicknamed imperial sons-in-law 'Fen Marquis'; Han Jiayan had married an imperial princess and called his elder brother Zhongyan 'Fen Kun.'

sentences.zh: 恕以書示蔡碩、蔡渭，渭上書訟摯及大防等十餘人陷其父確，謀危宗社，引及甫書為證。

translations.literal: Shu showed the letter to Cai Shuo and Cai Wei; Wei submitted a memorial accusing Zhi and Dafang and more than ten others of framing his father Que, plotting to endanger the dynasty, citing Jifu's letter as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Shu showed the letter to Cai Shuo and Cai Wei. Wei submitted a memorial accusing Zhi, Dafang, and more than a dozen others of framing his father Cai Que and plotting against the dynasty, citing Jifu's letter as evidence.

sentences.zh: 時章惇、蔡卞誣造元祐諸人事不已，因是欲殺摯及梁燾、王岩叟等。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Dun and Cai Bian ceaselessly fabricated matters against the Yuanyou figures; because of this they wished to put Zhi and Liang Tao and Wang Yansou to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun and Cai Bian were then ceaselessly fabricating charges against the Yuanyou faction; using this affair they sought to execute Zhi, Liang Tao, Wang Yansou, and others.

sentences.zh: 以為摯有廢立之意，遂起同文館獄，用蔡京、安惇雜治，逮問及甫。

translations.literal: Believing Zhi had intent to depose and establish, they raised the Tongwen Guan case, using Cai Jing and An Dun jointly to investigate, and seized and questioned Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Zhi harbored designs to depose and enthrone, they opened the Tongwen Guan investigation, assigning Cai Jing and An Dun jointly to conduct it, and seized Wen Jifu for questioning.

sentences.zh: 及甫元祐末德大防除權侍郎，又忠彥雖罷，哲宗眷之未衰，乃託其亡父嘗說司馬昭指劉摯，「粉」謂王岩叟面白如粉，「昆」謂梁燾字況之，「況」猶「兄」也。
