translations.literal: Jifu: at the end of Yuanyou he had opposed Dafang's appointment as Acting Vice Minister of the Secretariat; further, though Zhongyan had been dismissed, Emperor Zhezong's favor had not waned—so he claimed his deceased father had once said Sima Zhao pointed to Liu Zhi; 'Fen' meant Wang Yansou with a face white as powder, 'Kun' meant Liang Tao whose courtesy name was Kuangzhi—'Kuang' being like 'elder brother.'
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanyou, Wen Jifu had opposed Dafang's appointment as Acting Vice Minister of the Secretariat; though Zhongyan had been dismissed, Emperor Zhezong's favor had not yet faded. Jifu therefore claimed his late father had once explained that Sima Zhao referred to Liu Zhi: 'Fen' meant Wang Yansou, whose face was white as powder, and 'Kun' meant Liang Tao, courtesy name Kuangzhi—'Kuang' being homophonous with 'elder brother.'

sentences.zh: 又問實狀，但云：「疑其事勢如此。

translations.literal: Questioning him further about the facts, he only said: "I suspect the situation was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed further about the facts, he could only say, "I suspect the affair was of this nature.

sentences.zh: 」會摯卒，京奏不及考驗，遂免其子官，與家屬徙英州，凡三年，死於瘴者十人。

translations.literal: Just then Zhi died; Cai Jing reported there was no time for examination; they thereupon stripped his son of office, and with family members were exiled to Yingzhou; in all three years ten died in the miasma.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zhi died. Cai Jing reported that there was no time for further examination; Zhi's son was stripped of office and the family was exiled to Yingzhou. Over three years ten died of the miasma.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，詔反其家屬，用子跂請，得歸葬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, an edict recalled his family members; at his son Qi's request, they were granted burial at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, an edict recalled Zhi's family; at the request of his son Qi, the body was permitted burial at home.

sentences.zh: 跂又伏闕訴及甫之誣，遂貶及甫並渭於湖外，復摯中大夫。

translations.literal: Qi also prostrated at the palace gate to accuse Jifu of fabrication; thereupon Jifu and Wei were demoted beyond the lakes, and Zhi's rank of Grand Master of Palace Attendance was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Qi also prostrated himself at the palace gate to denounce Jifu's false charges; Jifu and Wei were then demoted beyond the lakes, and Zhi's rank of Grand Master of Palace Attendance was restored.

sentences.zh: 蔡京為相，降朝散大夫。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing became chief minister, the rank was lowered to Grand Master for Spread Morning.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing became chief minister, the posthumous rank was reduced to Grand Master for Spreading Dawn.

sentences.zh: 後又復觀文殿大學士、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Later the titles Academician Exemplar of the Hall for Viewing Literary Works and Grand Master of Palace Attendance were again restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later his titles of Academician Exemplar of the Hall for Viewing Literary Works and Grand Master of Palace Attendance were restored.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，贈少師，諡曰「忠肅」。

translations.literal: At the start of Shaoxing, he was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor; his posthumous title was Zhongsu ("Loyal and Solemn").
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shaoxing era he was posthumously honored as Junior Preceptor, with the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 摯嗜書，自幼至老，未嘗釋卷。

translations.literal: Zhi loved books; from youth to old age he never put down the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi loved books; from youth to old age he never set a text aside.

sentences.zh: 家藏書多自讎校，得善本或手抄錄，孜孜無倦。

translations.literal: Many books in his family collection he personally collated; obtaining fine editions he sometimes copied by hand, diligently without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He personally collated much of his family library; when he found a fine edition he would sometimes copy it by hand, working tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 少好《禮》學，其究《三禮》，視諸經尤粹。

translations.literal: In youth he loved Ritual learning; his investigation of the Three Rites he regarded as especially pure among all the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved Ritual studies; his mastery of the Three Rites he regarded as especially refined among the Classics.

sentences.zh: 晚好《春秋》，考諸儒異同，辨其得失，通聖人經意為多。

translations.literal: In old age he loved the Spring and Autumn Annals, examined the differences among the Ru, distinguished their gains and losses—mostly penetrating the sage's Classic intent.
translations.idiomatic: In later life he turned to the Spring and Autumn Annals, compared the divergences among the Ru scholars, weighed their strengths and weaknesses, and largely penetrated the sage's intent.

sentences.zh: 其教子孫，先行實，後文藝。

translations.literal: In teaching sons and grandchildren, he put conduct first and literary arts after.
translations.idiomatic: In instructing his sons and grandchildren, he put character first and literary accomplishment second.

sentences.zh: 每曰：「士當以器識為先，一號為文人，無足觀矣。」

translations.literal: He often said: "A scholar should take breadth of mind and discernment first; once labeled a man of letters, there is nothing worth looking at."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "A scholar should value breadth of mind and judgment above all; once a man is known merely as a man of letters, there is little worth admiring in him."

sentences.zh: 跂能為文章，遭黨事，為官拓落，家居避禍，以壽終。

translations.literal: Qi could compose literary works; caught up in factional affairs, his official career was desolate; he lived at home avoiding calamity and died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was a capable writer; caught in the factional persecutions, his official career foundered; he lived at home avoiding further harm and died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 蘇頌，字子容，泉州南安人。

translations.literal: Su Song, courtesy name Zirong, was a man of Nan'an in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Song, whose courtesy name was Zirong, was a native of Nan'an in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父紳，葬潤州丹陽，因徙居之。

translations.literal: His father Shen was buried in Danyang in Runzhou; the family therefore moved and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen was buried at Danyang in Runzhou, and the family moved there to settle.

sentences.zh: 第進士，歷宿州觀察推官、知江寧縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served successively as Investigating Secretary of Suzhou Observation Commission and Magistrate of Jiangning County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served successively as Investigating Secretary under the Suzhou observation commission and as magistrate of Jiangning County.

sentences.zh: 時建業承李氏後，稅賦圖籍，一皆無藝，每發斂，高下出吏手。

translations.literal: At the time Jianye had inherited the situation after the Li dynasty of Southern Tang; tax and levy registers lacked all method—each time revenues were assessed, high and low came from officials' hands.
translations.idiomatic: Jianye at the time still bore the legacy of the Li dynasty of Southern Tang; tax registers were in complete disorder, and assessments were made entirely at clerks' discretion.

sentences.zh: 頌因治訊他事，互問民鄰里丁產，識其詳。

translations.literal: Song, while investigating and examining other matters, cross-questioned the people about households and property in the neighborhoods and came to know the details.
translations.idiomatic: While investigating other cases, Song cross-examined people about neighboring households and property, learning the details by heart.

sentences.zh: 及定戶籍，民或自占不悉，頌警之曰：「汝有某丁某產，何不言？

translations.literal: When household registers were fixed, sometimes people did not fully declare themselves; Song warned them, saying: "You have so many males and so much property—why not speak of it?
translations.idiomatic: When household registers were being compiled, some people failed to declare everything. Song warned them: "You have such-and-such males and such-and-such property—why do you not declare them?

sentences.zh: 」民駭懼，皆不敢隱，遂剗剔夙蠹，成賦一邑，簡而易行，諸令視以為法，至領某民拜庭下以謝。

translations.literal: The people were terrified and none dared conceal; thus long-standing corruption was cut away and tax assessment for the whole county was completed—simple and easy to implement. All magistrates took it as model; some leaders of communities bowed in the court hall in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the people dared conceal nothing. He cut away long-standing abuses and completed tax assessment for the entire county in a simple, workable form. Other magistrates took it as their model, and some community leaders came to bow in thanks at his court.

sentences.zh: 凡民有忿爭，頌喻以鄉黨宜相親善，若以小忿而失歡心，一旦緩急，將何賴焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the people had quarrels, Song admonished them that neighbors in the community should be mutually kind; if through small anger one loses good will, once urgency comes, on whom will one rely?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever neighbors quarreled, Song urged them that people of the same community ought to treat one another kindly; if a small grudge destroyed goodwill, whom could they rely on in a crisis?

sentences.zh: 民往往謝去，或半途思其言而止。

translations.literal: The people often took their leave in thanks, or halfway home reflected on his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: People often went away appeased, or stopped halfway home to reconsider his words and abandon their quarrel.

sentences.zh: 時監司王鼎、王綽、楊紘於部吏少許可，及觀頌施設，則曰：「非吾所及也。」

translations.literal: At the time Supervisory commissioners Wang Ding, Wang Chuo, and Yang Hong rarely approved subordinate officials; when they observed Song's measures they said: "This is beyond what we could achieve."
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory commissioners Wang Ding, Wang Chuo, and Yang Hong rarely praised subordinates, but observing Song's work they said, "This is beyond our reach."

sentences.zh: 調南京留守推官，留守歐陽修委以政，曰：「子容處事精審，一經閱覽，則修不復省矣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Investigating Secretary of the Nanjing garrison command; Garrison Commander Ouyang Xiu entrusted him with governance, saying: "Zirong handles affairs with meticulous care; once I have read them through, I need look no more.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to investigating secretary under the Nanjing garrison commander. Garrison Commander Ouyang Xiu entrusted him with administrative affairs, saying, "Zirong handles matters with meticulous care; once I have reviewed his work, I need look at it no further.

sentences.zh: 」時杜衍老居睢陽，見頌，深器之，曰：「如君，真所謂不可得而親疏者。

translations.literal: At the time Du Yan in old age resided at Suiyang; seeing Song, he greatly valued him and said: "One like you is truly what they call impossible to draw close or keep distant.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan was then living in retirement at Suiyang. Meeting Song, he deeply admired him and said, "A man like you is truly what they mean by one who cannot be won by intimacy or alienated by distance.

sentences.zh: 」衍又自謂平生人罕見其用心處，遂自小官以至為侍從、宰相所以施設出處，悉以語頌，曰：「以子相知，且知子異日必為此官，老夫非以自矜也。

translations.literal: Yan also said that in his lifetime few had seen where his mind was applied; from minor office through attendant and chief minister, how he acted, advanced, and withdrew—he told Song all of it, saying: "Because we know each other, and I know you will one day surely hold this office—I do not speak thus to boast.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also said that in his lifetime few had seen the full working of his mind. From his days in minor office through his service as court attendant and chief minister—all his principles of action, advancement, and withdrawal—he confided entirely to Song, saying, "Because I know you, and because I know you will one day hold such office, I tell you this—not to boast of myself.

sentences.zh: 」故頌後歷政，略似衍云。

translations.literal: Therefore when Song later administered government, it broadly resembled Yan's ways.
translations.idiomatic: Song's later career in government broadly resembled Du Yan's in this respect.

sentences.zh: 皇祐五年，召試館閣校勘，同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangyou, he was summoned for the Library examination as collator and served concurrently as Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huangyou he was summoned for the library examination as collator and was appointed associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 至和中，文彥博為相，請建家廟，事下太常。

translations.literal: In the Zhehe era, Wen Yanbo as chief minister requested to establish a family temple; the matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhehe era, Chief Minister Wen Yanbo petitioned to establish a family temple; the matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 頌議以為：「禮，大夫士有田則祭，無田則薦，是有土者乃為廟祭也。

translations.literal: Song submitted his opinion: "By ritual, grandees and officers with fiefs sacrifice; without fiefs they offer seasonal offerings—only those who hold land perform ancestral temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Song argued: "By ritual law, grandees and officers with landholdings sacrifice in temples; without land they offer seasonal presentations—only those with fiefs perform temple worship.

sentences.zh: 有田則有爵，無土無爵，則子孫無以繼承宗祀，是有廟者止於其躬，子孫無爵，祭乃廢也。

translations.literal: With fief there is rank; without land and without rank, then descendants have no means to inherit ancestral sacrifice—thus those with temples extend only to their own person; descendants without rank, and sacrifice is abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Land implies rank; without land and without rank, descendants have no means to maintain ancestral worship—so the right to a family temple ends with the man himself; when descendants hold no rank, sacrifice ceases.

sentences.zh: 若參合古今之制，依約封爵之令，為之等差，錫以土田，然後廟制可議。

translations.literal: If one consults and combines ancient and modern institutions, in accordance with the edicts on enfeoffment and titles establishes gradations of distinction, and bestows land and fields, then temple regulations may be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Only if institutions past and present are harmonized, enfeoffment edicts are applied with proper gradations, and land is granted accordingly can the question of family temples be seriously entertained.

sentences.zh: 若猶未也，即請考案唐賢寢堂祠饗儀，止用燕器常食而已。」

translations.literal: If still not so, then please investigate and examine the Tang worthy's resting-hall sacrifice rites, using only banquet vessels and ordinary food."
translations.idiomatic: If that cannot be done, then consult the Tang practice of worship in the resting hall, limiting offerings to banquet vessels and ordinary fare."

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，詔禮院議立故郭皇后神御殿於景靈宮，頌謂：「敕書云：『向因忿鬱，偶失謙恭』，此則無可廢之事。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, an edict ordered the Board of Rites to discuss establishing a Spirit Hall for the late Empress Guo at Jingling Palace. Song said: "The imperial edict states: 'Previously, owing to resentment and depression, I occasionally failed in humility'—this is a matter that cannot be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou era, the court ordered the Board of Rites to consider establishing a Spirit Hall for the late Empress Guo at Jingling Palace. Song argued: "The imperial edict reads, 'Previously, in a fit of anger and vexation, I failed in humility'—and that is something that cannot simply be undone.

sentences.zh: 又云：『朕念其自歷長秋，僅周一紀，逮事先后，祗奉寢園』，此則有不當廢之悔。

translations.literal: It also states: 'I recall that she held the office of Changqiu for nearly a full cycle, served the former and later empresses, and reverently attended the imperial tombs'—this expresses regret that she ought not to have been deposed.
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 'I remember that she held the empress's seat for nearly twelve years, served both the former and the reigning empress, and dutifully tended the imperial tombs'—which shows remorse that her deposition was wrong.

sentences.zh: 又云：『可追復皇后，其祔廟諡冊並停。

translations.literal: It also states: 'She may be posthumously restored as empress; her temple enshrinement and posthumous title documents are both suspended.
translations.idiomatic: It further states, 'She may be posthumously restored as empress, but her enshrinement in the ancestral temple and her posthumous title documents are both suspended.

sentences.zh: 』此則有合祔廟及諡冊之義。

translations.literal: '" This carries the meaning of proper temple enshrinement and posthumous title documents.
translations.idiomatic: '" That wording still implies the right to temple enshrinement and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 請祔郭皇后於后廟，以成追復之道。

translations.literal: I request that Empress Guo be enshrined in the empresses' temple, to complete the path of posthumous restoration.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ask that Empress Guo be enshrined in the empresses' temple, so that the restoration may be fully accomplished.

sentences.zh: 」眾論未定，宰相曾公亮問曰：「郭后，上元妃，若祔廟，則事體重矣。

translations.literal: " Opinion remained unsettled. Chief Minister Zeng Gongliang asked: "Empress Guo was the emperor's primary consort before his enthronement; if she is enshrined in the temple, the matter becomes weighty indeed.
translations.idiomatic: " Debate continued without resolution. Chief Minister Zeng Gongliang asked, "Empress Guo was the emperor's consort before he took the throne; enshrining her in the temple would make this a matter of grave consequence.

sentences.zh: 」頌曰：「國朝三聖，賀、尹、潘皆元妃，事體正相類。

translations.literal: " Song said: "The Three Sages of our dynasty—He, Yin, and Pan—were all primary consorts; the circumstances are exactly of the same kind.
translations.idiomatic: " Song replied, "The Three Sage Emperors of our dynasty—Empresses He, Yin, and Pan—were all primary consorts before enthronement; the precedent is precisely the same.

sentences.zh: 今止祔后廟，則豈得有同異之言。

translations.literal: If we now only enshrine her in the empresses' temple, how could there be differing opinions?
translations.idiomatic: If we enshrine her only in the empresses' temple, as with those precedents, how could anyone argue otherwise?

sentences.zh: 」公亮曰：「議者以謂陰逼母后，是恐萬歲後配祔之意。

translations.literal: " Gongliang said: "Some who debate the matter say this covertly pressures the empress dowager—that it reflects a fear of being enshrined alongside her after death.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongliang said, "Some argue that this covertly pressures the empress dowager—that it anticipates her eventual enshrinement beside Empress Guo after the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 」頌曰：「若加一『懷』、『哀』、『愍』之諡，則不為逼矣。

translations.literal: " Song said: "If one adds a posthumous title with the character 'Cherished,' 'Lamented,' or 'Pitied,' then it would not constitute pressure.
translations.idiomatic: " Song said, "If her posthumous title includes a qualifier such as 'Cherished,' 'Lamented,' or 'Pitied,' it would no longer appear coercive.

sentences.zh: 」公亮歎重。

translations.literal: " Gongliang sighed in deep admiration.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongliang sighed, deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 遷集賢校理，編定書籍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, compiling and fixing books.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, where he helped compile and edit the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 頌在館下九年，奉祖母及母，養姑姊妹與外族數十人，甘旨融怡，昏嫁以時。

translations.literal: Song spent nine years at the Hall, supporting his grandmother and mother, raising aunts, sisters, and several dozen members of the maternal clan; delicacies were harmonious and joyful, and marriages were arranged in season.
translations.idiomatic: Song served at the Hall for nine years, supporting his grandmother and mother and providing for aunts, sisters, and dozens of maternal relatives. The household was warm and well provisioned, and marriages were arranged at the proper times.

sentences.zh: 妻子衣食常不及，而處之晏如。

translations.literal: His wife and children often lacked adequate clothing and food, yet he remained perfectly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children often went without adequate food and clothing, yet he remained entirely unperturbed.

sentences.zh: 富弼嘗稱頌為古君子，及與韓琦為相，同表其廉退，以知潁州。

translations.literal: Fu Bi once praised Song as a gentleman of ancient stamp; when he and Han Qi became chief ministers, they jointly memorialized his integrity and retirement, appointing him prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi had once called Song a gentleman in the ancient mold. When Fu and Han Qi became chief ministers, they jointly recommended his integrity and modesty and appointed him prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 通判趙至忠本邊徼降者，所至與守競，頌待之以禮，具盡誠意。

translations.literal: Vice-prefect Zhao Zhizhong was originally a defector from the frontier; wherever he went he competed with the prefect. Song treated him with ritual and showed him every sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-prefect Zhao Zhizhong was a former defector from the frontier who habitually contended with his prefect wherever he served. Song treated him with courtesy and showed him every sincerity.

sentences.zh: 至忠感泣曰：「身雖夷人，然見義則服，平生誠服者，唯公與韓魏公耳。」

translations.literal: Zhizhong wept with gratitude and said: "Though I am a barbarian, when I see righteousness I submit. In my life the only ones I truly respect are you and Duke Han of Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong wept and said, "Though I am a frontier man, I yield when I see what is right. In all my life, the only men I have truly admired are you and Duke Han of Wei."

sentences.zh: 遷度支判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to revenue-section judge.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as judge in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 送契丹使，宿恩州，驛舍火，左右請出避，頌不動。

translations.literal: While escorting Liao envoys, he lodged at Enzhou; the relay station caught fire, and his attendants asked him to flee, but Song did not move.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting Liao envoys, he lodged at Enzhou. When the relay station caught fire, his attendants urged him to flee, but Song did not stir.

sentences.zh: 州兵欲入救，閉門不納，徐使防卒撲滅之。

translations.literal: Prefecture troops wished to enter to rescue him, but he closed the door and would not admit them; he leisurely had guard soldiers beat out the fire.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural troops tried to force their way in to rescue him, he shut the door and refused them entry, then calmly had the guards extinguish the blaze.

sentences.zh: 初火時，郡人洶洶，唱使者有變，救兵亦欲因而生事，賴頌安靜而止。

translations.literal: At the first outbreak of fire, the people of the prefecture were in an uproar, spreading word that the envoys had caused trouble; the rescue troops also wished to take advantage and stir up incident—only Song's calmness brought it to a stop.
translations.idiomatic: When the fire first broke out, the local populace was in an uproar, claiming the envoys had caused trouble, and the rescue troops were ready to exploit the chaos. Only Song's composure kept matters from escalating.

sentences.zh: 遂聞京師，神宗疑焉。

translations.literal: The report reached the capital, and Emperor Shenzong was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the capital, and Emperor Shenzong grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 頌使還，入奏，稱善久之。

translations.literal: When Song returned from his mission and entered to report, the emperor praised him at length.
translations.idiomatic: When Song returned and reported to the throne, the emperor praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 命為淮南轉運使。

translations.literal: He was appointed transport commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed transport commissioner for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 召修起居注，擢知制誥、知通進銀臺司、知審刑院。

translations.literal: He was summoned to compile the Daily Record, then promoted to drafter of edicts, director of the Gateway Office, and director of the Review Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to compile the imperial diary, then promoted to drafter of edicts and appointed director of both the Gateway Office and the Review Office.

sentences.zh: 時知金州張仲宣坐枉法贓罪至死，法官援李希輔例，杖脊黥配海島。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Zhongxuan, prefect of Jinzhou, was convicted of bending the law for bribes, a capital offense; the law officers cited Li Xifu's precedent—flogging on the back, tattooing, and exile to an island.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Zhongxuan, prefect of Jinzhou, was convicted of corruption in the administration of justice, a capital offense. The judges cited the precedent of Li Xifu and recommended flogging, tattooing, and exile to an island.

sentences.zh: 頌奏曰：「希輔、仲宣均為枉法，情有輕重。

translations.literal: Song memorialized: "Xifu and Zhongxuan both bent the law, but the circumstances differ in severity.
translations.idiomatic: Song memorialized: "Both Xifu and Zhongxuan perverted the law, but the circumstances differ in severity.

sentences.zh: 希輔知台，受賕數百千，額外度僧。

translations.literal: Xifu held a censorate post, received bribes of several hundred thousand, and ordained monks beyond the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu held a censorate post, accepted bribes totaling several hundred thousand cash, and ordained monks beyond the permitted quota.

sentences.zh: 仲宣所部金坑，發檄巡檢體究，其利甚微，土人憚興作，以金八兩屬仲宣，不差官比校，止係違令，可比恐喝條，視希輔有間矣。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan's jurisdiction had a gold pit; he issued a dispatch for a patrol inspector to investigate; the profit was very slight; the local people feared the labor; they gave Zhongxuan eight taels of gold; no official was sent to verify the matter; it amounted only to violation of an edict and may be compared to the statute on intimidation—clearly distinct from Xifu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan's district contained a gold mine. He dispatched a patrol inspector to investigate; the yield proved negligible, and the locals feared the disruption of mining. They gave Zhongxuan eight taels of gold. No official was sent to verify the transaction. This was merely a violation of an edict and falls closer to the statute on intimidation—quite different from Xifu's case.

sentences.zh: 」神宗曰：「免杖而黥之，可乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Exempt the flogging but tattoo him—would that be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "What if we exempt the flogging but still tattoo him?

sentences.zh: 」頌曰：「古者刑不上大夫，仲宣官五品，今貸死而黥之，使與徒隸為伍，雖其人無可矜，所重者，污辱衣冠耳。

translations.literal: " Song said: "In antiquity punishment did not reach grandees. Zhongxuan holds fifth rank. To spare his life yet tattoo him and place him among convict laborers—though the man himself may not deserve pity, what matters is the disgrace to the scholar-official class.
translations.idiomatic: " Song replied, "In antiquity, punishment did not extend to grandees. Zhongxuan holds fifth rank. To spare his life yet tattoo him and make him the equal of convict laborers—though the man himself may not deserve sympathy, what matters is the disgrace inflicted on the scholar-official class.

sentences.zh: 」遂免仗黥，流海外，遂為定法。

translations.literal: " Thus flogging and tattooing were waived; he was exiled overseas, and this became fixed law.
translations.idiomatic: " Flogging and tattooing were waived; Zhongxuan was exiled overseas instead, and this became established precedent.

sentences.zh: 又言：「提舉青苗官不能體朝廷之意，邀功爭利，務為煩擾。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Green Sprouts outreach officials cannot embody the court's intent; they seek merit and compete for profit, striving to cause trouble and harassment.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "The Green Sprouts outreach officials fail to grasp the court's intent. They vie for credit and profit and deliberately cause harassment.

sentences.zh: 且與諸司不相臨統，文移同異，州縣莫知適從。

translations.literal: Moreover they do not supervise the other offices; documents differ in content, and the prefectures and counties do not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, they do not supervise the other offices, their directives conflict with those of other agencies, and prefectures and counties do not know which orders to obey.

sentences.zh: 乞與常平、眾役一切付之監司，改提舉為之屬，則事有統一，而於更張之政無所損也。

translations.literal: I request that the Ever-Normal Granary and corvée labor be entirely entrusted to the supervisory commissioners, with the Green Sprouts office made subordinate to them; then administration would be unified, and the reform policy would suffer no harm.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Ever-Normal Granary and corvée labor be placed entirely under the supervisory commissioners, with the Green Sprouts office made subordinate to them. Administration would then be unified, and the reform itself would lose nothing.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " The proposal was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court did not accept his proposal.

sentences.zh: 大臣薦秀州判官李定，召見，擢太子中允，除監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: Grand ministers recommended Li Ding, vice-prefect of Xiuzhou; he was summoned for audience, promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and appointed investigating censor ad interim.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers recommended Li Ding, vice-prefect of Xiuzhou. He was summoned to audience, promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and appointed investigating censor ad interim.

sentences.zh: 宋敏求知制誥，封還詞頭。

translations.literal: Song Minqiu, drafter of edicts, returned the draft commission.
translations.idiomatic: Song Minqiu, who held the post of drafter of edicts, returned the draft commission unsigned.

sentences.zh: 復下，頌當制，頌奏：「祖宗朝，天下初定，故不起孤遠而登顯要者。

translations.literal: The commission was resubmitted; it was Song's turn to draft. Song memorialized: "In the reigns of our ancestors, when the realm was newly settled, no one was raised from isolation and remoteness to prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: The commission was resubmitted, and it fell to Song to draft the edict. Song memorialized: "In the reigns of our founding emperors, when the realm was newly settled, no one was elevated from obscurity and remoteness to high office.

sentences.zh: 真宗以來，雖有幽人異行，亦不至超越資品。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Zhenzong, though there have been recluses of unusual conduct, none have exceeded their qualification grades.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Zhenzong, even men of reclusive or exceptional character have not been promoted beyond their proper rank.

sentences.zh: 今定不由銓考，擢授朝列；

translations.literal: Now Ding, without passing through examination and appointment, is promoted to court rank;
translations.idiomatic: Now Li Ding, without passing through the regular examination and appointment process, is promoted to court rank;

sentences.zh: 不緣御史，薦置憲臺。

translations.literal: not through the censorate route, is recommended and placed on the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: and without entering through the censorate, is recommended directly to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 雖朝廷急於用才，度越常格，然隳紊法制，所益者小，所損者大，未敢具草。

translations.literal: Though the court is eager to employ talent and exceed the usual rules, it destroys and disorders the legal system; the benefit is small, the harm great—I dare not draft the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Though the court is eager to employ talent and may exceed ordinary rules, this would wreck established procedure. The gain is small and the damage great. I dare not draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 」次至李大臨，亦封還。

translations.literal: " Next it came to Li Dalin's turn, and he too returned the commission.
translations.idiomatic: " When the commission next reached Li Dalin, he returned it as well.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「去年詔，臺官有闕，委御史臺奏舉，不拘官職高下。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said: "Last year's edict stated that when censor posts were vacant, the Censorate might recommend candidates regardless of official rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said, "Last year's edict authorized the Censorate to recommend candidates for vacant censor posts regardless of rank.

sentences.zh: 」頌與大臨對曰：「從前臺官，於太常博士以上、中行員外郎以下舉充。

translations.literal: " Song and Dalin replied: "Formerly censor posts were filled from among those of Erudite of the Imperial Diener and above, down to vice director of the middle rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: " Song and Dalin replied, "Formerly censors were drawn from among officials ranked from Erudite of the Imperial Diener upward down to vice director of the middle rank.

sentences.zh: 後為難得資敘相當，故朝廷特開此制。

translations.literal: Later it became difficult to find candidates of matching qualification and seniority, so the court specially opened this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Because suitable candidates of matching rank became hard to find, the court specially broadened the rule.

sentences.zh: 止是不限博士、員郎，非謂選人亦許奏舉。

translations.literal: It meant only that erudites and directors were not the sole limit—it did not mean that election candidates were also permitted to be recommended.
translations.idiomatic: The change meant only that the pool was not limited to erudites and directors; it did not authorize recommending men still in the examination track.

sentences.zh: 若不拘官職高下，並選人在其間，則是秀州判官亦可為裏行，不必更改中允也。

translations.literal: If regardless of rank election candidates are included, then a Xiuzhou vice-prefect could also serve as censor ad interim without even being changed to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: If rank is ignored and examination-track officials are included, then a Xiuzhou vice-prefect could serve as investigating censor ad interim without even being promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 今定改京官，已是優恩，更處之憲臺，先朝以來，未有此比。

translations.literal: Now Ding is changed to capital official—that is already exceptional grace; to place him further on the Censorate—since previous reigns there has been no such precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ding's promotion to capital official is already an exceptional favor. To place him on the Censorate as well is without precedent since the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 幸門一啟，則士塗奔競之人，希望不次之擢，朝廷名器有限，焉得人人滿其意哉！

translations.literal: Once the gate of favor is opened, careerists will hope for exceptional promotion; the court's honors are limited—how can everyone's wishes be satisfied!
translations.idiomatic: Once the gate of favor is opened, every ambitious office-seeker will hope for extraordinary promotion. The court's honors are finite—how could everyone be satisfied?

sentences.zh: 」執奏不已，於是並落知制誥，歸工部郎中班，天下謂頌及敏求、大臨為「三舍人」。

translations.literal: " They persisted in memorializing without cease; thereupon all were stripped of their posts as drafters of edicts and returned to the rank of director in the Ministry of Works. The realm called Song, Minqiu, and Dalin the "Three Academy Draftsmen."
translations.idiomatic: " They continued to press their objections until all three were stripped of their posts as drafters of edicts and returned to the rank of director in the Ministry of Works. The realm came to call Song, Minqiu, and Dalin the "Three Academy Draftsmen."

sentences.zh: 歲餘，知婺州。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year, he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 方溯桐廬，江水暴迅，舟橫欲覆，母在舟中幾溺矣，頌哀號赴水救之，舟忽自正。

translations.literal: While going upstream at Tonglu, the river suddenly surged; the boat heeled and nearly capsized; his mother in the boat nearly drowned. Song wailed and rushed into the water to save her, and the boat suddenly righted itself.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling upstream at Tonglu, the river suddenly rose in a swift current. The boat heeled and nearly capsized; his mother aboard was nearly drowned. Song cried out and plunged into the water to save her, and the boat suddenly righted itself.

sentences.zh: 母甫及岸，舟乃覆，人以為純孝所感。

translations.literal: His mother had just reached shore when the boat capsized; people regarded it as moved by pure filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had just reached shore when the boat overturned. People took this as a response to his pure filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 徙亳州，有豪婦罪當杖而病，每旬檢之，未愈，譙簿鄧元孚謂頌子曰：「尊公高明以政稱，豈可為一婦所紿。

translations.literal: Transferred to Bozhou: a powerful woman deserving flogging claimed illness; she was examined every ten days but did not recover. Clerk Deng Yuanfu of Qiao told Song's son: "Your honored father is renowned for wise governance—how can he be deceived by one woman?
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Bozhou, he encountered a powerful woman liable to flogging who claimed illness. She was examined every ten days but never recovered. Clerk Deng Yuanfu of Qiao told Song's son, "Your father is famed for wise governance—surely he cannot be fooled by one woman.

sentences.zh: 但諭醫如法檢，自不誣矣。

translations.literal: Simply instruct the physician to examine her according to law, and deception will naturally be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Simply instruct the physician to examine her by the proper procedure, and deception will be impossible.

sentences.zh: 」頌曰：「萬事付公議，何容心焉。

translations.literal: " Song said: "All matters are entrusted to public deliberation—how could personal intent intrude?
translations.idiomatic: " Song said, "All matters should rest on public deliberation. How could personal intent intrude?

sentences.zh: 若言語輕重，則人有觀望，或致有悔。

translations.literal: If one's words carry too much weight, people will watch and wait, and regret may follow.
translations.idiomatic: If one's words carry too much weight, people will hesitate, and regret may follow.

sentences.zh: 」既而婦死，元孚慚曰：「我輩狹小，豈可測公之用心也。

translations.literal: " Before long the woman died. Yuanfu said in shame: "We are narrow-minded—how could we fathom the governor's intent?
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the woman died. Yuanfu said in shame, "We were petty-minded. How could we fathom the governor's intent?

sentences.zh: 」加集賢院學士、知應天府。

translations.literal: " He was additionally made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Yingtianfu.
translations.idiomatic: " He was additionally appointed Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Yingtianfu.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿嘗語人曰：「子容，吾鄉里先進，苟一詣我，執政可得也。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing once told people: "Zirong is a senior of my home district; if he would but visit me once, he could obtain the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing once told others, "Zirong is a senior from my home district. If he would but call on me once, he could become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」頌聞之，笑而不應。

translations.literal: " When Song heard this, he smiled and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " When Song heard this, he smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 凡更三赦，大臨還侍從，頌才授秘書監、知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: Through three general amnesties, Dalin returned to court attendance; only then was Song appointed Director of the Archive and director of the Gateway Office.
translations.idiomatic: After three general amnesties, Dalin returned to court attendance; only then was Song appointed Director of the Archive and director of the Gateway Office.

sentences.zh: 吳越飢，選知杭州。

translations.literal: When Wu and Yue suffered famine, he was selected as prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Wu and Yue, he was selected as prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 一日，出遇百餘人，哀訴曰：「某以轉運司責逋市易緡錢，夜囚晝繫，雖死無以償。

translations.literal: One day, going out, he encountered more than a hundred people who pleaded in grief: "We owe the transport office arrears on Market Exchange cash; we are imprisoned by night and bound by day—even death would not repay the debt.
translations.idiomatic: One day while out on official business, he encountered more than a hundred people pleading in grief: "We owe the transport office arrears on Market Exchange cash. We are imprisoned by night and bound by day—even death would not settle the debt.

sentences.zh: 」頌曰：「吾釋汝，使汝營生，奉衣食之餘，悉以償官，期以歲月而足，可乎？

translations.literal: " Song said: "I will release you and let you earn your livelihood; after providing for food and clothing, you shall repay the state in full over months and years—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: " Song said, "I will release you so you can earn a living. After meeting your food and clothing needs, you will repay the state in full over time. Is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」皆謝不敢負，果如期而足。

translations.literal: " All thanked him and pledged not to default; indeed they fulfilled the debt on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: " All thanked him and pledged not to default, and they repaid the debt exactly on schedule.

sentences.zh: 頌宴客有美堂，或告將兵欲亂，頌密使捕渠領十輩，荷校付獄中，迨夕會散，坐客不知也。

translations.literal: Song was entertaining guests at the Hall of Beauty when someone reported that garrison soldiers intended to revolt. Song secretly had ten ringleaders arrested with cangues and sent to prison; by evening the banquet ended, and the seated guests knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: While entertaining guests at the Hall of Beauty, Song received word that garrison soldiers were plotting a revolt. He secretly had ten ringleaders arrested in cangues and sent to prison. By evening the banquet had ended, and the guests knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 及修兩朝正史，轉右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When he compiled the standard histories of the two reigns, he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: While compiling the standard histories of the two reigns, he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Adviser.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，遇冬至，其國曆後宋曆一日。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Liao, he encountered the winter solstice; their calendar lagged the Song calendar by one day.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Liao, he encountered the winter solstice, when their calendar lagged the Song calendar by one day.

sentences.zh: 北人問孰為是，頌曰：「曆家算術小異，遲速不同，如亥時節氣交，猶是今夕；

translations.literal: The northerners asked which was correct. Song said: "Calendar experts' calculations differ slightly in speed and slowness; if the solar term arrives in the hai hour, it is still this evening;
translations.idiomatic: The northerners asked which calendar was correct. Song replied, "Calendar calculations differ slightly in timing. If the solar term arrives during the hai hour, it is still this evening;

sentences.zh: 若逾數刻，則屬子時，為明日矣。

translations.literal: if it passes several quarters, it belongs to the zi hour and becomes tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: but if it passes by several quarters, it falls into the zi hour and becomes tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 或先或後，各從其歷可也。

translations.literal: Whether earlier or later, each may follow his own calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Whether earlier or later, each side may follow its own calendar.

sentences.zh: 」北人以為然。

translations.literal: " The northerners agreed that this was so.
translations.idiomatic: " The northerners accepted this explanation.

sentences.zh: 使還以奏，神宗嘉曰：「朕嘗思之，此最難處，卿所對殊善。

translations.literal: On returning from his mission he reported to the throne. Emperor Shenzong praised him: "I have considered this matter; it is the hardest to handle. Your reply was excellent.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his mission he reported to the throne. Emperor Shenzong praised him: "I had considered this problem myself—it is the hardest sort to handle. Your reply was excellent.

sentences.zh: 」因問其山川、人情向背，對曰：「彼講和日久，頗竊中國典章禮義，以維持其政，上下相安，未有離貳之意。

translations.literal: " He then asked about their terrain and the people's loyalties. Song replied: "They have been at peace with us for a long time and have extensively borrowed Chinese institutions and ritual to maintain their government; upper and lower ranks are secure, and there is no inclination to split away.
translations.idiomatic: " He then asked about Liao terrain and the people's loyalties. Song replied, "They have been at peace with us for a long time and have extensively adopted Chinese institutions and ritual to sustain their government. High and low are settled, and there is no sign of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝自謂：『高皇帝遺朕平城之憂，雖久勤征討，而匈奴終不服。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han said of himself: 'High Emperor left me the anxiety of Pingcheng; though I campaigned diligently for long, the Xiongnu never submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han said, 'High Emperor left me the burden of Pingcheng. Though I campaigned tirelessly for years, the Xiongnu never submitted.

sentences.zh: 』至宣帝，呼韓單于稽首稱藩。

translations.literal: ' By the time of Emperor Xuan, Chanyu Huhanye kowtowed and declared himself a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet by the time of Emperor Xuan, Chanyu Huhanye kowtowed and declared himself a vassal.

sentences.zh: 唐自中葉以後，河湟陷於吐蕃，憲宗每讀《貞觀政要》，慨然有收復意。

translations.literal: From the mid-Tang onward, the Hehuang region fell to Tibet; Emperor Xianzong, whenever he read the Essentials of Governance from the Zhenguan Era, was stirred with intent to recover it.
translations.idiomatic: From the mid-Tang onward, the Hehuang region fell to Tibet. Emperor Xianzong, whenever he read the Essentials of Governance from the Zhenguan Era, was stirred with the desire to recover it.

sentences.zh: 至宣宗時，乃以三關、七州歸於有司。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Xuanzong, the three passes and seven prefectures were returned to imperial administration.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Xuanzong, the three passes and seven prefectures had been restored to imperial control.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，外國之叛服不常，不繫中國之盛衰也。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, foreign submission and rebellion are inconstant and are not tied to China's rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that foreign submission and rebellion are inconstant and do not depend on China's strength or decline.

sentences.zh: 」頌意蓋有所諷，神宗然之。

translations.literal: " Song's meaning evidently carried subtle admonition, and Emperor Shenzong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Song's meaning clearly carried a subtle admonition, and Emperor Shenzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，權知開封府，頗嚴鞭朴。

translations.literal: In the early Yuangfeng era, acting as prefect of Kaifeng, he was quite strict with flogging.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuangfeng era, while serving as acting prefect of Kaifeng, he was quite strict in applying corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 謂京師浩穰，須彈壓，當以柱後惠文治之，非亳、潁臥治之比。

translations.literal: He said the capital was vast and crowded and required suppression; it should be governed with the judicial staff of Huiwen—not comparable to the leisurely rule of Bozhou and Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He said the capital was vast and crowded and required firm control; it should be governed with the stern authority symbolized by the cap of Huiwen—not with the relaxed style suited to Bozhou and Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 有僧犯法，事連祥符令李純，頌置不治。

translations.literal: A monk violated the law in a case that implicated Li Chun, magistrate of Xiangfu; Song left it uninvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: When a monk broke the law in a case that implicated Li Chun, magistrate of Xiangfu, Song left the matter uninvestigated.

sentences.zh: 御史舒亶糾其故縱，貶秘書監、知濠州。

translations.literal: Censor Shu Dan impeached him for deliberate leniency; he was demoted to Director of the Archive and appointed prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shu Dan impeached him for deliberate leniency. He was demoted to Director of the Archive and appointed prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，頌在開封，國子博士陳世儒妻李惡世儒庶母，欲其死，語群婢曰：「博士一日持喪，當厚餉汝輩。

translations.literal: Initially, while Song was at Kaifeng, Li, wife of National University Erudite Chen Shiru, hated Shiru's stepmother and wished her dead. She told the maidservants: "When the erudite one day enters mourning, I shall richly reward you.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Song was at Kaifeng, Li, wife of National University Erudite Chen Shiru, hated her husband's stepmother and wished her dead. She told the maidservants, "When the erudite one day enters mourning, I shall richly reward you.

sentences.zh: 」既而母為婢所殺，開封治獄，法吏謂李不明言使殺姑，法不至死。

translations.literal: " Before long the stepmother was killed by the maidservants. Kaifeng tried the case; the law officers held that Li had not explicitly ordered the killing of her mother-in-law, and the law did not reach death.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the stepmother was killed by the maidservants. When Kaifeng tried the case, the law officers held that Li had not explicitly ordered her mother-in-law's murder, and the law did not prescribe death.

sentences.zh: 或譖頌欲寬世儒夫婦，帝召頌曰：「此人倫大惡，當窮竟。

translations.literal: Some slandered Song as wishing leniency for the Shiru couple. The emperor summoned Song and said: "This is a great outrage against human relations; it must be thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Some accused Song of seeking leniency for the Shiru couple. The emperor summoned Song and said, "This is a grave violation of human relations and must be thoroughly investigated.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「事在有司，臣固不敢言寬，亦不敢諭之使重。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The matter rests with the officials in charge. I dare not speak of leniency, nor dare I instruct them to impose heavier punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "The matter rests with the officials in charge. I dare not speak of leniency, nor dare I instruct them to impose heavier punishment.

sentences.zh: 」獄久不決。

translations.literal: " The case long remained unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: " The case dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 至是，移之大理。

translations.literal: At this point it was transferred to the Grand Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the case was transferred to the Grand Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 意頌前次請求，移御史臺逮頌對。

translations.literal: Interpreting Song's earlier request as suspicious, the case was transferred to the Censorate to detain Song for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreting Song's earlier request as suspicious, the authorities transferred the matter to the Censorate and detained Song for questioning.

sentences.zh: 御史曰：「公速自言，毋重困辱。

translations.literal: The censor said: "Sir, confess quickly and do not increase your hardship and disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: The censor said, "Sir, confess quickly and spare yourself further hardship and disgrace.

sentences.zh: 」頌曰：「誣人死，不可為已，若自誣以獲罪，何傷乎？

translations.literal: " Song said: "Falsely accusing another of a capital crime cannot be done; if one falsely accuses oneself to receive punishment, what harm is there?
translations.idiomatic: " Song said, "I cannot falsely accuse another of a capital crime. If I falsely accuse myself to receive punishment, what harm is there in that?

sentences.zh: 」即手書數百言伏其咎。

translations.literal: " He immediately wrote several hundred characters by hand confessing his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately wrote out a confession of several hundred characters in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏牘，以為疑，反覆究實，乃大理丞賈種民增減其文傅致也，由是事得白。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed the memorial and found it suspicious; after repeated investigation it turned out that Grand Court Assistant Jia Zhongmin had altered and added to the text to frame him—thus the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reviewed the memorial and found it suspicious. After repeated investigation, it emerged that Grand Court Assistant Jia Zhongmin had altered the text to frame him, and Song was cleared.

sentences.zh: 同列猶以嘗因人語及世儒帷薄事，頌應曰：「然。

translations.literal: His colleagues still held against him that once, when someone spoke of a Confucian scholar's private scandal, Song had answered, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues still held it against him that once, when someone mentioned a Confucian scholar's domestic scandal, Song had replied, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」以是為泄獄情，罷郡。

translations.literal: " Taking this as leaking details of the case, he was removed from his prefectural post.
translations.idiomatic: Taking this as a leak of confidential case details, he was dismissed from his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知河陽，改知滄州。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed prefect of Heyang, then transferred to serve as prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入辭，帝曰：「朕知卿久，然每欲用，輒為事奪，命也夫！

translations.literal: On taking leave to assume office, the emperor said: "I have known you long, yet every time I wished to employ you, something intervened—such is fate!
translations.idiomatic: When he came to take leave before assuming office, the emperor said, "I have known you for a long time, yet every time I wished to use you, something got in the way. Such is fate!

sentences.zh: 卿直道，久而自明。

translations.literal: You walk the straight path; in time it will become clear of itself.
translations.idiomatic: You walk the straight path; in time the truth will make itself plain.

sentences.zh: 」頌頓首謝。

translations.literal: " Song kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Song kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 召判尚書吏部兼詳定官制。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as administrative overseer of the Ministry of Personnel in the Department of State Affairs, concurrently charged with drafting the official system regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to oversee the Ministry of Personnel and to draft reforms to the official system.

sentences.zh: 唐制，吏部主文選，兵部主武選；

translations.literal: Under the Tang system, the Ministry of Personnel handled civil appointments and the Ministry of War handled military appointments;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang system, the Ministry of Personnel handled civil appointments and the Ministry of War handled military ones;

sentences.zh: 神宗謂三代、兩漢本無文武之別，議者不知所處。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong held that the Three Dynasties and the Two Han originally made no distinction between civil and military offices, and those debating the issue did not know how to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong held that in the Three Dynasties and the Two Han there had originally been no civil-military distinction, and the debaters did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 頌言：「唐制吏部有三銓之法，分品秩而掌選事。

translations.literal: Song said: "Under the Tang system the Ministry of Personnel had the method of three selection boards, dividing ranks and grades to manage appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "Under the Tang system the Ministry of Personnel used three selection boards, dividing ranks and grades to manage appointments.

sentences.zh: 今欲文武一歸吏部，則宜分左右曹掌之，每選更以品秩分治。

translations.literal: If civil and military appointments are now to be unified under the Ministry of Personnel, then left and right bureaus should be set up to manage them, and within each selection cycle duties should again be divided by rank and grade.
translations.idiomatic: If civil and military appointments are now to fall under the Ministry of Personnel, left and right bureaus should manage them, with each selection cycle again divided by rank and grade.

sentences.zh: 」於是吏部始有四選法。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Ministry of Personnel first established the four-selection method.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the Ministry of Personnel established the four-selection system for the first time.

sentences.zh: 因陛對，神宗謂頌曰：「欲修一書，非卿不可。

translations.literal: During an audience at the imperial steps, Emperor Shenzong said to Song: "I wish to compile a book, and no one but you will do.
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial audience, Emperor Shenzong told Song, "I wish to compile a book, and no one but you can do it.

sentences.zh: 契丹通好八十餘年，盟誓、聘使、禮幣、儀式，皆無所考據，但患修書者遷延不早成耳。

translations.literal: Peace with the Khitan has lasted more than eighty years, yet oaths, envoys, ceremonial gifts, and ritual forms all lack documentary basis; the only worry is that those compiling the book will delay and not finish it soon.
translations.idiomatic: Peace with the Khitan has lasted more than eighty years, yet oaths, envoys, ceremonial gifts, and ritual forms all lack documentary support. The only worry is that those compiling the book will delay and not finish it soon.

sentences.zh: 然以卿度，此書何時可就？

translations.literal: Yet by your estimate, when can this book be completed?
translations.idiomatic: By your estimate, when can this book be finished?

sentences.zh: 」頌曰：「須一二年。

translations.literal: " Song said: "It will take one or two years.
translations.idiomatic: " Song said, "One or two years."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「果然，非卿不能如是之敏也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "As I expected—no one but you could be so quick.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Just as I expected. No one but you could be so quick."

sentences.zh: 」及書成，帝讀《序引》，喜曰：「正類《序卦》之文。

translations.literal: " When the book was finished, the emperor read the preface and said with delight: "It is just like the language of the Sequence of Hexagrams.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was finished, the emperor read the preface and said with delight, "It reads just like the Sequence of Hexagrams."

sentences.zh: 」賜名《魯衛信錄》。

translations.literal: " It was granted the title Records of Faith between Lu and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: It was given the title Records of Faith between Lu and Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問宗子主祭、承重之義，頌對曰：「古者貴賤不同禮，諸侯、大夫世有爵祿，故有大宗、小宗、主祭、承重之義，則喪服從而異制，匹士庶人亦何預焉。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked about the meaning of lineage heirs leading sacrifice and bearing the ancestral burden. Song replied: "In antiquity noble and base had different rites; feudal lords and grandees held hereditary ranks and stipends generation after generation, hence the principles of major and minor lineages, sacrificial leadership, and bearing the ancestral burden—mourning garments then differed accordingly. What had common scholars and commoners to do with this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked about the rites governing lineage heirs who lead sacrifice and bear the ancestral burden. Song replied, "In antiquity noble and base followed different rites. Feudal lords and grandees held hereditary ranks and stipends from generation to generation, so there were major and minor lineages, sacrificial leadership, and the burden of ancestral succession—and mourning garments differed accordingly. What did ordinary scholars and commoners have to do with any of it?

sentences.zh: 近代不世爵，宗廟因而不立，尊卑亦無所統，其長子孫與眾子孫無以異也。

translations.literal: In recent times ranks are not inherited generation after generation; ancestral temples therefore are not established, high and low have no governing order, and eldest sons and grandsons are no different from other sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times ranks are no longer inherited from generation to generation. Ancestral temples are therefore not established, high and low have no governing order, and eldest sons and grandsons are treated no differently from other descendants.

sentences.zh: 今《五服敕》，嫡孫為祖、父為長子猶斬衰三年，生而情禮則一，死而喪服獨異，恐非先王制禮之本意。

translations.literal: Now under the Five Mourning Grades Edict, a grandson by the principal line mourning a grandfather, and a father mourning an eldest son, still wear the three-year coarse hemp of the highest mourning grade; in life affection and ritual are one, yet in death mourning garments alone differ—this may not be the original intent of the ancient kings in establishing rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under the present Five Mourning Grades Edict, a grandson by the principal line mourning a grandfather, and a father mourning an eldest son, still wear three years of the highest mourning grade. In life affection and ritual are the same, yet in death mourning garments alone differ. That may not be what the ancient kings intended when they established the rites.

sentences.zh: 世俗之論，乃以三年之喪為承重，不知為承大宗之重也。

translations.literal: Popular opinion takes the three-year mourning as bearing the ancestral burden, not knowing that it means bearing the burden of the major lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Popular opinion treats the three-year mourning as bearing the ancestral burden, without understanding that it means bearing the burden of the major lineage.

sentences.zh: 臣聞慶曆中，朝廷議百僚應任子者，長子與長孫差優與官，餘皆降殺，亦近古立宗之法。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that during the Qingli era, when the court debated officials whose sons were eligible for appointment by privilege, eldest sons and eldest grandsons were given slightly preferential offices while the rest were reduced in rank—this too approximates the ancient method of establishing lineages.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that during the Qingli era, when the court debated officials whose sons were eligible for hereditary appointment, eldest sons and eldest grandsons received slightly preferential offices while the rest were reduced in rank. That too approximates the ancient method of establishing lineages.

sentences.zh: 乞詔禮官、博士參議禮律，合承重者，酌古今收族主祭之禮，立為宗子繼祖者，以異於眾子孫之法。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict summon ritual officials and erudites to deliberate on ritual law; for those who should bear the ancestral burden, weigh the ancient and modern rites of gathering the clan and leading sacrifice, establish them as lineage heirs who succeed the ancestors, and distinguish them from the rules governing other sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty summon ritual officials and erudites to deliberate on ritual law. For those who should bear the ancestral burden, weigh the ancient and modern rites of gathering the clan and leading sacrifice, establish them as lineage heirs who succeed the ancestors, and distinguish them from other descendants.

sentences.zh: 士庶人不當同用一律，使人知尊祖，不違禮教也。

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners should not be governed by the same single rule, so that people may know how to honor ancestors and not violate ritual teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners should not be governed by the same rule, so that people may learn to honor their ancestors and not violate ritual teaching.

sentences.zh: 」除吏部侍郎，遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，帝遣中貴人唁勞，賜白金千兩。

translations.literal: When his mother died, the emperor sent a palace eunuch of honored rank to offer condolences and comfort, and granted one thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, the emperor sent a palace eunuch to offer condolences and granted him one thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，拜刑部尚書，遷吏部兼侍讀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was appointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel concurrently serving as Lecturer to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was appointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel while also serving as Lecturer to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 奏：「國朝典章，沿襲唐舊，乞詔史官採《新》、《舊唐書》中君臣所行，日進數事，以備聖覽。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Our dynasty's statutes and regulations follow the Tang precedent; I beg that an edict order the historiographers to select from the New and Old Books of Tang actions taken by rulers and ministers, and each day submit several items for the sage's perusal.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Our dynasty's statutes and regulations follow Tang precedent. I beg that Your Majesty order the historiographers to select from the New and Old Books of Tang actions taken by rulers and ministers, and each day submit several items for your review.

sentences.zh: 」遂詔經筵官遇非講讀日，進漢、唐故事二條。

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued that on days when the imperial lecture sessions were not devoted to formal reading, the lecturers should submit two items of Han and Tang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued that on days when the imperial lecture sessions were not devoted to formal reading, the lecturers should submit two items of Han and Tang precedent.

sentences.zh: 頌每進可為規戒、有補時事者，必述己意，反覆言之。

translations.literal: Whenever Song submitted items that could serve as admonition or were useful to current affairs, he always set forth his own views and repeated them again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Song submitted items that could serve as admonitions or bear on current affairs, he always set forth his own views and repeated them at length.

sentences.zh: 又謂：「人主聰明，不可有所向，有則偏，偏則為患大矣。

translations.literal: He also said: "A ruler is intelligent; he must not lean in any direction—if he does, he becomes partial, and partiality brings great harm.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "A ruler is intelligent, but he must not lean in any direction. If he does, he becomes partial, and partiality brings great harm.

sentences.zh: 今守成之際，應之以無心，則無不治。

translations.literal: Now in a time of preserving what has been achieved, if one responds with a mind free of bias, nothing will go ungoverned.
translations.idiomatic: In a time of preserving what has been achieved, if one responds with an unbiased mind, nothing will go ungoverned.

sentences.zh: 」每進讀至弭兵息民，必援引古今，以動人主之意。

translations.literal: " Whenever his submitted readings touched on halting warfare and giving the people rest, he always cited ancient and modern examples to move the ruler's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his submitted readings touched on halting warfare and giving the people rest, he always cited ancient and modern examples to move the ruler's mind.

sentences.zh: 既又請別制渾儀，因命頌提舉。

translations.literal: He then also requested that a new armillary sphere be made, and Song was ordered to take charge of the project.
translations.idiomatic: He then also requested that a new armillary sphere be built, and Song was ordered to take charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 頌既邃於律曆，以吏部令史韓公廉曉算術，有巧思，奏用之。

translations.literal: Song was already deeply versed in calendrical astronomy; he found that Han Gonglian, a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, understood calculation and had ingenious ideas, and memorialized that he be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Song was already deeply versed in calendrical astronomy. He found that Han Gonglian, a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, understood calculation and had ingenious ideas, and memorialized that he be employed.

sentences.zh: 授以古法，為臺三層，上設渾儀，中設渾象，下設司辰，貫以一機，激水轉輪，不假人力。

translations.literal: Following ancient methods, they built a tower of three tiers: on top an armillary sphere, in the middle a celestial globe, below a time announcer—all driven by one mechanism, with water activating wheels to turn it, requiring no human labor.
translations.idiomatic: Following ancient methods, they built a tower of three tiers: an armillary sphere on top, a celestial globe in the middle, and a time announcer below—all driven by one mechanism, with water turning the wheels and no human labor required.

sentences.zh: 時至刻臨，則司辰出告。

translations.literal: When the hour and quarter arrived, the time announcer came forth to announce it.
translations.idiomatic: When the hour and quarter arrived, the time announcer came forth to announce it.

sentences.zh: 星辰緾度所次，占候則驗，不差晷刻，晝夜晦明，皆可推見，前此未有也。

translations.literal: The positions of the stars along their celestial degrees, when tested by observation, proved accurate—not off by a shadow or a moment; day and night, light and dark, all could be calculated and seen. Nothing like it had existed before.
translations.idiomatic: The positions of the stars along their celestial degrees, when tested by observation, proved accurate to the very moment. Day and night, light and dark, all could be calculated and displayed. Nothing like it had existed before.

sentences.zh: 頌前後掌四選五年，每選人改官，吏求垢瑕，故為稽滯。

translations.literal: Song oversaw the four selection cycles for five years in all; whenever candidates sought changes of office, clerks hunted for flaws and therefore caused delays.
translations.idiomatic: Song oversaw the four selection cycles for five years in all. Whenever candidates sought changes of office, clerks hunted for flaws and deliberately caused delays.

sentences.zh: 頌敕吏曰：「某官緣某事，當會某處，仍引合用條格，具委無漏落狀同上。

translations.literal: Song ordered the clerks: "For such-and-such an office, on account of such-and-such a matter, documents should be assembled at such-and-such a place; cite the applicable statutes and regulations, and submit a complete report with nothing omitted, together with the memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Song ordered the clerks, "For such-and-such an office, on account of such-and-such a matter, documents should be assembled at such-and-such a place. Cite the applicable statutes and regulations, and submit a complete report with nothing omitted, together with the memorial."

sentences.zh: 」自是吏不得逞。

translations.literal: " From then on the clerks could not have their way.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the clerks could not have their way.

sentences.zh: 每訴者至，必取按牘使自省閱，訴者服，乃退；

translations.literal: Whenever a petitioner arrived, he always had the case file brought out for the petitioner to review personally; if the petitioner was satisfied, he was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a petitioner arrived, he always had the case file brought out for the petitioner to review. If the petitioner was satisfied, he was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 其不服，頌必往復詰難，度可行行之，苟有疑，則為奏請，或建白都堂。

translations.literal: if not satisfied, Song would repeatedly question and challenge the matter; if he judged it feasible he carried it out, and if there was doubt he memorialized for decision or raised the matter at the chief council.
translations.idiomatic: if not satisfied, Song would repeatedly question and challenge the matter. If he judged it feasible he carried it out; if there was doubt he memorialized for decision or raised the matter at the chief council.

sentences.zh: 故選官多感德，其不得所欲者，亦心服而去。

translations.literal: Therefore many appointees were grateful for his virtue; even those who did not get what they wanted left with hearts convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Many appointees were grateful for his fairness; even those who did not get what they wanted left convinced.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗行樞密事。

translations.literal: He once acted in the affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He once acted in the affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 邊帥遣种樸入奏：「得諜言，阿里骨已死，國人未知所立。

translations.literal: A frontier commander sent Zhong Pu to report to the throne: "According to spy reports, Aligu is already dead, and the people of the state do not yet know whom they will install.
translations.idiomatic: A frontier commander sent Zhong Pu to report to the throne, "According to spy reports, Aligu is already dead, and the people of the state do not yet know whom they will install.

sentences.zh: 契丹官趙純忠者，謹信可任，願乘其未定，以勁兵數千，擁純忠入其國立之。

translations.literal: The Khitan official Zhao Chunzhong is prudent and trustworthy and can be entrusted with the task; we wish, while their succession is unsettled, to take several thousand crack troops and escort Chunzhong into their state to install him as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan official Zhao Chunzhong is prudent and trustworthy and can be entrusted with the task. We wish, while their succession is unsettled, to take several thousand crack troops and escort Chunzhong into their state to install him as ruler.

sentences.zh: 」眾議如其請。

translations.literal: " The assembly agreed with his request.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly agreed with his request.

sentences.zh: 頌曰：「事未可知，其越境立君，使彼拒而不納，得無損威重乎？

translations.literal: Song said: "The matter is still uncertain; if we cross the border to install a ruler and they refuse to accept him, will we not damage our dignity and authority?
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "The matter is still uncertain. If we cross the border to install a ruler and they refuse to accept him, will we not damage our dignity and authority?

sentences.zh: 徐觀其變，俟其定而撫輯之，未晚也。

translations.literal: Watch the situation slowly, wait until it settles and then pacify and gather them—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Watch the situation unfold, wait until it settles and then pacify them—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」已而阿里骨果無恙。

translations.literal: " Before long Aligu proved to be unharmed after all.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Aligu proved to be unharmed after all.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜右僕射兼中書門下侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs concurrently Vice Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 頌為相，務在奉行故事，使百官守法遵職。

translations.literal: As chief minister, Song's aim was to follow established precedent and make all officials observe the law and keep to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Song's aim was to follow established precedent and make all officials observe the law and keep to their duties.

sentences.zh: 量能授任，杜絕僥倖之原，深戒疆場之臣邀功生事。

translations.literal: He matched ability to appointment, cut off the source of undeserved favor, and sternly warned frontier officials against seeking merit by provoking incidents.
translations.idiomatic: He matched ability to appointment, cut off the source of undeserved favor, and sternly warned frontier officials against seeking merit by provoking incidents.

sentences.zh: 論議有未安者，毅然力爭之。

translations.literal: When he found something unsettling in deliberation, he resolutely argued against it with all his force.
translations.idiomatic: When he found something unsettling in deliberation, he resolutely argued against it with all his force.

sentences.zh: 賈易除知蘇州，頌言：「易在御史名敢言，既為監司矣，今因赦令，反下遷為州，不可。

translations.literal: When Jia Yi was appointed prefect of Suzhou, Song said: "Yi was known as outspoken when he served as censor; now that he has become a supervisory commissioner, to demote him to a prefecture on account of an amnesty is unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Yi was appointed prefect of Suzhou, Song said, "Yi was known as outspoken when he served as censor. Now that he has become a supervisory commissioner, to demote him to a prefecture on account of an amnesty is unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 」爭論未決。

translations.literal: " The debate remained unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: The debate remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 諫官楊畏、來之邵謂稽留詔命，頌遂上章辭位，罷為觀文殿大學士、集禧觀使，繼出知揚州。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials Yang Wei and Lai Zhishao charged that he was delaying imperial edicts; Song thereupon submitted a memorial resigning his post, was removed to serve as Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Commissioner of Jixi Abbey, and was then sent out as prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials Yang Wei and Lai Zhishao charged that he was delaying imperial edicts. Song thereupon submitted a memorial resigning his post, was removed to serve as Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Commissioner of Jixi Abbey, and was then sent out as prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 徒河南，辭不行，告老，以中太一宮使居京口。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Henan but declined to go; he requested retirement on grounds of age and lived at Jingkou as Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Henan but declined to go. He requested retirement on grounds of age and lived at Jingkou as Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，拜太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaosheng he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 方頌執政時，見哲宗年幼，諸臣太紛紜，常曰：「君長，誰任其咎耶？

translations.literal: While Song was in power, seeing that Emperor Zhezong was young and the ministers too contentious, he often said: "When the ruler grows up, who will bear the blame?
translations.idiomatic: While Song was in power, seeing that Emperor Zhezong was young and the ministers too contentious, he often said, "When the ruler grows up, who will bear the blame?

sentences.zh: 」每大臣奏事，但取決於宣仁后，哲宗有言，或無對者。

translations.literal: " Whenever great ministers reported affairs, decisions were taken only from Empress Dowager Xuanren; when Emperor Zhezong spoke, sometimes no one answered.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever great ministers reported affairs, decisions were taken only from Empress Dowager Xuanren. When Emperor Zhezong spoke, sometimes no one answered.

sentences.zh: 惟頌奏宣仁后，必再稟哲宗；

translations.literal: Only Song, when memorializing Empress Dowager Xuanren, always reported again to Emperor Zhezong;
translations.idiomatic: Only Song, when memorializing Empress Dowager Xuanren, always reported again to Emperor Zhezong;

sentences.zh: 有宣諭，必告諸臣以聽聖語。

translations.literal: when there was an imperial pronouncement, he always told the ministers to hear the sage's words.
translations.idiomatic: when there was an imperial pronouncement, he always told the ministers to hear the emperor's words.

sentences.zh: 及貶元祐故臣，御史周秩劾頌。

translations.literal: When former Yuanyou ministers were demoted and punished, Censor Zhou Ji impeached Song.
translations.idiomatic: When former Yuanyou ministers were demoted and punished, Censor Zhou Ji impeached Song.

sentences.zh: 哲宗曰：「頌知君臣之義，無輕議此老。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong said: "Song understands the obligations between ruler and minister—do not lightly criticize this old man.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong said, "Song understands the obligations between ruler and minister. Do not lightly criticize this old man.

sentences.zh: 」徽宗立，進太子太保，爵累趙郡公。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Song was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and his noble rank accumulated to Duke of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Song was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and his noble rank accumulated to Duke of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年夏至，自草遺表，明日卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: On the summer solstice of the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo he drafted his death memorial himself; the next day he died, at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: On the summer solstice of the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo he drafted his own death memorial. The next day he died, at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔輟視朝二日，贈司空。

translations.literal: An edict suspended court audiences for two days and posthumously granted him the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: An edict suspended court audiences for two days and posthumously granted him the title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 頌器局閎遠，不與人校短長，以禮法自持。

translations.literal: Song's capacity and outlook were broad and far-reaching; he did not measure himself against others in small matters, and held himself by ritual and law.
