translations.idiomatic: Song's capacity and outlook were broad and far-reaching. He did not measure himself against others in small matters and held himself by ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 雖貴，奉養如寒士。

translations.literal: Though eminent, he maintained himself like a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Though eminent, he maintained himself like a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 自書契以來，經史、九流、百家之說，至於圖緯、律呂、星官、算法、山經、本草，無所不通。

translations.literal: From the age of written records onward, the classics and histories, the nine schools, and the teachings of the hundred masters, down to apocryphal charts, pitch pipes, star offices, calculation methods, mountain classics, and materia medica—there was nothing he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of written records onward, he mastered the classics and histories, the nine schools, and the teachings of the hundred masters, as well as apocryphal charts, pitch pipes, star offices, calculation methods, mountain classics, and materia medica—there was nothing he did not know.

sentences.zh: 尤明典故，喜為人言，亹亹不絕。

translations.literal: He was especially versed in historical precedents, delighted in speaking to others, and talked on and on without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially versed in historical precedents, delighted in speaking to others, and talked on without cease.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有所制作，必就而正焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the court undertook some new work, it always sought him out to correct and verify it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court undertook some new project, it always sought him out to correct and verify it.

sentences.zh: 嘗議學校，欲博士分經；

translations.literal: He once debated school policy, wishing erudites to specialize by classic;
translations.idiomatic: He once debated school policy, wishing erudites to specialize by classic;

sentences.zh: 課試諸生，以行藝為升俊之路。

translations.literal: students were to be examined and tested, with conduct and talent made the path to advancement.
translations.idiomatic: students were to be examined and tested, with conduct and talent made the path to advancement.

sentences.zh: 議貢舉，欲先行實而後文藝，去封彌、謄錄之法，使有司參考其素，行之自州縣始，庶幾復鄉貢里選之遣範，論者韙之。

translations.literal: In debating the tribute and selection examinations, he wished character and conduct to come before literary skill, abolished the methods of sealed copies and transcription, and had officials consult a candidate's established record, beginning the practice at the district and county level—in the hope of restoring the lost model of local recommendation and selection; commentators approved.
translations.idiomatic: In debating the tribute and selection examinations, he wished character and conduct to come before literary skill. He proposed abolishing sealed copies and transcription, having officials consult a candidate's established record, and beginning the practice at the district and county level—in the hope of restoring the lost model of local recommendation and selection. Commentators approved.

sentences.zh: 論曰：大防重厚，摯骨鯁，頌有德量。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Dafang was grave and solid, Zhi was firm and upright, Song had moral breadth.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Dafang was grave and solid, Zhi was firm and upright, and Song had moral breadth.

sentences.zh: 三人者，皆相於母后垂簾聽政之秋，而能使元祐之治，比隆嘉祐，其功豈易致哉！

translations.literal: These three all served as chief ministers in the autumn of the empress dowager's regency behind the curtain, yet were able to make the Yuanyou governance rise to the level of the Jiayou era—such achievement is not easily attained!
translations.idiomatic: All three served as chief ministers during the empress dowager's regency, yet were able to make the Yuanyou governance rise to the level of the Jiayou era. Such achievement is not easily attained!

sentences.zh: 大防疏宋家法八事，言非溢美，是為萬世矜式。

translations.literal: Dafang's memorial on the eight points of the Song house law was no empty praise—it stands as a model for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang's memorial on the eight points of the Song house law was no empty praise—it stands as a model for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 摯正邪之辨甚嚴，終以直道慍於群小，遂與大防並死於貶，士論冤之。

translations.literal: Zhi's distinction between upright and corrupt was very strict; in the end, because he walked the straight path he provoked the resentment of petty men, and he died in exile together with Dafang—scholarly opinion held it a grievous wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's distinction between upright and corrupt was very strict. In the end, because he walked the straight path he provoked the resentment of petty men, and he died in exile together with Dafang—scholarly opinion held it a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 頌獨巋然高年，未嘗為奸邪所污，世稱其明哲保身。

translations.literal: Song alone stood towering in advanced age, never stained by the corrupt, and the world praised him for preserving wisdom and protecting himself.
translations.idiomatic: Song alone stood towering in advanced age, never stained by the corrupt, and the world praised him for preserving wisdom and protecting himself.

sentences.zh: 然觀其論知州張仲宣受金事，犯顏辨其情罪重輕，又陳刑不上大夫之義，卒免仲宣於黥。

translations.literal: Yet consider his argument in the case of Prefect Zhang Zhongxuan's acceptance of gold: he risked offense to distinguish the gravity of the circumstances and the crime, further set forth the principle that punishment does not reach grandees, and in the end spared Zhongxuan from tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet consider his argument in the case of Prefect Zhang Zhongxuan's acceptance of gold: he risked offense to distinguish the gravity of the circumstances and the crime, set forth the principle that punishment does not reach grandees, and in the end spared Zhongxuan from tattooing.

sentences.zh: 自是宋世命官犯贓抵死者，例不加刑，豈非所為多雅德君子之事，造物者自有以相之歟？

translations.literal: From then on, when appointed officials of the Song committed corruption punishable by death, as a rule no physical punishment was applied—is this not mostly the work of a gentleman of refined virtue, and does not Heaven itself have its way of assisting such men?
translations.idiomatic: From then on, when appointed officials of the Song committed corruption punishable by death, as a rule no physical punishment was applied. Is this not mostly the work of a gentleman of refined virtue—and does not Heaven itself have its way of assisting such men?
